# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Attachment → vision content constants
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Raster formats accepted by the vision APIs we talk to (OpenAI compatible
# providers and Anthropic through LiteLLM). Anything else allowed by
# ``db.ALLOWED_IMAGE_TYPES`` (``image/svg+xml``, ``image/bmp``, ``image/tiff``,
# ``image/heic`` ...) is not a valid ``image_url`` payload: the provider either
# rejects it or silently replaces it with an ``[Unsupported Image]`` placeholder.
# Those attachments therefore travel ONLY through the ``## Attachments`` block.
VISION_IMAGE_MEDIA_TYPES = frozenset({
    "image/png",
    "image/jpeg",
    "image/webp",
    "image/gif",
})

# Media type inferred from the file name when the stored ``file_type`` is
# missing or generic.
MEDIA_TYPE_BY_EXTENSION = {
    "png": "image/png",
    "jpg": "image/jpeg",
    "jpeg": "image/jpeg",
    "webp": "image/webp",
    "gif": "image/gif",
    "svg": "image/svg+xml",
    "bmp": "image/bmp",
    "tif": "image/tiff",
    "tiff": "image/tiff",
    "heic": "image/heic",
    "heif": "image/heif",
}

# Media types that must NEVER reach the provider verbatim: a
# ``data:application/octet-stream`` or ``data:image/*`` URI is exactly what makes
# a model answer "[Unsupported Image]".
GENERIC_MEDIA_TYPES = frozenset({
    "",
    "*/*",
    "image/*",
    "application/octet-stream",
})

# Inline budget per image. Anthropic rejects images over ~5 MB and most proxies
# keep request bodies well below that, so bigger screenshots are downscaled and
# re-encoded before being attached.
MAX_VISION_IMAGE_CHARS = 3_500_000  # base64 characters (~2.6 MB of image)
MAX_VISION_IMAGE_SIDE = 1_560       # longest side, in pixels

# Downscale results are cached per payload: the same screenshot is re-sent with
# every following turn of the conversation.
_IMAGE_SHRINK_CACHE: Dict[str, Dict[str, str]] = {}
_IMAGE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 32


def concat_content(arr):
    """Join non-empty items with newlines."""
    return "\n".join(filter(lambda el: True if el else False, arr))


def new_chat_message(role, content=""):
    """Create a new Message with a generated doc_id."""
    return Message(
        role=role,
        content=content,
        files=[],
        doc_id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
    )


class ChatPromptBuilder:
    """
    Builds the message list sent to the LLM.

    The builder needs two callables from the engine to resolve parent chats
    and parent analysis content:

    * ``get_chat_manager(project_id=...)`` -> ChatManager
    * ``get_chat_analysis_parents(chat=...)`` -> str
    """

    def __init__(self, get_chat_manager, get_chat_analysis_parents):
        self._get_chat_manager = get_chat_manager
        self._get_chat_analysis_parents = get_chat_analysis_parents

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Message conversion
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def convert_message(message):
        """
        Convert a DB Message object into a LangChain message type.

        Handles text-only messages, image messages, and role-based conversion.

        CHANGED: only provider-supported image attachments (see
        :data:`VISION_IMAGE_MEDIA_TYPES`) are converted into ``image_url``
        parts. Audio notes are allowed by ``db.py`` and used to be sent as
        ``image_url`` with a ``data:audio/...`` URI, producing an invalid
        request; unsupported image formats (SVG, BMP, TIFF, HEIC) produce an
        ``[Unsupported Image]`` placeholder on the model side. Both are left to
        the attachment text block built by
        :meth:`_build_attachment_text_block`.

        :param message: The Message object to convert.
        :return: A LangChain HumanMessage or AIMessage (never a dict).
        """
        if message.attachments:
            images = [
                ChatPromptBuilder._attachment_data_uri(attachment)
                for attachment in message.attachments
                if ChatPromptBuilder._is_image_attachment(attachment)
            ]
            if images:
                content = [
                    {"type": "text", "text": message.content}
                ] + [
                    {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": src}}
                    for src in images
                ]
                if message.role == "user":
                    return HumanMessage(content=content)
                return AIMessage(content=content)
        if message.role == "user":
            return HumanMessage(content=message.content)
        return AIMessage(content=message.content)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Multimodal content helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _get_text_content(msg):
        """
        Extract the TEXT part of a message WITHOUT touching multimodal parts.

        Messages converted from a DB message with ``attachments`` carry a LIST
        of content parts (``{"type": "text"}`` + N ``{"type": "image_url"}``).
        ``str(msg.content)`` on such a list returns its Python representation,
        which would REPLACE the images with literal text and make them
        invisible to the model — so only the text parts are joined here.

        :param msg: LangChain message object or OpenAI-style dict.
        :return: The message text (never the image parts).
        """
        if isinstance(msg, dict):
            raw = msg.get("content", "")
        else:
            raw = getattr(msg, "content", "")

        if isinstance(raw, list):
            texts = []
            for part in raw:
                if isinstance(part, dict):
                    if part.get("type") == "text":
                        texts.append(part.get("text") or "")
                elif getattr(part, "type", None) == "text":
                    texts.append(getattr(part, "text", "") or "")
            return " ".join(texts)

        return str(raw) if raw else ""

    @staticmethod
    def _set_text_content(msg, value):
        """
        Replace ONLY the TEXT part of a message, preserving multimodal parts.

        Attachment images (``{"type": "image_url"}``) are kept untouched so the
        model keeps receiving them. When the message has no text part yet, one
        is inserted at the beginning of the parts list.

        :param msg: LangChain message object or OpenAI-style dict.
        :param value: New text content.
        """
        if isinstance(msg, dict):
            existing = msg.get("content", "")
        else:
            existing = getattr(msg, "content", "")

        if isinstance(existing, list):
            for part in existing:
                if isinstance(part, dict) and part.get("type") == "text":
                    part["text"] = value
                    return
                if not isinstance(part, dict) and getattr(part, "type", None) == "text":
                    part.text = value
                    return
            existing.insert(0, {"type": "text", "text": value})
            return

        if isinstance(msg, dict):
            msg["content"] = value
        else:
            msg.content = value

    @staticmethod
    def _set_image_content_parts(msg, parts):
        """
        Replace the ``image_url`` parts of a message with *parts*.

        The message content is promoted to a parts LIST when it is still a
        plain string. Existing ``image_url`` parts are dropped first: the image
        parts are rebuilt from the collected conversation attachments
        (normalized, possibly downscaled), so keeping the ones already produced
        by :meth:`convert_message` would send the same screenshot twice — once
        with its un-normalized payload.

        :param msg: LangChain message object or OpenAI-style dict.
        :param parts: Content parts to set (``image_url`` blocks).
        """
        if isinstance(msg, dict):
            existing = msg.get("content", "")
        else:
            existing = getattr(msg, "content", "")

        if not isinstance(existing, list):
            existing = [
                {"type": "text", "text": "" if existing is None else str(existing)}
            ]
            if isinstance(msg, dict):
                msg["content"] = existing
            else:
                msg.content = existing

        existing[:] = [
            part for part in existing
            if not (isinstance(part, dict) and part.get("type") == "image_url")
        ]
        existing.extend(parts)

    @staticmethod
    def count_attachment_parts(messages):
        """
        Count the ``image_url`` parts contained in the outgoing messages.

        Used by the engine to report how many attachments are being re-sent
        with the request (traceability).

        :param messages: The assembled prompt messages.
        :return: Number of ``image_url`` content parts.
        """
        total = 0
        for msg in messages:
            if isinstance(msg, dict):
                content = msg.get("content")
            else:
                content = getattr(msg, "content", None)
            if isinstance(content, list):
                total += len([
                    part for part in content
                    if isinstance(part, dict) and part.get("type") == "image_url"
                ])
        return total

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Attachment payload normalization
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _attachment_raw_data(attachment):
        """
        Return the raw (not normalized) payload stored for an attachment.

        ``ChatAttachment`` keeps the base64 payload in ``base64_data``; some
        clients store the FULL data URI there (``FileReader.readAsDataURL``).
        Legacy string attachments are JSON image descriptors
        (``{"src": "...", "alt": "..."}``).

        :param attachment: ChatAttachment or legacy string attachment.
        :return: Raw payload string (may still contain a ``data:`` prefix).
        """
        if isinstance(attachment, ChatAttachment):
            return attachment.base64_data or ""

        if isinstance(attachment, str):
            try:
                descriptor = json.loads(attachment)
            except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
                return attachment
            if isinstance(descriptor, dict):
                return str(descriptor.get("src") or "")
            return str(descriptor)

        return str(attachment)

    @classmethod
    def _attachment_media_type(cls, attachment) -> str:
        """
        Return the normalized MIME type of an attachment.

        Resolution order: stored ``file_type`` → the type declared by a stored
        data URI → the file extension. Generic values
        (``application/octet-stream``, ``image/*``) are never returned when a
        better source is available, because sending them verbatim is what makes
        a provider report "[Unsupported Image]".

        :param attachment: ChatAttachment or legacy string attachment.
        :return: Lower-case media type without parameters.
        """
        declared = ""
        file_name = ""

        if isinstance(attachment, ChatAttachment):
            declared = (attachment.file_type or "").split(";")[0].strip().lower()
            file_name = attachment.file_name or ""

        raw = cls._attachment_raw_data(attachment).strip()
        if raw.lower().startswith("data:"):
            uri_type = raw.split(";")[0].partition(":")[2].strip().lower()
            if not declared or declared in GENERIC_MEDIA_TYPES:
                declared = uri_type

        # ``image/jpg`` is not a registered type although some clients send it.
        if declared == "image/jpg":
            declared = "image/jpeg"

        if declared and declared not in GENERIC_MEDIA_TYPES:
            return declared

        extension = file_name.rsplit(".", 1)[-1].lower() if "." in file_name else ""
        return MEDIA_TYPE_BY_EXTENSION.get(extension, "application/octet-stream")

    @classmethod
    def _attachment_payload(cls, attachment) -> str:
        """
        Return the bare base64 payload of an attachment.

        A stored ``data:`` URI is reduced to its payload and every whitespace
        character (JSON line wrapping, pretty printed legacy records) is
        removed: any of those makes the data URI undecodable for the provider.

        :param attachment: ChatAttachment or legacy string attachment.
        :return: Whitespace-free base64 payload (may be empty).
        """
        raw = cls._attachment_raw_data(attachment).strip()
        if raw.lower().startswith("data:"):
            raw = raw.partition(",")[2]
        return "".join(raw.split())

    @classmethod
    def _attachment_data_uri(cls, attachment) -> str:
        """
        Build the ``data:<mime>;base64,<data>`` URI used by vision APIs.

        The payload is normalized (see :meth:`_attachment_payload`) so an
        already prefixed value is never prefixed twice and no whitespace
        survives.

        :param attachment: The ChatAttachment to encode.
        :return: Data URI string.
        """
        return (
            f"data:{cls._attachment_media_type(attachment)}"
            f";base64,{cls._attachment_payload(attachment)}"
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _is_image_attachment(attachment) -> bool:
        """
        Decide whether an attachment can be sent as an ``image_url`` part.

        Only formats accepted by vision APIs qualify (PNG/JPEG/WEBP/GIF).
        Audio notes are stored the same way and must never be sent to providers
        as an image; non-raster images (SVG, BMP, TIFF, HEIC) are rejected by
        providers or replaced with an ``[Unsupported Image]`` placeholder.

        :param attachment: ChatAttachment or legacy string attachment.
        :return: True when the attachment must be sent as an image part.
        """
        return (
            ChatPromptBuilder._attachment_media_type(attachment)
            in VISION_IMAGE_MEDIA_TYPES
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _cache_store(cache: Dict[str, Any], key: str, value: Any) -> None:
        """Store *value* in *cache*, evicting the oldest entry when full."""
        if key not in cache and len(cache) >= _IMAGE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES:
            cache.pop(next(iter(cache)))
        cache[key] = value

    @classmethod
    def _shrink_image_data_uri(
        cls,
        data_uri: str,
        payload: str,
        file_name: str,
    ):
        """
        Downscale and re-encode an image that exceeds the inline budget.

        A screenshot bigger than the provider limit is not "seen" by the model:
        the image part is replaced with an ``[Unsupported Image]`` placeholder.
        The longest side is limited to :data:`MAX_VISION_IMAGE_SIDE` and the
        result is encoded as JPEG.

        Best effort: on any failure the original data URI is kept (and the
        reason is reported in the attachments text block). Results are cached
        per payload, since the same screenshot is re-sent on every turn.

        :param data_uri: The original (normalized) data URI.
        :param payload: The bare base64 payload of *data_uri*.
        :param file_name: Attachment name, used for logging only.
        :return: Tuple of ``(data_uri, note)`` where *note* is appended to the
                 attachment description.
        """
        cache_key = hashlib.md5(payload.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
        cached = _IMAGE_SHRINK_CACHE.get(cache_key)
        if cached is not None:
            return cached["uri"], cached["note"]

        result = {"uri": data_uri, "note": ""}
        try:
            import io

            from PIL import Image

            image = Image.open(io.BytesIO(base64.b64decode(payload)))
            image.load()
            width, height = image.size

            scale = min(1.0, MAX_VISION_IMAGE_SIDE / float(max(width, height) or 1))
            if scale < 1.0:
                image = image.resize(
                    (max(1, int(width * scale)), max(1, int(height * scale))),
                    Image.LANCZOS,
                )
            # JPEG has no alpha channel: flatten transparent screenshots.
            if image.mode not in ("RGB", "L"):
                image = image.convert("RGB")

            buffer = io.BytesIO()
            image.save(buffer, format="JPEG", quality=85, optimize=True)
            candidate = (
                "data:image/jpeg;base64,"
                + base64.b64encode(buffer.getvalue()).decode("ascii")
            )

            if len(candidate) < len(data_uri):
                result = {
                    "uri": candidate,
                    "note": (
                        f", downscaled {width}x{height} -> "
                        f"{image.size[0]}x{image.size[1]} (jpeg)"
                    ),
                }
                logger.info(
                    "Attachment '%s' downscaled %sx%s -> %sx%s "
                    "(%d -> %d base64 chars)",
                    file_name, width, height,
                    image.size[0], image.size[1],
                    len(payload), len(candidate),
                )
            else:
                result = {
                    "uri": data_uri,
                    "note": ", oversized (keeping original encoding)",
                }
                logger.warning(
                    "Attachment '%s' exceeds the vision payload budget and "
                    "re-encoding did not reduce it",
                    file_name,
                )
        except ImportError:
            result = {
                "uri": data_uri,
                "note": ", oversized (Pillow not available)",
            }
            logger.warning(
                "Attachment '%s' exceeds the vision payload budget and Pillow "
                "is not installed; sending it unchanged",
                file_name,
            )
        except (binascii.Error, ValueError, KeyError, OSError, Exception) as ex:
            result = {
                "uri": data_uri,
                "note": ", oversized (re-encode failed)",
            }
            logger.warning(
                "Attachment '%s' exceeds the vision payload budget and could "
                "not be re-encoded: %s",
                file_name, ex,
            )

        cls._cache_store(_IMAGE_SHRINK_CACHE, cache_key, result)
        return result["uri"], result["note"]

    @classmethod
    def _prepare_attachment(cls, item: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Resolve a single collected attachment into its outgoing representation.

        Normalizes the payload and decides whether it travels as an
        ``image_url`` content part or only as text. The returned dict is the
        single source of truth used by both
        :meth:`_build_attachment_parts` and
        :meth:`_build_attachment_text_block`.

        :param item: Attachment item from :meth:`collect_attachments`.
        :return: Dict with keys ``item``, ``file_name``, ``media_type``,
                 ``size_kb``, ``part`` (image part or None) and ``note``.
        """
        attachment = item["attachment"]
        media_type = cls._attachment_media_type(attachment)
        payload = cls._attachment_payload(attachment)
        file_name = (
            attachment.file_name
            if isinstance(attachment, ChatAttachment)
            else f"legacy attachment {item.get('label', '')}".strip()
        )

        prepared = {
            "item": item,
            "file_name": file_name,
            "media_type": media_type,
            "size_kb": round(len(payload) * 3 / 4 / 1024.0, 1),
            "part": None,
            "note": "",
        }

        if media_type not in VISION_IMAGE_MEDIA_TYPES:
            prepared["note"] = (
                f"not sent to the model ({media_type} is not a supported "
                f"vision format)"
            )
            return prepared

        if not payload:
            prepared["note"] = "not sent to the model (empty payload)"
            return prepared

        data_uri = f"data:{media_type};base64,{payload}"
        shrink_note = ""
        if len(data_uri) > MAX_VISION_IMAGE_CHARS:
            data_uri, shrink_note = cls._shrink_image_data_uri(
                data_uri=data_uri,
                payload=payload,
                file_name=file_name,
            )

        prepared["part"] = {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": data_uri}}
        prepared["note"] = f"sent to the model as image ({media_type}{shrink_note})"
        return prepared

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Attachment visibility
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def collect_attachments(self, chat, include_parent=True):
        """
        Collect every attachment the model must always see.

        Attachments of ALL visible messages are returned — parent chats first
        (grandparents first), then the current chat, in conversation order — so
        an image uploaded in an earlier turn keeps reaching the model on every
        following request instead of being lost with the text-only history
        rendering.

        Visibility rules:

        * current chat: ``hide`` / ``improvement`` messages are skipped,
        * parent chats: every VISIBLE message contributes (the ``is_answer``
          flag is not required — see
          :meth:`is_visible_parent_message`), and the traversal stops on
          ``ignore_parent_knowledge``,
        * duplicated payloads (same base64 data) are collapsed to one item.

        :param chat: The chat whose messages are inspected.
        :param include_parent: Whether parent chats contribute attachments.
        :return: List of ``{"role", "label", "attachment"}`` dicts in order.
        """
        items = []
        seen_payloads = set()

        if include_parent and chat.parent_id:
            self._collect_parent_attachments(
                chat=chat,
                items=items,
                seen_payloads=seen_payloads,
            )

        for index, message in enumerate(chat.messages):
            if message.hide or message.improvement:
                continue
            self._add_message_attachments(
                message=message,
                items=items,
                seen_payloads=seen_payloads,
                source="chat",
                index=index,
            )

        return items

    def _collect_parent_attachments(self, chat, items, seen_payloads):
        """
        Append the attachments of a chat's ancestor chain (grandparents first).

        Mirrors :meth:`build_parent_message_history`: stops on
        ``ignore_parent_knowledge`` and includes only VISIBLE messages (via
        :meth:`is_visible_parent_message`, i.e. no ``is_answer`` filtering), so
        attachments keep the same context as the rendered parent history.

        :param chat: The child chat whose ancestors are visited.
        :param items: Accumulator list of attachment items.
        :param seen_payloads: Set of already collected base64 payloads.
        """
        if not chat.parent_id or chat.ignore_parent_knowledge:
            return

        chat_manager = self._get_chat_manager(project_id=chat.owner_project_id)
        parent_chat = chat_manager.find_by_id(chat.parent_id)
        if not parent_chat:
            return

        self._collect_parent_attachments(
            chat=parent_chat,
            items=items,
            seen_payloads=seen_payloads,
        )

        for index, message in enumerate(parent_chat.messages):
            if not self.is_visible_parent_message(message):
                continue
            self._add_message_attachments(
                message=message,
                items=items,
                seen_payloads=seen_payloads,
                source="parent",
                index=index,
            )

    @staticmethod
    def _add_message_attachments(message, items, seen_payloads, source, index):
        """
        Append a single message's attachments to the collector.

        :param message: The message whose attachments are collected.
        :param items: Accumulator list of attachment items.
        :param seen_payloads: Set of already collected base64 payloads.
        :param source: Label prefix ("chat" or "parent").
        :param index: Message position inside its chat (used in the label).
        """
        role = message.role or "user"
        for attachment in (message.attachments or []):
            payload = (
                attachment.base64_data
                if isinstance(attachment, ChatAttachment)
                else str(attachment)
            )
            if payload in seen_payloads:
                continue
            seen_payloads.add(payload)
            items.append({
                "role": role,
                "label": f"{source} turn {index + 1} · {role}",
                "attachment": attachment,
            })

    @staticmethod
    def _build_attachment_parts(prepared_items):
        """
        Collect the ``image_url`` content parts of the prepared attachments.

        Attachments that cannot be sent as images (audio, unsupported raster
        formats, empty payloads) only appear in the text block.

        :param prepared_items: Output of :meth:`_prepare_attachment`.
        :return: List of ``{"type": "image_url"}`` content parts.
        """
        return [
            prepared["part"]
            for prepared in prepared_items
            if prepared.get("part")
        ]

    @staticmethod
    def _build_attachment_text_block(prepared_items):
        """
        Render the attachment list included in the request text.

        Gives the model a textual trace of every attachment (origin turn, file
        name, media type, size) and — crucially — states whether each one was
        sent as an image or not, so a model that cannot decode an image part can
        still report exactly what it received.

        :param prepared_items: Output of :meth:`_prepare_attachment`.
        :return: Markdown block, or an empty string when there is nothing.
        """
        if not prepared_items:
            return ""

        lines = ["## Attachments"]
        for prepared in prepared_items:
            lines.append(
                f"- [{prepared['item']['label']}] {prepared['file_name']} "
                f"({prepared['media_type']}, {prepared['size_kb']} KB) — "
                f"{prepared['note']}"
            )
        return "\n".join(lines)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # History rendering
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _render_history_message(message, formatted_content=None):
        """
        Render a single prior message as an inert turn block.

        Empty messages are skipped (empty string): a run that only executed
        tools produces an assistant message with no text, and its work is
        carried by the ``<session_memory>`` block instead of an empty turn.
        """
        content = (
            formatted_content if formatted_content is not None
            else (message.content or "")
        )
        if not content.strip():
            return ""
        tag = "user" if message.role == "user" else "assistant_done"
        return f"<{tag}>\n{content}\n</{tag}>"

    @staticmethod
    def is_visible_parent_message(message):
        """
        Decide whether a parent chat message should be loaded as content.

        CHANGED: parent content is no longer restricted to messages flagged as
        ``is_answer``. Every VISIBLE message (``hide == False``) of the ancestor
        chats is included, matching what the user sees in the parent chat.

        :param message: The parent chat message to evaluate.
        :return: True when the message must be part of the parent context.
        """
        return not message.hide

    @staticmethod
    def format_parent_message(message):
        """Render a parent message using content, files and attachments."""
        parts = []

        if message.content:
            parts.append(message.content)

        if message.files:
            files_block = "\n".join(f"- {file_path}" for file_path in message.files)
            parts.append(f"Files:\n{files_block}")

        if message.attachments:
            attachments_block = "\n".join(
                f"- {attachment.file_name} ({attachment.file_type})"
                for attachment in message.attachments
            )
            parts.append(f"Attachments:\n{attachments_block}")

        return concat_content(parts)

    def build_parent_message_history(self, chat):
        """
        Build rendered strings from a chat's ancestor chain.

        Only VISIBLE (not hidden) messages are included — the ``is_answer``
        flag is no longer required (see :meth:`is_visible_parent_message`).
        Respects ``ignore_parent_knowledge`` during traversal.

        :return: List of rendered turn strings (grandparents first).
        """
        parts = []

        if not chat.parent_id or chat.ignore_parent_knowledge:
            return parts

        chat_manager = self._get_chat_manager(project_id=chat.owner_project_id)
        parent_chat = chat_manager.find_by_id(chat.parent_id)

        if not parent_chat:
            logger.warning(
                "Parent chat '%s' not found for chat '%s' "
                "(owner_project_id='%s')",
                chat.parent_id,
                chat.doc_id,
                chat.owner_project_id,
            )
            return parts

        logger.info(
            "Including parent chat messages for chat '%s' "
            "(parent_id='%s', ignore_parent_knowledge=%s)",
            chat.doc_id,
            chat.parent_id,
            chat.ignore_parent_knowledge,
        )

        parts.extend(self.build_parent_message_history(chat=parent_chat))

        for message in parent_chat.messages:
            if not self.is_visible_parent_message(message):
                continue

            formatted_content = self.format_parent_message(message)
            if not formatted_content:
                continue

            parts.append(
                self._render_history_message(
                    message, formatted_content=formatted_content
                )
            )

        return parts

    def collect_prior_messages(
        self,
        chat,
        include_parent=True,
        only_answers=False,
    ):
        """
        Return the prior VISIBLE messages of a chat, ancestors first.

        Used to build the tool memory of the next turn: it must see the tool
        events attached to every completed message, including the ones of the
        ancestor chats that contribute context (unless
        ``ignore_parent_knowledge`` is set).

        The last message of the current chat is EXCLUDED: it is the live user
        request and has no prior tool events.

        :param chat: The chat whose prior messages are collected.
        :param include_parent: Whether ancestor chats contribute messages.
        :param only_answers: When True, restrict CURRENT-chat messages to
                             ``is_answer`` ones (refine/vibe mode). Parent
                             messages are not filtered, mirroring
                             :meth:`build_message_history`.
        :return: List of visible Message objects in chronological order.
        """
        messages = []

        if include_parent and chat.parent_id and not chat.ignore_parent_knowledge:
            self._collect_parent_messages(chat=chat, messages=messages)

        for message in chat.messages[0:-1]:
            if message.hide or message.improvement:
                continue
            if only_answers and not message.is_answer:
                continue
            messages.append(message)

        return messages

    def _collect_parent_messages(self, chat, messages):
        """
        Append the visible messages of a chat's ancestor chain (oldest first).

        Mirrors :meth:`build_parent_message_history`: stops on
        ``ignore_parent_knowledge`` and includes only visible messages.

        :param chat: The child chat whose ancestors are visited.
        :param messages: Accumulator list (mutated in place).
        """
        if not chat.parent_id or chat.ignore_parent_knowledge:
            return

        chat_manager = self._get_chat_manager(project_id=chat.owner_project_id)
        parent_chat = chat_manager.find_by_id(chat.parent_id)
        if not parent_chat:
            logger.warning(
                "Parent chat '%s' not found while collecting tool memory of "
                "chat '%s'",
                chat.parent_id,
                chat.doc_id,
            )
            return

        self._collect_parent_messages(chat=parent_chat, messages=messages)

        for message in parent_chat.messages:
            if not self.is_visible_parent_message(message):
                continue
            messages.append(message)

    def build_message_history(
        self,
        chat,
        include_parent_messages=True,
        only_answers=False,
        tool_memory_section=None,
    ):
        """
        Build a single inert history message from prior turns.

        All prior turns (parent + current, excluding the last/current user
        message) are collapsed into one ``<conversation_history>`` block so the
        model sees them as completed context rather than live instructions.

        ADDED: the block also carries the tool memory of the previous turns
        (``<session_memory>``) built from the tool events already persisted on
        the chat messages. This is what stops the agent from re-running the
        same reads/searches on every turn. Callers may pass a pre-built
        *tool_memory_section* (the engine does, to log its stats); when None it
        is built here from the prior messages.

        NOTE: the history block is TEXT only. Attachments of prior turns are
        not lost: they are hoisted into the current request message by
        :meth:`build_ai_prompt_messages` (see :meth:`collect_attachments`).

        :param chat: The chat whose history to convert.
        :param include_parent_messages: Whether to include parent chat history.
        :param only_answers: When True, restrict CURRENT-chat history to
                             ``is_answer`` messages (used in refine/vibe mode).
                             Parent chat history is never filtered by
                             ``is_answer``.
        :param tool_memory_section: Optional pre-rendered ``<session_memory>``
                                    block (built by the caller).
        :return: List containing one HumanMessage, or [] when empty.
        """
        parts = []

        if include_parent_messages and chat.parent_id and not chat.ignore_parent_knowledge:
            parts.extend(self.build_parent_message_history(chat=chat))
        elif chat.parent_id and chat.ignore_parent_knowledge:
            logger.info(
                "Skipping parent chat messages for chat '%s' "
                "(ignore_parent_knowledge=True)",
                chat.doc_id,
            )

        for message in chat.messages[0:-1]:
            if message.hide or message.improvement:
                continue
            if only_answers and not message.is_answer:
                continue
            rendered = self._render_history_message(message)
            if rendered:
                parts.append(rendered)

        if tool_memory_section is None:
            tool_memory_section, _ = build_tool_memory_section(
                self.collect_prior_messages(
                    chat=chat,
                    include_parent=include_parent_messages,
                    # Tool memory is never filtered by ``is_answer``: it
                    # describes work already done, not rendered answers.
                    only_answers=False,
                )
            )

        if not parts and not tool_memory_section:
            return []

        blocks = []
        if parts:
            blocks.append(
                CONVERSATION_HISTORY_HEADER
                + "\n".join(parts)
                + "\n"
                + CONVERSATION_HISTORY_FOOTER
            )
        if tool_memory_section:
            blocks.append(tool_memory_section)

        return [HumanMessage(content="\n".join(blocks))]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Final prompt assembly
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def build_ai_prompt_messages(
        self,
        chat,
        messages,
        user_message,
        last_ai_message,
        context,
        chat_files_content,
        is_refine,
    ):
        """
        Assemble the final list of LangChain messages to send to the AI.

        Appends context, working-file content, and the mode-specific prompt.
        The live instruction is wrapped in ``<current_request>`` and kept as the
        LAST message so it is clearly separated from inert history.

        CHANGED: the ``<current_request>`` wrapping and the working-files
        preamble only rewrite the TEXT part of the last message
        (:meth:`_get_text_content` / :meth:`_set_text_content`). Message
        attachments (vision ``image_url`` parts) are therefore preserved and
        remain visible to the model instead of being flattened into a string.

        ADDED: attachments of EVERY visible message (current chat and parent
        chats) are appended to the request message, so ``message.attachments``
        keeps reaching the model on every following turn. Images are sent as
        ``image_url`` parts; any other type is listed in the ``## Attachments``
        text block only.

        CHANGED: the image parts are REPLACED by the normalized ones built from
        :meth:`_prepare_attachment` (payload without a duplicated ``data:``
        prefix, whitespace stripped, media type resolved, oversized screenshots
        downscaled), so each attachment is sent exactly once and in a form the
        provider can actually decode.

        :return: Mutated messages list ready for AI invocation.
        """
        if context:
            messages.append(
                self.convert_message(
                    new_chat_message(
                        role="user",
                        content=f"<project_files>{context}</project_files>",
                    )
                )
            )

        if is_refine:
            messages = self.append_refine_message(
                chat=chat,
                messages=messages,
                user_message=user_message,
                last_ai_message=last_ai_message,
            )
        else:
            messages.append(self.convert_message(user_message))

        # Wrap the live request so the model can distinguish it from history.
        # Only the text part is rewritten: attachment images must survive.
        last_msg = messages[-1]
        current_content = self._get_text_content(last_msg)
        self._set_text_content(
            last_msg,
            f"<current_request>\n{current_content}\n</current_request>",
        )

        if chat_files_content:
            last_msg = messages[-1]
            current_content = self._get_text_content(last_msg)
            new_content = (
                f"## Working Files:\n"
                f"{chat_files_content}\n"
                f"\n## User request\n"
                f"{current_content}"
            )
            self._set_text_content(last_msg, new_content)

        # ADDED: make every conversation attachment visible in the single
        # request message (images as content parts, everything else as text).
        attachment_items = self.collect_attachments(
            chat=chat,
            include_parent=not chat.ignore_parent_knowledge,
        )
        if attachment_items:
            prepared_items = [
                self._prepare_attachment(item) for item in attachment_items
            ]
            last_msg = messages[-1]
            current_content = self._get_text_content(last_msg)
            self._set_text_content(
                last_msg,
                f"{self._build_attachment_text_block(prepared_items)}"
                f"\n\n{current_content}",
            )
            self._set_image_content_parts(
                last_msg,
                self._build_attachment_parts(prepared_items),
            )
            logger.info(
                "Attached %d conversation attachment(s) to the request of "
                "chat '%s': %s",
                len(prepared_items),
                chat.doc_id,
                "; ".join(
                    f"{prepared['file_name']} ({prepared['media_type']}, "
                    f"{prepared['size_kb']} KB) -> {prepared['note']}"
                    for prepared in prepared_items
                ),
            )

        self._redact_for_model(messages, chat=chat)

        return messages

    def _redact_for_model(self, messages, chat=None):
        """Neutralise secrets in every outgoing message (CISO).

        A prompt is a permanent third-party disclosure: the provider stores it,
        and the same text is echoed back into the answer and from there into the
        task card. Tool output is the usual carrier (a ``cat`` of a config file,
        a ``git remote -v``, a container log), which is why the check runs here
        instead of trusting every caller.

        Only the TEXT part is rewritten: attachment images
        (``{"type": "image_url"}``) are preserved, see
        :meth:`_get_text_content` / :meth:`_set_text_content`.

        :param messages: The messages about to be sent to the model.
        :param chat: The chat being processed (used in the log line).
        :return: Number of redacted occurrences.
        """
        replacements = 0
        for message in messages:
            try:
                text = self._get_text_content(message)
            except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
                continue
            if not text:
                continue
            redacted, found = redact_text(text)
            if not found:
                continue
            replacements += found
            self._set_text_content(message, redacted)
        if replacements:
            logger.warning(
                "CISO: redacted %d secret(s) from the prompt of chat '%s' "
                "before sending it to the model",
                replacements,
                getattr(chat, "doc_id", None) or getattr(chat, "id", None),
            )
        return replacements

    def append_refine_message(self, chat, messages, user_message, last_ai_message):
        """
        Append a task-refinement prompt to the message list.

        Attachments are no longer copied here: they are collected from every
        visible message (including the current one) and appended to the request
        message by :meth:`build_ai_prompt_messages`.
        """
        existing_document = last_ai_message.content if last_ai_message else ""
        parent_task = ""

        if not chat.ignore_parent_knowledge:
            parent_task = self._get_chat_analysis_parents(chat=chat)

        task_content = ""

        answer_messages = [
            message.content for message in chat.messages if message.is_answer
        ]
        if answer_messages:
            task_content += "Task Document Header:\n"
            task_content += concat_content(answer_messages)
            task_content += "\n\n"

        if parent_task:
            task_content += (
                f"\nYou are writing a child document.\n"
                f"This information comes from the parent document for your information:\n"
                f"<parent_document>\n{parent_task}\n</parent_document>\n"
            )

        if existing_document:
            task_content += (
                f"\n<document>\n{existing_document}\n</document>\n\n"
                f"<comments>\n{user_message.content}\n</comments>\n\n"
                f"INSTRUCTIONS:\n"
                f" * Read comments and update document content based on them\n"
                f" * Leave all parts of the document not affected by the comments untouched\n"
                f" * Output the final document content\n"
            )
        else:
            task_content += user_message.content

        refine_message = new_chat_message(role="user", content=task_content)
        messages.append(self.convert_message(refine_message))
        return messages

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Response parsing
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def extract_files_from_response(content):
        """
        Extract code blocks with filenames from the AI response content.
        """
        files = []
        lines = content.split("\n")
        i = 0

        while i < len(lines):
            line = lines[i]
            open_match = re.match(r'^```(\w+)\s+(.+)$', line)

            if open_match:
                language = open_match.group(1)
                file_path = open_match.group(2).strip()
                code_lines = []
                i += 1
                nesting_depth = 1

                while i < len(lines) and nesting_depth > 0:
                    current_line = lines[i]

                    if re.match(r'^```(\w+)', current_line):
                        nesting_depth += 1
                        code_lines.append(current_line)
                    elif current_line == '```':
                        nesting_depth -= 1
                        if nesting_depth > 0:
                            code_lines.append(current_line)
                    else:
                        code_lines.append(current_line)

                    i += 1

                if file_path:
                    files.append({
                        "language": language,
                        "file_path": file_path,
                        "content": "\n".join(code_lines),
                    })
            else:
                i += 1

        logger.info("Extracted %d files from response content", len(files))
        return files

        rel_path: Project-relative path.

    Returns:
        bool: True for ``.codx`` and ``.codx/...``.

    Example:
        >>> is_codx_relative_path(".codx/tasks/a.json")
        True
        >>> is_codx_relative_path("docs/about.codx.md")
        False
    """
    normalized = str(rel_path or "").replace("\\", "/").strip("/")
    return normalized == CODX_DIRNAME or normalized.startswith(CODX_DIRNAME + "/")


def is_codx_path(project_root: str, abs_path: str) -> bool:
    """
    Return True when *abs_path* is inside the project's ``.codx`` folder.

    Args:
        project_root: Absolute project root.
        abs_path: Absolute path to test.

    Returns:
        bool: True when the path belongs to the control plane.
    """
    try:
        rel_path = os.path.relpath(abs_path, project_root)
    except ValueError:  # pragma: no cover - different drives on Windows
        return False
    if rel_path == os.pardir or rel_path.startswith(os.pardir + os.sep):
        return False
    return is_codx_relative_path(rel_path)


def is_path_within_project(
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings, abs_path: str
) -> bool:
    """
    Check that an absolute path resolves inside the project root.

    Unlike a plain ``str.startswith`` check, this compares path components and
    resolves symlinks, so it rejects siblings such as ``/project-other`` while
    accepting every real descendant of ``/project``.

    Args:
        settings: The project settings.
        abs_path: Absolute path to validate.

    Returns:
        bool: True when the path is inside (or is) the project root.

    Example:
        >>> is_path_within_project(settings, "/project/src/main.py")
        True
        >>> is_path_within_project(settings, "/project-other/src/main.py")
        False
    """
    if not abs_path:
        return False
    try:
        root = os.path.realpath(_project_root(settings))
        target = os.path.realpath(os.path.abspath(abs_path))
        return os.path.commonpath([root, target]) == root
    except (ValueError, OSError):
        return False


def _to_relative_path(settings: CODXJuniorSettings, abs_path: str) -> str:
    """
    Convert an absolute file path to a relative path within the project.

    Args:
        settings: The project settings.
        abs_path: Absolute path to convert.

    Returns:
        str: Relative path from project root, or the original path when the
        path is outside the project.
    """
    root = _project_root(settings)
    try:
        abs_path = os.path.abspath(abs_path)
        if os.path.commonpath([root, abs_path]) == root:
            return os.path.relpath(abs_path, root)
    except (ValueError, OSError):
        pass
    return abs_path


async def code_block(file_path: str, code: str, code_language: str, **kwargs) -> str:
    """
    Ensure the code follows the project's standards and best practices and return it in a code block format.

    Args:
        file_path: Absolute file path.
        code: The code to process.
        code_language: The programming language of the code.

    Returns:
        str: The processed code in a code block format.
    """
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings = kwargs.get("settings", None)
    if not settings:
        raise Exception("Invalid project settings")

    session = CODXJuniorSession(settings=settings)
    processed_code = await session.process_project_file_before_saving(
        file_path=file_path, content=code
    )

    return f"```{code_language} {file_path}\n{processed_code}\n```"


def path_to_absolute_project_path(
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings, file_path: str
) -> str:
    """
    Convert a relative or absolute file path to an absolute project path.

    Paths are resolved literally: glob wildcards are NOT interpreted. The
    returned path always points inside the project root and does not need to
    exist on disk, which allows callers such as ``project_write_file`` to
    create new files.

    An absolute path is honored only when it really belongs to the project
    (path-component check, symlinks resolved). Any other absolute path keeps
    the historical behavior of being interpreted relative to the project root,
    so a leading ``/`` never escapes the sandbox.

    Args:
        settings: The project settings.
        file_path: Relative or absolute path to resolve.

    Returns:
        str: Absolute path inside the project root.

    Example:
        >>> path_to_absolute_project_path(settings, "src/main.py")
        '/project/src/main.py'
        >>> path_to_absolute_project_path(settings, "/project/src/main.py")
        '/project/src/main.py'
    """
    project_root = _project_root(settings)
    raw_path = (file_path or "").strip()

    if os.path.isabs(raw_path):
        if is_path_within_project(settings, raw_path):
            return os.path.normpath(os.path.abspath(raw_path))
        # Keep the legacy "absolute-looking path is project-relative" mapping,
        # but drop the separator first so it cannot escape the root.
        raw_path = raw_path.lstrip(os.sep)

    return os.path.normpath(os.path.abspath(os.path.join(project_root, raw_path)))


def _is_glob_pattern(path: str) -> bool:
    """
    Check whether a path string contains glob wildcard characters.

    Used only by search tools that return file paths (see
    :func:`find_project_files`). Reading tools treat every path literally.

    Args:
        path: The path string to inspect.

    Returns:
        bool: True if the path contains glob wildcards ('*', '?' or '[').
    """
    return isinstance(path, str) and any(char in path for char in GLOB_PATTERN_CHARS)


def _find_glob_files(
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings, pattern: str, limit: int = MAX_FILE_MATCHES
) -> List[str]:
    """
    Find project-relative files matching a glob pattern.

    Wildcards follow the standard glob syntax (``*``, ``?``, ``[abc]``,
    ``**``). Only matching files inside the project root are returned, and the
    repository ``.gitignore`` plus the project's custom ignore patterns are
    honored (see :func:`list_project_files`).

    Args:
        settings: The project settings.
        pattern: Relative or absolute glob pattern (e.g. ``**/*.py``).
        limit: Maximum number of matching files to return.

    Returns:
        List[str]: Sorted project-relative file paths.

    Example:
        >>> _find_glob_files(settings, "codx/**/*.py")
        ['codx/junior/tools/project_tools.py', ...]
    """
    project_root = os.path.abspath(settings.abs_project_path)
    ignore_patterns = settings.get_ignore_patterns()

    rel_pattern = pattern
    if os.path.isabs(rel_pattern):
        rel_pattern = os.path.relpath(rel_pattern, project_root)
    rel_pattern = rel_pattern.lstrip("/")

    # Reject patterns that escape the project root
    if rel_pattern.startswith(".."):
        logger.warning("Glob pattern outside project root: %s", pattern)
        return []

    matches = glob.glob(
        rel_pattern,
        root_dir=project_root,
        recursive=True,
        include_hidden=True,
    )

    # Build the authoritative file list once: it honors the repository
    # .gitignore (via git ls-files) plus the project's custom ignore patterns.
    # glob() itself walks ignored directories, so matches must be intersected.
    valid_files = None
    try:
        valid_files = set(list_project_files(settings))
    except Exception as ex:
        logger.warning("Could not apply project ignores to glob: %s", ex)

    results = []
    for match in matches:
        abs_match = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(project_root, match))
        # Keep results inside the project (resolving symlinks) and files only
        if not is_path_within_project(settings, abs_match):
            continue
        if not os.path.isfile(abs_match):
            continue
        if any(p and p in abs_match for p in ignore_patterns):
            continue
        rel_match = os.path.relpath(abs_match, project_root)
        if valid_files is not None and rel_match not in valid_files:
            continue
        results.append(rel_match)

    logger.debug("Glob '%s' matched %d file(s)", pattern, len(results))
    return sorted(set(results))[:limit]


# Declaration patterns used to build the heuristic file outline. The first
# matching pattern wins for a line; the actual declaration line is rendered, so
# the outline never invents names.
_OUTLINE_PATTERNS: Tuple[Tuple["re.Pattern[str]", str], ...] = (
    (re.compile(r"^(\s*)class\s+[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*"), "class"),
    (re.compile(r"^(\s*)(?:async\s+)?def\s+[A-Za-z_]\w*\s*\("), "def"),
    (
        re.compile(
            r"^(\s*)(?:export\s+)?(?:default\s+)?(?:async\s+)?function\s+"
            r"[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*"
        ),
        "function",
    ),
    (
        re.compile(
            r"^(\s*)(?:export\s+)?(?:default\s+)?class\s+[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*"
        ),
        "class",
    ),
    (
        re.compile(
            r"^(\s*)(?:export\s+)?(?:interface|type|enum)\s+[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*"
        ),
        "type",
    ),
    (
        re.compile(
            r"^(\s*)(?:export\s+)?(?:const|let|var)\s+[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*\s*=\s*"
            r"(?:async\s*)?(?:\(|function)"
        ),
        "const",
    ),
    (
        re.compile(r"^(\s{0,4})(?:get|set)\s+[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*\s*\("),
        "accessor",
    ),
    (
        re.compile(r"^(\s{0,4})([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\{"),
        "method",
    ),
)

# Words that look like a method declaration (``if (x) {``) but are control flow.
_OUTLINE_NON_SYMBOLS = frozenset({
    "if", "for", "while", "switch", "catch", "with", "return", "function",
    "else", "do", "try", "finally", "typeof", "await", "yield",
})

# File extensions whose headings are useful in the outline.
_MARKDOWN_EXTENSIONS = frozenset({"md", "mdx", "rst"})

# Maximum characters of one outline declaration line.
_OUTLINE_LINE_MAX_CHARS = 120


def _build_file_outline(
    lines: List[str],
    extension: str,
    max_entries: int,
) -> List[Tuple[int, int, str]]:
    """
    Return a heuristic list of declaration lines for *lines*.

    The outline is deliberately cheap and language-agnostic: it recognises the
    common Python/JS/TS/Vue declaration forms (and Markdown headings) and
    reports the ORIGINAL line, so the model can jump straight to it. It never
    replaces a real parser; it only prevents page-by-page reads of large files.

    Args:
        lines: File lines (without line terminators).
        extension: File extension without the dot (used for Markdown headings).
        max_entries: Maximum number of declarations returned.

    Returns:
        List of ``(line_number, indent, rendered_line)`` in file order.
    """
    entries: List[Tuple[int, int, str]] = []
    for number, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        if len(entries) >= max_entries:
            break
        if not line or not line.strip():
            continue
        if len(line) > MAX_READ_LINE_CHARS:
            continue

        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
        # Nested callbacks/declarations deeper than this add noise, not a map.
        if indent > 8:
            continue

        stripped = line.strip()

        if extension in _MARKDOWN_EXTENSIONS and stripped.startswith("#"):
            entries.append((number, indent, stripped[:_OUTLINE_LINE_MAX_CHARS]))
            continue

        for pattern, kind in _OUTLINE_PATTERNS:
            match = pattern.match(line)
            if not match:
                continue
            if kind == "method" and match.group(2) in _OUTLINE_NON_SYMBOLS:
                break
            entries.append((number, indent, stripped[:_OUTLINE_LINE_MAX_CHARS]))
            break

    return entries


def _render_outline(
    rel_path: str,
    lines: List[str],
    extension: str,
    *,
    max_entries: int,
    automatic: bool,
) -> str:
    """
    Render the outline block prepended to a file read.

    Args:
        rel_path: Project-relative path (shown in the header).
        lines: Full file content split into lines.
        extension: File extension without the dot.
        max_entries: Maximum declarations to render.
        automatic: True when the outline was added by the tool (not requested).

    Returns:
        Markdown outline block, or an empty string when no declaration matched.
    """
    entries = _build_file_outline(lines, extension, max_entries)
    if not entries:
        return ""

    reason = (
        "added automatically because the file is large; "
        "request only the lines you need"
        if automatic
        else "requested"
    )
    header = (
        f"### Outline ({len(entries)} declaration(s), {reason})\n"
        "Line numbers below can be used with `start_line`/`end_line` "
        "or `pattern`."
    )
    body = "\n".join(
        f"{number:>6}| {line}"
        for number, _indent, line in entries
    )
    return f"{header}\n```\n{body}\n```"


def _render_pattern_matches(
    rel_path: str,
    extension: str,
    lines: List[str],
    pattern: str,
    context_lines: int,
    start_line: int,
    end_line: int,
    max_chars: int,
) -> str:
    """
    Return only the lines of a file that match *pattern*, with context.

    Used by ``project_read_file(pattern=...)`` so the model can locate a symbol
    or a config key in a large file in ONE call instead of paging through it.
    Matching lines are always numbered so the model can follow up with an exact
    ``start_line``/``end_line`` read.

    Args:
        rel_path: Project-relative path (shown in the header).
        extension: File extension without the dot (code fence language).
        lines: Full file content split into lines.
        pattern: Literal text or regular expression.
        context_lines: Lines of context before/after each match (clamped).
        start_line: First line of the searched scope (1-based).
        end_line: Last line of the searched scope (inclusive).
        max_chars: Maximum characters returned (the file read budget).

    Returns:
        Formatted matches block (or a clear "no matches" message).
    """
    total_lines = len(lines)
    regex_note = ""
    try:
        regex = re.compile(pattern)
    except re.error:
        regex = re.compile(re.escape(pattern))
        regex_note = " (not valid as a regex; searched literally)"

    scope_start = max(1, start_line)
    scope_end = min(total_lines, end_line)
    matches = [
        number
        for number in range(scope_start, scope_end + 1)
        if regex.search(lines[number - 1])
    ]

    scope_note = (
        f"lines {scope_start}-{scope_end} of {total_lines}"
        if (scope_start, scope_end) != (1, total_lines)
        else f"{total_lines} lines"
    )
    header = (
        f"# {rel_path} — pattern `{pattern}`{regex_note} "
        f"({len(matches)} match(es); {scope_note})"
    )

    if not matches:
        return (
            f"{header}\n\n"
            f"> No line matches `{pattern}`. The pattern is case-sensitive. "
            "Try a shorter pattern, or read a line range if you know where the "
            "code is."
        )

    limited = matches[:MAX_PATTERN_MATCHES]
    context = max(0, min(int(context_lines or 0), MAX_PATTERN_CONTEXT_LINES))

    # Merge overlapping context windows so shared context is shown once.
    windows: List[List[int]] = []
    for number in limited:
        low = max(scope_start, number - context)
        high = min(scope_end, number + context)
        if windows and low <= windows[-1][1] + 1:
            windows[-1][1] = max(windows[-1][1], high)
        else:
            windows.append([low, high])

    rendered: List[str] = []
    used_chars = 0
    stopped = False
    for index, (low, high) in enumerate(windows):
        if index > 0:
            gap = f"{'':>6}| …"
            if used_chars + len(gap) + 1 > max_chars:
                stopped = True
                break
            rendered.append(gap)
            used_chars += len(gap) + 1
        for number in range(low, high + 1):
            line = lines[number - 1]
            if len(line) > MAX_READ_LINE_CHARS:
                line = line[:MAX_READ_LINE_CHARS] + " …[line truncated]"
            entry = f"{number:>6}| {line}"
            if used_chars + len(entry) + 1 > max_chars:
                stopped = True
                break
            rendered.append(entry)
            used_chars += len(entry) + 1
        if stopped:
            break

    formatted = (
        f"{header}\n```{extension} {rel_path}\n"
        + "\n".join(rendered)
        + "\n```"
    )
    notes: List[str] = []
    if len(matches) > len(limited):
        notes.append(
            f"{len(matches) - len(limited)} more match(es) not shown; "
            "narrow the pattern."
        )
    if stopped:
        notes.append(
            "Output truncated at the read budget; narrow the pattern or use "
            "`start_line`/`end_line`."
        )
    if notes:
        formatted += "\n\n> " + " ".join(notes)
    return formatted


def _read_single_file(
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings,
    file_path: str,
    start_line: Optional[int] = None,
    end_line: Optional[int] = None,
    max_chars: Optional[int] = None,
    line_numbers: bool = False,
    pattern: Optional[str] = None,
    context_lines: int = 2,
    outline: bool = False,
) -> Tuple[str, Optional[str]]:
    """
    Read a single file (or a line range of it) and return its content or error.

    The read is bounded: a file is never returned whole when it would exceed
    ``max_chars``, binary files are rejected, and very long lines are shortened.
    The returned header always states which lines of the file are shown so the
    model can request the next range.

    Args:
        settings: The project settings.
        file_path: Path to the file to read.
        start_line: First line to return (1-based). Defaults to line 1.
        end_line: Last line to return (inclusive). Defaults to the last line.
        max_chars: Maximum characters in the code block. Defaults to
            ``DEFAULT_MAX_READ_CHARS`` and is clamped to ``MAX_READ_CHARS``.
        line_numbers: Prefix every returned line with its 1-based number.
        pattern: Optional literal/regex. When set, only matching lines (plus
            ``context_lines`` of context) are returned — the cheap way to find
            a symbol in a large file without paging through it.
        context_lines: Lines of context around each ``pattern`` match.
        outline: Prepend a heuristic outline of the file declarations.

    Returns:
        tuple: (content_or_error, error_message_or_none)
            - If successful: (formatted_content, None)
            - If failed: (error_block, error_description)
    """
    try:
        abs_path = path_to_absolute_project_path(
            settings=settings, file_path=file_path
        )

        if not is_path_within_project(settings, abs_path):
            error_msg = f"Path must belong to {settings.abs_project_path}"
            error_block = FILE_READ_ERROR_TEMPLATE % (
                file_path, file_path, error_msg
            )
            logger.warning("Invalid file path: %s", file_path)
            return error_block, error_msg

        if not os.path.isfile(abs_path):
            error_msg = "File not found"
            error_block = FILE_READ_ERROR_TEMPLATE % (
                file_path, file_path, error_msg
            )
            logger.warning("File not found: %s", abs_path)
            return error_block, error_msg

        # Binary files (null bytes in the sample) cannot be shown as text.
        try:
            with open(abs_path, "rb") as binary_file:
                sample = binary_file.read(BINARY_SAMPLE_BYTES)
        except OSError as e:
            error_msg = str(e)
            error_block = FILE_READ_ERROR_TEMPLATE % (
                file_path, file_path, error_msg
            )
            logger.error("Error reading file %s: %s", file_path, error_msg)
            return error_block, error_msg

        if b"\x00" in sample:
            error_msg = (
                "File appears to be binary and cannot be read as text"
            )
            error_block = FILE_READ_ERROR_TEMPLATE % (
                file_path, file_path, error_msg
            )
            logger.warning("Binary file rejected: %s", abs_path)
            return error_block, error_msg

        with open(abs_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as file:
            content = file.read()

        lines = content.splitlines()
        total_lines = len(lines)
        rel_path = _to_relative_path(settings=settings, abs_path=abs_path)
        extension = os.path.splitext(abs_path)[1].lstrip(".")

        if total_lines == 0:
            if pattern:
                return (
                    f"# {rel_path} (empty file; 0 lines)\n\n"
                    f"> No line matches `{pattern}`: the file is empty.",
                    None,
                )
            formatted = f"# {rel_path} (empty file)\n```{extension} {rel_path}\n\n```"
            return formatted, None

        try:
            requested_start = 1 if start_line is None else int(start_line)
            requested_end = total_lines if end_line is None else int(end_line)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            error_msg = "start_line and end_line must be integers"
            return (
                FILE_READ_ERROR_TEMPLATE % (file_path, file_path, error_msg),
                error_msg,
            )

        requested_start = max(1, requested_start)
        if requested_start > total_lines:
            error_msg = (
                f"start_line ({requested_start}) is beyond the end of the file "
                f"({total_lines} lines)"
            )
            return (
                FILE_READ_ERROR_TEMPLATE % (file_path, file_path, error_msg),
                error_msg,
            )
        if requested_end < requested_start:
            error_msg = (
                f"end_line ({requested_end}) must be greater than or equal to "
                f"start_line ({requested_start})"
            )
            return (
                FILE_READ_ERROR_TEMPLATE % (file_path, file_path, error_msg),
                error_msg,
            )

        requested_end = min(requested_end, total_lines)
        cap = max(
            200,
            min(int(max_chars or DEFAULT_MAX_READ_CHARS), MAX_READ_CHARS),
        )

        # In-file search: one call returns the lines that matter instead of
        # making the model page through the whole file.
        if pattern and str(pattern).strip():
            try:
                context = int(context_lines)
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                context = 2
            return (
                _render_pattern_matches(
                    rel_path=rel_path,
                    extension=extension,
                    lines=lines,
                    pattern=str(pattern),
                    context_lines=context,
                    start_line=requested_start,
                    end_line=requested_end,
                    max_chars=cap,
                ),
                None,
            )

        # Large files get a heuristic map when the model asks for the whole
        # file (or explicitly asks for an outline). A targeted range read does
        # not need the map repeated on every page.
        outline_block = ""
        automatic_outline = (
            not outline
            and start_line is None
            and end_line is None
            and total_lines >= OUTLINE_AUTO_MIN_LINES
        )
        if outline or automatic_outline:
            outline_block = _render_outline(
                rel_path=rel_path,
                lines=lines,
                extension=extension,
                max_entries=(
                    AUTO_OUTLINE_ENTRIES if automatic_outline
                    else MAX_OUTLINE_ENTRIES
                ),
                automatic=automatic_outline,
            )

        rendered_lines: List[str] = []
        used_chars = 0
        last_line = requested_start - 1
        truncated_by_chars = False

        for line_number, line in enumerate(
            lines[requested_start - 1:requested_end], start=requested_start
        ):
            if len(line) > MAX_READ_LINE_CHARS:
                line = line[:MAX_READ_LINE_CHARS] + " …[line truncated]"
            if line_numbers:
                line = f"{line_number:>6}| {line}"

            if used_chars + len(line) + 1 > cap:
                truncated_by_chars = True
                break

            rendered_lines.append(line)
            used_chars += len(line) + 1
            last_line = line_number

        # Guarantee at least one line, even when the cap is tiny.
        if not rendered_lines:
            line = lines[requested_start - 1]
            if len(line) > MAX_READ_LINE_CHARS:
                line = line[:MAX_READ_LINE_CHARS] + " …[line truncated]"
            if line_numbers:
                line = f"{requested_start:>6}| {line}"
            rendered_lines.append(line[:cap])
            last_line = requested_start
            truncated_by_chars = True

        shown_range = f"lines {requested_start}-{last_line} of {total_lines}"
        formatted = "\n".join(
            [f"# {rel_path} ({shown_range})"]
            + [f"```{extension} {rel_path}"]
            + rendered_lines
            + ["```"]
        )

        remaining = total_lines - last_line
        if truncated_by_chars:
            formatted += (
                f"\n\n> Truncated: showing {shown_range} ({remaining} line(s) "
                f"left). Call project_read_file again with "
                f"`start_line={last_line + 1}`, or use `pattern=...` to jump "
                f"directly to the lines you need."
            )
        elif last_line < total_lines and end_line is not None:
            # The caller asked for a specific range: do not nudge it into
            # reading the rest of the file page by page. Offer a targeted way
            # to continue instead.
            formatted += (
                f"\n\n> Showing the requested range {shown_range}; "
                f"{remaining} line(s) follow it. Request them only if needed, "
                f"or use `pattern=...` / the outline to jump to a symbol."
            )

        if outline_block:
            formatted = f"{outline_block}\n\n{formatted}"

        logger.debug(
            "Successfully read file: %s (%s)", file_path, shown_range
        )
        return formatted, None

    except (IOError, OSError, ValueError) as e:
        error_msg = str(e)
        error_block = FILE_READ_ERROR_TEMPLATE % (
            file_path, file_path, error_msg
        )
        logger.error("Error reading file %s: %s", file_path, error_msg)
        return error_block, error_msg


def project_read_file(
    file_path: Union[str, List[str]],
    start_line: Optional[int] = None,
    end_line: Optional[int] = None,
    max_chars: Optional[int] = None,
    line_numbers: bool = False,
    pattern: Optional[str] = None,
    context_lines: int = 2,
    outline: bool = False,
    **kwargs,
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Read the content of one or multiple files from the project.

    Supports bulk file reading to reduce tool calls. For optimal performance,
    read multiple related files in a single call instead of multiple individual calls.

    Paths are read literally: glob wildcards ('*', '?', '[') are NOT interpreted.
    Use ``project_search`` to discover files by pattern and then read the paths
    it returns.

    Output is bounded. Large files are truncated at a line boundary and the
    response states which lines were shown; call again with ``start_line`` /
    ``end_line`` to read the rest. Binary files are reported as errors and never
    dumped into the context.

    To find a symbol or a configuration key in a large file, pass ``pattern``:
    only the matching lines (plus context) are returned, with line numbers. For
    a map of a large file, pass ``outline=True`` (a heuristic outline is also
    added automatically when the whole file is large).

    Args:
        file_path: Single file path (str) or list of file paths to read.
                   Supports relative and absolute paths. Glob patterns are not
                   supported.
        start_line: First line to return (1-based). Applies to every file in a
                   bulk read. Defaults to line 1.
        end_line: Last line to return (inclusive). Applies to every file in a
                  bulk read. Defaults to the last line of each file.
        max_chars: Maximum characters returned per file. Defaults to 50000 and
                   is clamped between 200 and 400000.
        line_numbers: If true, prefix every returned line with its number.
        pattern: Optional literal text or regular expression. When set, only
                 matching lines are returned (with ``context_lines`` of
                 context), so a symbol can be located without paging through
                 the file.
        context_lines: Lines of context around each ``pattern`` match.
        outline: If true, prepend a heuristic outline (declaration line
                 numbers) of the file.
        **kwargs: Additional arguments including:
            - settings (CODXJuniorSettings): Project settings (required).

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: Contains:
            - user_response: Summary of successfully read files and errors.
            - llm_response: File contents with error blocks for invalid/missing files.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If file_path is not provided or empty.
        Exception: If project settings are not provided.

    Example:
        Read a specific range with line numbers:
        >>> project_read_file("src/main.py", start_line=40, end_line=80,
        ...                   line_numbers=True)

        Find a symbol in a large file:
        >>> project_read_file("src/store/ui.js", pattern="setActiveTab")

        Read multiple files at once:
        >>> project_read_file(["src/main.py", "config/settings.py"])
    """
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings = kwargs.get("settings", None)
    if not settings:
        raise Exception("Invalid project settings")

    if not file_path:
        raise ValueError("file_path must be provided and cannot be empty")

    # Normalize to list for uniform processing
    file_paths = [file_path] if isinstance(file_path, str) else file_path

    if not file_paths:
        raise ValueError("At least one file path must be provided")

    # Warn if exceeding recommended bulk operation size
    if len(file_paths) > MAX_FILES_BULK_OP:
        logger.warning(
            "Reading %d files exceeds recommended bulk operation limit of %d",
            len(file_paths),
            MAX_FILES_BULK_OP,
        )

    contents: List[str] = []
    successful_reads: List[str] = []
    failed_reads: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []
    skipped_reads: List[str] = []
    total_chars = 0

    for index, fp in enumerate(file_paths):
        # Keep the overall response within the context budget.
        if total_chars >= MAX_TOTAL_READ_CHARS:
            skipped_reads.extend(str(item) for item in file_paths[index:])
            break

        content, error = _read_single_file(
            settings=settings,
            file_path=fp,
            start_line=start_line,
            end_line=end_line,
            max_chars=max_chars,
            line_numbers=line_numbers,
            pattern=pattern,
            context_lines=context_lines,
            outline=outline,
        )
        contents.append(content)
        total_chars += len(content)

        if error:
            failed_reads.append((str(fp), error))
        else:
            successful_reads.append(str(fp))

    # Build LLM content and feedback summary
    llm_response = "\n".join(contents)
    if skipped_reads:
        llm_response += (
            f"\n\n> Skipped {len(skipped_reads)} file(s) after reaching the "
            f"{MAX_TOTAL_READ_CHARS:,}-character read budget: "
            + ", ".join(skipped_reads)
        )

    summary_lines = [f"Read {len(successful_reads)} file(s)"]
    if successful_reads:
        summary_lines.append(f"Successfully read: {', '.join(successful_reads)}")
    if failed_reads:
        summary_lines.append(
            f"Failed to read {len(failed_reads)} file(s): "
            + ", ".join([f[0] for f in failed_reads])
        )
    if skipped_reads:
        summary_lines.append(f"Skipped {len(skipped_reads)} file(s) (budget)")

    user_response = " | ".join(summary_lines)
    logger.info(
        "File read operation completed: %d file(s), %d chars",
        len(successful_reads),
        len(llm_response),
    )

    return ToolResponse(user_response=user_response, llm_response=llm_response)


def _list_git_files(project_root: str) -> Optional[List[str]]:
    """
    List absolute file paths tracked by git, honoring the repository ``.gitignore``.

    Uses ``git ls-files`` so that every folder and file ignored through
    ``.gitignore`` (and its nested ignore files) is discarded automatically.

    Args:
