"""CISO gates: the single call a process makes before crossing a boundary.

Every integration point of the platform uses one of these functions instead of
talking to the detectors directly. That is what keeps the security behaviour
consistent: change the gate, every process changes.

| Gate                    | Process it protects                          |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| ``guard_file_write``    | writing / editing a project file             |
| ``guard_diff``          | committing or merging a change               |
| ``guard_command``       | running a shell command or a container exec  |
| ``guard_container``     | building / running a container               |
| ``guard_output``        | returning model output or tool output to a user |
| ``guard_knowledge``     | ingesting external content into the RAG index |
| ``sanitize_for_log``    | writing a log line that may carry a secret   |

Failure model
    A gate never raises. When the scanner itself fails the operation is allowed
    and a warning is logged (``policy.fail_closed`` reverses this for
    deployments that prefer availability of security over availability of
    service). Auditing is best effort: a broken audit file must never block a
    legitimate operation.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import logging
from typing import Any, Optional

from codx.junior.security.ciso import malicious
from codx.junior.security.ciso import policy as ciso_policy
from codx.junior.security.ciso import scanner, secrets
from codx.junior.security.ciso.models import (
    CisoPolicy,
    SecurityAction,
    SecurityDomain,
    SecurityVerdict,
)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

#: Audit event name used for every CISO decision.
AUDIT_EVENT = "ciso_verdict"

#: Maximum number of finding summaries recorded per audit entry.
AUDIT_MAX_FINDINGS = 20


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def is_enabled(settings: Any = None) -> bool:
    """Return True when the CISO subsystem is active for *settings*.

    Args:
        settings: Optional project settings.

    Returns:
        bool: ``policy.enabled`` of the effective policy.
    """
    try:
        return ciso_policy.resolve_policy(settings).enabled
    except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        return True


def _audit(
    settings: Any,
    verdict: SecurityVerdict,
    subject: str,
    extra: Optional[dict] = None,
) -> None:
    """Append the verdict to the project audit journal (best effort).

    Args:
        settings: Project settings (used to locate ``.codx``).
        verdict: Decision to record.
        subject: What was inspected (path, command, domain).
        extra: Extra fields to attach.
    """
    codx_path = getattr(settings, "codx_path", None)
    if not codx_path:
        return
    try:
        from codx.junior.harness.audit import record_audit

        record_audit(
            codx_path,
            AUDIT_EVENT,
            domain=verdict.domain.value,
            action=verdict.action.value,
            risk_score=verdict.risk_score,
            highest_severity=(verdict.highest_severity.value if verdict.highest_severity else None),
            subject=subject,
            blocked=verdict.blocked,
            requires_approval=verdict.requires_approval,
            rules=verdict.rules_evaluated,
            findings=[
                {
                    "rule": finding.rule_id,
                    "severity": finding.severity.value,
                    "category": finding.category.value,
                    "path": finding.path,
                    "line": finding.line,
                }
                for finding in verdict.findings[:AUDIT_MAX_FINDINGS]
            ],
            **(extra or {}),
        )
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - audit must never break work
        logger.debug("CISO: could not record the audit entry: %s", ex)


def _fail(policy: CisoPolicy, domain: SecurityDomain, error: Exception) -> SecurityVerdict:
    """Build the verdict used when a scanner raised."""
    logger.warning("CISO gate (%s) failed: %s", domain.value, error)
    verdict = SecurityVerdict(domain=domain)
    if policy.fail_closed:
        verdict.action = SecurityAction.BLOCK
        verdict.blocked = True
        verdict.allowed = False
        verdict.summary = f"blocked: the security scanner failed ({type(error).__name__})"
    else:
        verdict.action = SecurityAction.WARN
        verdict.allowed = True
        verdict.summary = f"scanner error, operation allowed (fail-open): {error}"
    return verdict


def notice(verdict: SecurityVerdict, subject: str = "") -> str:
    """Return a one line, user facing notice describing *verdict*.

    Args:
        verdict: Decision to describe.
        subject: What was inspected (shown when the verdict is not clean).

    Returns:
        str: ``""`` when clean, otherwise a Markdown line with the decision.
    """
    if verdict.action == SecurityAction.ALLOW:
        return ""
    icon = {
        SecurityAction.WARN: "⚠️",
        SecurityAction.REDACT: "🟡",
        SecurityAction.REQUIRE_APPROVAL: "🟠",
        SecurityAction.BLOCK: "⛔",
    }.get(verdict.action, "•")
    target = f" `{subject}`" if subject else ""
    rules = ", ".join(sorted({f.rule_id for f in verdict.findings})[:5])
    return (
        f"{icon} **CISO {verdict.action.value}**{target}: {verdict.summary}"
        + (f" — {rules}" if rules else "")
    )


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Gates
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def guard_file_write(
    file_path: str,
    content: str,
    settings: Any = None,
    policy: Optional[CisoPolicy] = None,
) -> SecurityVerdict:
    """Inspect a payload before it is written to *file_path*.

    Args:
        file_path: Target path (relative to the project).
        content: Exact content that would be written.
        settings: Project settings (for the policy and the audit journal).
        policy: Explicit policy override.

    Returns:
        SecurityVerdict: ``blocked`` means the write must not happen; when
        ``redacted_text`` is set the caller may write that instead.

    Example:
        >>> verdict = guard_file_write(".env", 'DB_PASSWORD="hunter2-hunter2-hunter2"')
        >>> verdict.blocked
        True
    """
    policy = policy or ciso_policy.resolve_policy(settings)
    try:
        verdict = scanner.scan_content(
            content, path=file_path, domain=SecurityDomain.FILE_WRITE, policy=policy
        )
        _audit(settings, verdict, file_path)
        return verdict
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        return _fail(policy, SecurityDomain.FILE_WRITE, ex)


def guard_diff(
    patch: str,
    settings: Any = None,
    domain: SecurityDomain = SecurityDomain.GIT_COMMIT,
    policy: Optional[CisoPolicy] = None,
) -> SecurityVerdict:
    """Inspect a unified diff before it is committed, pushed or merged.

    Args:
        patch: ``git diff`` / ``git show`` output.
        settings: Project settings.
        domain: ``git_commit`` or ``pull_request``.
        policy: Explicit policy override.

    Returns:
        SecurityVerdict: ``blocked`` means the change must not be committed.
    """
    policy = policy or ciso_policy.resolve_policy(settings)
    try:
        verdict = scanner.scan_diff(patch, domain=domain, policy=policy)
        _audit(settings, verdict, "diff")
        return verdict
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        return _fail(policy, domain, ex)


def guard_command(
    command: str,
    settings: Any = None,
    domain: SecurityDomain = SecurityDomain.COMMAND,
    policy: Optional[CisoPolicy] = None,
) -> SecurityVerdict:
    """Inspect a shell command before it is executed.

    Args:
        command: Command line about to run.
        settings: Project settings.
        domain: ``command`` or ``container``.
        policy: Explicit policy override.

    Returns:
        SecurityVerdict: ``blocked`` means the command must not run.
    """
    policy = policy or ciso_policy.resolve_policy(settings)
    try:
        findings, truncated = malicious.scan_command(command, policy=policy)
        verdict = ciso_policy.evaluate(
            findings,
            domain=domain,
            policy=policy,
            rules_evaluated=scanner.RULE_COUNT,
            truncated=truncated,
        )
        _audit(settings, verdict, command[:200])
        return verdict
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        return _fail(policy, domain, ex)


def guard_container(
    command: str,
    settings: Any = None,
    policy: Optional[CisoPolicy] = None,
) -> SecurityVerdict:
    """Inspect a container build/run command.

    Args:
        command: Docker/compose command line.
        settings: Project settings.
        policy: Explicit policy override.

    Returns:
        SecurityVerdict: ``blocked`` means the container operation is refused.
    """
    return guard_command(
        command, settings=settings, domain=SecurityDomain.CONTAINER, policy=policy
    )

    settings: Any = None,
    policy: Optional[CisoPolicy] = None,
) -> SecurityVerdict:
    """Inspect content that is about to be returned to a user or stored.

    Args:
        text: Answer, tool output, log excerpt or exported file body.
        settings: Project settings.
        policy: Explicit policy override.

    Returns:
        SecurityVerdict: when ``redacted_text`` is set the caller MUST return

    """
    policy = policy or ciso_policy.resolve_policy(settings)
    try:
        verdict = scanner.scan_content(

        )
        if verdict.findings:
            _audit(settings, verdict, "output")
        return verdict
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        return _fail(policy, SecurityDomain.MODEL_OUTPUT, ex)


def redact_output(text: str, settings: Any = None, policy: Optional[CisoPolicy] = None) -> str:
    """Return *text* with secrets neutralised (convenience over :func:`guard_output`).

    Most call sites only need the safe string, not the decision: they render a
    snapshot, a log excerpt or a prompt and must never emit a credential. This
    wrapper keeps them to one line while still recording the audit entry and
    honouring ``policy``.

    Args:
        text: Content about to be returned, stored or sent.
        settings: Project settings (for the policy and the audit journal).
        policy: Explicit policy override.

    Returns:
        str: The redacted text, or *text* unchanged when nothing matched.

        False

    verdict = guard_output(text, settings=settings, policy=policy)
    if verdict.redacted_text is None:

    return verdict.redacted_text

    text: str,
    source: Optional[str] = None,
    settings: Any = None,
    policy: Optional[CisoPolicy] = None,
) -> SecurityVerdict:
    """Inspect external content before it is indexed for retrieval.

    A poisoned chunk is retrieved into every later prompt, so ingestion is the
    most valuable place to stop a stored injection.

    Args:

        source: Document origin (URL, path, task id).
        settings: Project settings.
        policy: Explicit policy override.

    Returns:
        SecurityVerdict: ``blocked`` means the chunk must not be indexed.
    """
    policy = policy or ciso_policy.resolve_policy(settings)
    try:
        verdict = scanner.scan_content(
            text,
            path=source,
            domain=SecurityDomain.KNOWLEDGE_INGESTION,
            policy=policy,
        )
        if verdict.findings:
            _audit(settings, verdict, source or "knowledge")
        return verdict
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        return _fail(policy, SecurityDomain.KNOWLEDGE_INGESTION, ex)


def guard_profile(
    definition: Any,
    settings: Any = None,
    policy: Optional[CisoPolicy] = None,
) -> SecurityVerdict:
    """Inspect a profile definition before it is saved or activated.

    A profile carries instructions and an allowlist: it is code for the agent.
    Two things are checked, the serialised definition and the instructions.

    Args:
        definition: ``Profile`` instance or its serialised form.
        settings: Project settings.
        policy: Explicit policy override.

    Returns:
        SecurityVerdict: ``blocked`` means the profile must not be saved.
    """
    policy = policy or ciso_policy.resolve_policy(settings)
    try:

    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        return _fail(policy, SecurityDomain.PROFILE, ex)

    """Return *text* with secrets neutralised and the length bounded.

"""Pre-commit secret gate.

Run it from a git hook::

    PYTHONPATH=<repo>/api python -m codx.junior.security.ciso.precommit

Exit codes
    0   the staged diff is clean (or has nothing to scan),
    1   a credential was found: the commit must be stopped,
    3   the scanner could not run (missing dependencies, no git): the hook
        decides whether that is fatal (``CISO_PRECOMMIT_STRICT=1``).

Why the check belongs here
    Remote push protection fires *after* the commit exists: the secret is
    already a blob in the local object database, reachable from any branch and
    from the reflog, and stopping it then costs a history rewrite plus a
    credential rotation. This gate runs before the object is created, needs no
    network, works with any remote (GitHub, GitLab, self-hosted) and scans
    source files, not only committed history.

The rule tables of this very package contain the patterns they detect — the
literal ``"ignore previous instructions"`` and ``rm -rf /`` are *rules*, not
findings. Code-behaviour findings located inside this folder are therefore
dropped; **secret findings never are**, so a credential committed into the CISO
package is still blocked.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import os
import subprocess
import sys
from typing import List, Optional

#: Exit code when the staged changes are clean.
EXIT_OK = 0
#: Exit code when a finding blocks the commit.
EXIT_BLOCKED = 1
#: Exit code when the gate could not run at all.
EXIT_UNAVAILABLE = 3

#: ``--unified=0`` keeps the diff small; ``scan_diff`` reads added lines only.
DIFF_COMMAND = ["git", "diff", "--cached", "--unified=0", "--no-color"]

#: Categories that describe *code behaviour*. They are dropped when the finding
#: sits inside the CISO package, whose rule tables must contain the patterns.
RULE_TABLE_CATEGORIES = frozenset(
    {
        "malicious",
        "injection",
        "dangerous_operation",
        "supply_chain",
        "data_exfiltration",
    }
)


def staged_diff() -> str:
    """Return the staged patch (``git diff --cached``).

    Returns:
        str: Unified diff of the changes the next commit would include.

    Raises:
        OSError: ``git`` is not available.
        subprocess.CalledProcessError: the command failed (not a repository).
    """
    completed = subprocess.run(
        DIFF_COMMAND,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    )
    return completed.stdout or ""


def rule_table_prefix() -> str:
    """Return the repo-relative folder holding the CISO rules.

    Returns:
        str: ``"<path>/"`` (with a trailing slash), or ``""`` when the package
        is not inside the repository being committed.
    """
    here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    try:
        completed = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
        )
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
        return ""
    root = (completed.stdout or "").strip()
    if not root:
        return ""
    relative = os.path.relpath(here, root).replace(os.sep, "/")
    if relative.startswith(".."):
        return ""
    return f"{relative}/"


def relevant_findings(findings: List) -> List:
    """Drop rule-table findings of the CISO package.

    Args:
        findings: Findings produced by :func:`guard_diff`.

    Returns:
        List: Findings that must still block the commit.
    """
    prefix = rule_table_prefix()
    kept = []
    for finding in findings:
        path = (getattr(finding, "path", "") or "").replace(os.sep, "/")
        category = getattr(getattr(finding, "category", None), "value", "")
        if prefix and path.startswith(prefix) and category in RULE_TABLE_CATEGORIES:
            continue
        kept.append(finding)
    return kept


def main(argv: Optional[list] = None) -> int:
    """Scan the staged changes and decide whether the commit may proceed.

    Args:
        argv: Unused (kept for ``python -m`` compatibility).

    Returns:
        int: One of :data:`EXIT_OK`, :data:`EXIT_BLOCKED`, :data:`EXIT_UNAVAILABLE`.
    """
    try:
        from codx.junior.security.ciso import gate
        from codx.junior.security.ciso import policy as ciso_policy
        from codx.junior.security.ciso.models import SecurityDomain
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - depends on the environment
        print(f"CISO: the secret scanner is not importable ({ex})", file=sys.stderr)
        return EXIT_UNAVAILABLE

    try:
        patch = staged_diff()
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as ex:
        print(f"CISO: could not read the staged diff ({ex})", file=sys.stderr)
        return EXIT_UNAVAILABLE

    if not patch.strip():
        return EXIT_OK

    scanned = gate.guard_diff(patch)
    findings = relevant_findings(scanned.findings)
    if not findings:
        return EXIT_OK

    # Re-evaluate the ladder on the findings that survive the filter: keeping
    # the original decision would block on a rule the filter just dropped.
    policy = ciso_policy.resolve_policy(None)
    verdict = ciso_policy.evaluate(
        findings,
        domain=SecurityDomain.GIT_COMMIT,
        policy=policy,
        rules_evaluated=scanned.rules_evaluated,
        truncated=scanned.truncated,
    )

    print(ciso_policy.render_report(verdict, title="CISO pre-commit report"))
    if verdict.blocked:
        print(
            "\nCISO: commit blocked. Remove the credential, rotate it (assume it "
            "is disclosed) and stage the fix.\n"
            "Inspect the staged changes with: git diff --cached",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return EXIT_BLOCKED
    return EXIT_OK


if __name__ == "__main__":  # pragma: no cover
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

"""CISO security tools.

These are the tools the ``ciso`` profile (and any profile granted them) uses to
audit a project, review a change before it is committed or merged, validate a
payload before writing it, check a shell command and neutralise secrets in a
text that is about to be shared.

Two of them are also used as gates by other processes: ``security_review_changes``
is the pull-request gate and ``security_check_command`` is the command gate.
Gates that run automatically inside a process live in
:mod:`codx.junior.security.ciso.gate`, not here: a tool is an explicit action,
a gate is an implicit guarantee.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior

import logging

from .model import ToolResponse
from codx.junior.security.ciso import (
    CisoPolicy,

    gate,
    policy as ciso_policy,
    render_report,

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _settings_of(kwargs: Dict[str, Any]):
    """Return the project settings injected by the runtime (or ``None``)."""
    return kwargs.get("settings")


def _project_path(settings: Any) -> str:
    """Return the absolute project path of *settings*."""
    return getattr(settings, "abs_project_path", None) or os.getcwd()


def _verdict_answer(verdict, title: str) -> str:
    """Render a verdict as the user facing markdown report."""
    return render_report(verdict, title=title)


def _llm_summary(verdict, subject: str) -> str:
    """Build the compact machine friendly summary for the model."""
    lines = [
        f"# {subject}",
        f"- decision: {verdict.action.value}",
        f"- blocked: {verdict.blocked}",
        f"- requires_approval: {verdict.requires_approval}",
        f"- highest_severity: {(verdict.highest_severity.value if verdict.highest_severity else 'none')}",
        f"- risk_score: {verdict.risk_score}",
        f"- findings: {len(verdict.findings)}",
    ]
    for finding in verdict.findings[:10]:
        location = finding.path or "-"
        if finding.line:
            location = f"{location}:{finding.line}"
        lines.append(
            f"- [{finding.severity.value}] {finding.rule_id} @ {location}: "
            f"{finding.remediation or finding.reason}"
        )
    if len(verdict.findings) > 10:
        lines.append(f"- … {len(verdict.findings) - 10} more finding(s)")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _git_diff(settings: Any, base: str, scope: str, paths: Optional[List[str]]) -> str:
    """Return the unified diff requested by the caller.

    Args:
        settings: Project settings.
        base: Git reference to compare against.
        scope: ``all`` | ``staged`` | ``unstaged``.
        paths: Optional path filter.

    Returns:
        str: Unified diff (empty when there is nothing to review).
    """
    from .project_tools import _run_git

    args: List[str] = ["diff", "--no-ext-diff", "--no-textconv", "--no-color", "-U3"]
    if scope == "staged":
        args.append("--cached")
    elif scope == "all":
        args.append(base or "HEAD")

    if paths:
        args += ["--", *paths]

    ok, stdout, stderr = _run_git(settings, args)
    if not ok:
        raise ValueError(f"git diff failed: {(stderr or '').strip()}")
    return stdout or ""

def security_audit(
    path: Optional[str] = None,
    max_files: int = 200,
    include_dependency_files: bool = True,
    **kwargs
) -> ToolResponse:
    """Audit a project (or a sub path) for secrets, malicious code and injection.

    Scans the files of the project with every CISO detector and returns a
    Markdown report plus a machine friendly summary.

    Args:
        path: Optional project-relative folder or file to restrict the audit.
        max_files: Maximum number of files read (default 200).
        include_dependency_files: Also scan lock files / manifests
            (still skipped: vendored folders such as ``node_modules``).
        **kwargs: Runtime arguments; ``settings`` is injected automatically.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: Report, summary and the scan logs.

    Example:
        >>> security_audit(path="api/")  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    settings = _settings_of(kwargs)
    if not settings:
        raise Exception("Invalid project settings")

    project_path = _project_path(settings)
    policy = resolve_policy(settings)

    targets = None
    if path:
        absolute = path if os.path.isabs(path) else os.path.join(project_path, path)
        if os.path.isdir(absolute):
            from codx.junior.security.ciso.scanner import iter_project_files

            targets = iter_project_files(absolute, max_files=max_files, policy=policy)
        elif os.path.isfile(absolute):
            targets = [absolute]
        else:
            return ToolResponse(
                user_response=f"⚠️ Path not found: `{path}`",
                llm_response=f"security_audit: path not found: {path}",
            )

    verdict = scan_project(
        project_path,
        max_files=max_files,
        domain=SecurityDomain.FILE_READ,
        policy=policy,
        paths=targets,
    )

    title = f"CISO audit — {getattr(settings, 'project_name', 'project')}"
    if path:
        title += f" — `{path}`"

    logs = [
        f"CISO audit: {verdict.summary}",
        f"CISO audit: decision={verdict.action.value} blocked={verdict.blocked}",
    ]
    for finding in verdict.findings[:25]:
        logs.append(
            f"[{finding.severity.value.upper()}] {finding.rule_id} "
            f"{finding.path}:{finding.line or 0} — {finding.title}"
        )

    return ToolResponse(
        user_response=_verdict_answer(verdict, title),
        llm_response=_llm_summary(verdict, "CISO audit"),
        logs=logs,
    )


def security_scan_content(
    content: str,
    path: Optional[str] = None,
    domain: str = "file_write",
    **kwargs
) -> ToolResponse:
    """Scan a payload before writing, committing or sharing it.

    Use it to validate a file body *before* calling ``project_write_file`` or
    ``apply_file_changes``: it reports whether the content would be blocked and
    returns a redacted version when it carries secrets.

    Args:
        content: Exact payload to inspect.
        path: Target path (drives the reported location).
        domain: Integration point: ``file_write`` (default), ``git_commit``,
            ``model_output``, ``knowledge_ingestion``, ``profile``.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: Report; the summary includes the redacted payload when
        secrets were neutralised.

    Example:
        >>> security_scan_content('TOKEN="<your-token>"')  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    settings = _settings_of(kwargs)
    policy = resolve_policy(settings)

    try:
        domain_value = SecurityDomain(domain)
    except ValueError:
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"⚠️ Unknown domain `{domain}`. Valid: "
                          f"{', '.join(d.value for d in SecurityDomain)}",
            llm_response=f"security_scan_content: invalid domain {domain}",
        )

    verdict = scan_content(content, path=path, domain=domain_value, policy=policy)

    llm_summary = _llm_summary(verdict, "CISO content scan")
    if verdict.redacted_text is not None:
        llm_summary += (
            "\n\n## Redacted payload (safe to write)\n```\n"
            + verdict.redacted_text
            + "\n```\nUse this content instead of the original."
        )

    return ToolResponse(
        user_response=_verdict_answer(verdict, f"CISO scan — `{path or 'inline content'}`"),
        llm_response=llm_summary,
        logs=[f"CISO content scan: {verdict.summary}"],
    )


def security_review_changes(
    base: str = "HEAD",
    scope: str = "all",
    paths: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    **kwargs
) -> ToolResponse:
    """Review a change (working tree, staged or against a ref) before shipping it.

    This is the pull-request gate: only the **added** lines are inspected and
    the reported line numbers are the new file coordinates.

    Args:
        base: Git reference to compare against (default ``HEAD``).
        scope: ``all`` (working tree + staged vs base), ``staged`` (next commit)
            or ``unstaged`` (working tree vs index).
        paths: Optional list of paths to restrict the review.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: Report of the change.

    Example:
        >>> security_review_changes(scope="staged")  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    settings = _settings_of(kwargs)
    if not settings:
        raise Exception("Invalid project settings")

    policy = resolve_policy(settings)
    domain = SecurityDomain.GIT_COMMIT if scope == "staged" else SecurityDomain.PULL_REQUEST

    try:
        patch = _git_diff(settings, base=base, scope=scope, paths=paths)
    except Exception as ex:
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"⚠️ Could not read the change: {ex}",
            llm_response=f"security_review_changes: {ex}",
        )

    if not (patch or "").strip():
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response="✅ No pending changes to review.",
            llm_response="security_review_changes: empty diff, nothing to review.",
        )

    verdict = scan_diff(patch, domain=domain, policy=policy)
    return ToolResponse(
        user_response=_verdict_answer(verdict, f"CISO review — scope `{scope}` vs `{base}`"),
        llm_response=_llm_summary(verdict, "CISO change review"),
        logs=[f"CISO change review: {verdict.summary}"],
    )

def security_policy(action: str = "show", changes: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, **kwargs) -> ToolResponse:
    """Show or adjust the CISO policy of the project.

    The policy is stored in the project settings under ``ciso_policy``. Only the
    fields listed in the report can be changed, and every change is validated
    against the policy model before it is applied.

    Args:
        action: ``show`` (default) to display the effective policy.
        changes: Partial policy to merge (``action='show'`` ignores it). Fields
            include ``enabled``, ``block_above``, ``approval_above``,
            ``warn_above``, ``redact_secrets``, ``fail_closed``,
            ``ignore_paths``, ``ignore_rules``, ``allow_secret_files``.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: The effective policy as Markdown.

    Example:
        >>> security_policy()  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    settings = _settings_of(kwargs)
    if not settings:
        raise Exception("Invalid project settings")

    stored: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    configured = getattr(settings, "settings", None)
    if isinstance(configured, dict) and isinstance(configured.get(ciso_policy.POLICY_SETTINGS_KEY), dict):
        stored = dict(configured[ciso_policy.POLICY_SETTINGS_KEY])

    if changes and action == "show":
        merged = dict(stored)
        merged.update(changes or {})
        validated = ciso_policy.policy_from_dict(merged)
        try:
            configured = getattr(settings, "settings", None)
            if isinstance(configured, dict):
                configured[ciso_policy.POLICY_SETTINGS_KEY] = validated.to_dict()
                save = getattr(settings, "save", None)
                if callable(save):
                    save()
            else:
                return ToolResponse(
                    user_response="⚠️ This project settings object does not expose a writable `settings` dict.",
                    llm_response="security_policy: unsupported settings object",
                )
        except Exception as ex:
            return ToolResponse(
                user_response=f"⚠️ Could not persist the policy: {ex}",
                llm_response=f"security_policy: persist failed: {ex}",
            )

    policy = resolve_policy(settings)
    markdown = _policy_markdown(policy, stored)
    return ToolResponse(
        user_response=markdown,
        llm_response=f"CISO policy: enabled={policy.enabled} "
                     f"block_above={policy.block_above.value} "
                     f"approval_above={policy.approval_above.value} "
                     f"fail_closed={policy.fail_closed}",
        logs=["CISO policy reported"],
    )


def _policy_markdown(policy: CisoPolicy, stored: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """Render the effective policy as Markdown."""
    def _values(items) -> str:
        return ", ".join(f"`{item.value}`" for item in items) or "-"

    return "\n".join([
        "# CISO policy",
        "",
        f"- Enabled: **{policy.enabled}**",
        f"- Block severities: {_values(policy.block_severities)}",
        f"- Block categories: {_values(policy.block_categories)}",
        f"- Block above: `{policy.block_above.value}`",
        f"- Approval above: `{policy.approval_above.value}`",
        f"- Warn above: `{policy.warn_above.value}`",
        f"- Strict domains: {_values(policy.strict_domains)}",
        f"- Redact secrets: **{policy.redact_secrets}**",
        f"- Fail closed: **{policy.fail_closed}**",
        f"- Entropy threshold: `{policy.entropy_threshold}`",
        f"- Min secret length: `{policy.min_secret_length}`",
        "",
        "## Ignored paths",
        "```",
        "\n".join(policy.ignore_paths) or "-",
        "```",
        "## Silenced rules",
        "```",
        "\n".join(policy.ignore_rules) or "-",
        "```",
        "",
        f"_Stored overrides: {stored or 'none (defaults)'}_",
        "",
        "> Set `CODX_JUNIOR_CISO_DISABLED=1` in the environment for an emergency stop.",
    ])

"""Pre-commit secret gate.

Run it from a git hook::

    PYTHONPATH=<repo>/api python -m codx.junior.security.ciso.precommit

Exit codes
    0   the staged diff is clean (or has nothing to scan),
    1   a credential was found: the commit must be stopped,
    3   the scanner could not run (missing dependencies, no git): the hook
        decides whether that is fatal (``CISO_PRECOMMIT_STRICT=1``).

Why the check belongs here
    Remote push protection fires *after* the commit exists: the secret is
    already a blob in the local object database, reachable from any branch and
    from the reflog, and stopping it then costs a history rewrite plus a
    credential rotation. This gate runs before the object is created, needs no
    network, works with any remote (GitHub, GitLab, self-hosted) and scans
    source files, not only committed history.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import os
import subprocess
import sys
from typing import List, Optional

#: Exit code when the staged changes are clean.
EXIT_OK = 0
#: Exit code when a finding blocks the commit.
EXIT_BLOCKED = 1
#: Exit code when the gate could not run at all.
EXIT_UNAVAILABLE = 3

#: ``--unified=0`` keeps the diff small; ``scan_diff`` reads added lines only.
DIFF_COMMAND = ["git", "diff", "--cached", "--unified=0", "--no-color"]


def staged_diff() -> str:
    """Return the staged patch (``git diff --cached``).

    Returns:
        str: Unified diff of the changes the next commit would include.

    Raises:
        OSError: ``git`` is not available.
        subprocess.CalledProcessError: the command failed (not a repository).
    """
    completed = subprocess.run(
        DIFF_COMMAND,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    )
    return completed.stdout or ""


def package_prefix() -> str:
    """Return the repo-relative folder of the CISO package itself.

    Returns:
        str: ``"<path>/"`` (with a trailing slash), or ``""`` when the package
        is not inside the repository being committed.
    """
    here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    try:
        completed = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
        )
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
        return ""
    root = (completed.stdout or "").strip()
    if not root:
        return ""
    relative = os.path.relpath(here, root).replace(os.sep, "/")
    if relative.startswith(".."):
        return ""
    return f"{relative}/"


def relevant_findings(findings: List) -> List:
    """Drop findings located inside the CISO package itself.

    The detectors, their rule tables and their documentation have to CONTAIN
    the patterns they look for: the literal token shape, the private-key header
    and ``rm -rf /`` appear in this package by construction. Scanning it would
    block every change to the security module and train people to use
    ``--no-verify``, which is worse than the blind spot.

    The blind spot is bounded and covered elsewhere: ``tests/security``
    exercises the detectors against generated values, and the package holds no
    deployable code — a credential written next to a rule is caught by the same
    gate in the next file that uses it.

    Args:
        findings: Findings produced by :func:`guard_diff`.

    Returns:
        List: Findings that must still block the commit.
    """
    prefix = package_prefix()
    if not prefix:
        return list(findings)
    return [
        finding
        for finding in findings
        if not (getattr(finding, "path", "") or "")
        .replace(os.sep, "/")
        .startswith(prefix)
    ]


def main(argv: Optional[list] = None) -> int:
    """Scan the staged changes and decide whether the commit may proceed.

    Args:
        argv: Unused (kept for ``python -m`` compatibility).

    Returns:
        int: One of :data:`EXIT_OK`, :data:`EXIT_BLOCKED`, :data:`EXIT_UNAVAILABLE`.
    """
    try:
        from codx.junior.security.ciso import gate
        from codx.junior.security.ciso import policy as ciso_policy
        from codx.junior.security.ciso.models import SecurityDomain
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - depends on the environment
        print(f"CISO: the secret scanner is not importable ({ex})", file=sys.stderr)
        return EXIT_UNAVAILABLE

    try:
        patch = staged_diff()
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as ex:
        print(f"CISO: could not read the staged diff ({ex})", file=sys.stderr)
        return EXIT_UNAVAILABLE

    if not patch.strip():
        return EXIT_OK

    scanned = gate.guard_diff(patch)
    findings = relevant_findings(scanned.findings)
    if not findings:
        return EXIT_OK

    # Re-evaluate the ladder on the findings that survive the filter: keeping
    # the original decision would block on a rule the filter just dropped.
    policy = ciso_policy.resolve_policy(None)
    verdict = ciso_policy.evaluate(
        findings,
        domain=SecurityDomain.GIT_COMMIT,
        policy=policy,
        rules_evaluated=scanned.rules_evaluated,
        truncated=scanned.truncated,
    )

    print(ciso_policy.render_report(verdict, title="CISO pre-commit report"))
    if verdict.blocked:
        print(
            "\nCISO: commit blocked. Remove the credential, rotate it (assume it "
            "is disclosed) and stage the fix.\n"
            "Inspect the staged changes with: git diff --cached",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return EXIT_BLOCKED
    return EXIT_OK


if __name__ == "__main__":  # pragma: no cover
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

_ASSIGNMENT_PATTERN = re.compile(
    r"(?P<key>[A-Za-z0-9_.\-]*(?:passw(?:or)?d|passwd|pwd|secret|token|api[_\-]?key|"

)

_URL_CREDENTIALS_PATTERN = re.compile(
    r"\b(?P<scheme>https?|ftp|smtp|ssh|ldap)://(?P<user>[^\s:@/{]{1,64}):(?P<password>[^\s@/{]{3,64})@[^\s/]+",

_ENTROPY_CANDIDATE_PATTERN = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9+/=_\-]{20,}")

# Redaction marker kept short so it survives excerpt truncation.
REDACTED_MARKER = "[REDACTED]"


def shannon_entropy(value: str) -> float:
    """Return the Shannon entropy (bits per character) of *value*.

    Args:
        value: Text to measure.

    Returns:
        float: Entropy in bits/char; ``0.0`` for an empty string.

    Example:
        >>> round(shannon_entropy("aaaaaaaa"), 2)
        0.0
        >>> shannon_entropy("aB3$xY9!qW2&zR5%") > 3
        True
    """
    if not value:
        return 0.0
    counts = Counter(value)
    length = len(value)
    return -sum((count / length) * math.log2(count / length) for count in counts.values())


def is_secret_file(path: Optional[str]) -> bool:
    """Return True when *path* is a file conventionally holding credentials.

    Args:
        path: File path (relative or absolute).

    Returns:
        bool: True for ``.env``, ``*.pem``, ``id_rsa``, ``.npmrc``, ...

    Example:
        >>> is_secret_file("config/.env.production")
        True
        >>> is_secret_file("src/app.py")
        False
    """
    if not path:
        return False
    normalised = path.replace("\\", "/")
    return any(pattern.search(normalised) for pattern in _SECRET_FILE_PATTERNS)


def is_secret_placeholder(value: str) -> bool:
    """Return True when *value* looks like a placeholder instead of a secret.

    Filters documentation examples, environment variable references and
    identifiers, which are the main source of false positives.

    Paths are also rejected: a long absolute project path
    (``/home/user/projects/my-project-api``) has enough entropy to look like a
    token, and every settings or config file written by the platform contains
    dozens of them.

    Args:
        value: Candidate secret value.

    Returns:
        bool: True when the value must not be reported.
    """
    candidate = (value or "").strip()
    if not candidate:
        return True
    if len(candidate) < 8:
        return True
    if candidate.startswith(("/", "~/", "./", "../")):
        # Filesystem path, not a credential.
        return True
    return any(pattern.search(candidate) for pattern in _PLACEHOLDER_PATTERNS)


def _redact(value: str) -> str:
    """Render a detected secret in a shape that cannot be reused.

    A short prefix is kept so a human can tell *which* credential leaked in a
    report, while the remainder is unrecoverable.

    Args:
        value: Raw secret.

    Returns:
        str: Redacted representation.
    """
    text = (value or "").strip()
    if not text:
        return REDACTED_MARKER
    if len(text) <= 8:
        return REDACTED_MARKER
    return f"{text[:4]}{REDACTED_MARKER}({len(text)} chars)"


def _line_of(text: str, index: int) -> int:
    """Return the 1-based line number of *index* inside *text*."""
    return text.count("\n", 0, index) + 1


def _excerpt(text: str, start: int, end: int, max_chars: int) -> str:
    """Build a redacted, bounded excerpt around a match."""
    radius = max(20, max_chars // 2)
    left = max(0, start - radius)
    right = min(len(text), end + radius)
    excerpt = text[left:right].replace("\n", " ⏎ ")
    if len(excerpt) > max_chars:
        excerpt = excerpt[:max_chars] + "…"
    return excerpt


def redact_text(text: str, policy: Optional[CisoPolicy] = None) -> Tuple[str, int]:
    """Neutralise every detected secret inside *text*.

    Args:
        text: Payload to sanitise.
        policy: Optional policy (size and excerpt limits).

    Returns:
        tuple: ``(redacted_text, replacements)``. When nothing matched the
        original string is returned unchanged and replacements is ``0``.

    Example:
        >>> redact_text('password = "s3cr3t-value-1234"')[0]
        'password = "s3cr…'
    """
    policy = policy or CisoPolicy()
    result = text or ""
    replacements = 0

    def _replace(match: re.Match) -> str:
        nonlocal replacements
        raw = match.group(0)
        if is_secret_placeholder(raw):
            return raw
        replacements += 1
        return _redact(raw)

    for _, _, _, pattern in _TOKEN_PATTERNS:
        result = pattern.sub(_replace, result)

    def _replace_assignment(match: re.Match) -> str:
        nonlocal replacements
        value = match.group("value")
        if is_secret_placeholder(value):
            return match.group(0)
        replacements += 1
        return match.group(0).replace(value, _redact(value))

    result = _ASSIGNMENT_PATTERN.sub(_replace_assignment, result)

    def _replace_url(match: re.Match) -> str:
        nonlocal replacements
        password = match.group("password")
        if is_secret_placeholder(password):
            return match.group(0)
        replacements += 1
        return match.group(0).replace(f":{password}@", f":{_redact(password)}@", 1)

    result = _URL_CREDENTIALS_PATTERN.sub(_replace_url, result)
    return result, replacements


def scan_text(
    text: str,
    path: Optional[str] = None,
    policy: Optional[CisoPolicy] = None,
) -> Tuple[List[SecurityFinding], str, bool]:
    """Detect secrets in *text*.

    Args:
        text: Payload to scan.
        path: File the payload belongs to (used for reporting and for the
            entropy relaxation inside documentation files).
        policy: Optional policy.

    Returns:
        tuple: ``(findings, redacted_text, truncated)``. The redacted text is
        safe to log and is what callers must store when they only need to keep
        a record of the payload.
    """
    policy = policy or CisoPolicy()
    payload = text or ""
    truncated = False
    if len(payload.encode("utf-8", errors="replace")) > policy.max_scan_bytes:
        payload = payload.encode("utf-8", errors="replace")[: policy.max_scan_bytes].decode(
            "utf-8", errors="replace"
        )
        truncated = True

    findings: List[SecurityFinding] = []

    def _add(
        rule_id: str,
        title: str,
        severity: SecuritySeverity,
        category: SecurityCategory,
        start: int,
        end: int,
        evidence: str,
        remediation: str,
    ) -> None:
        if policy.ignores_rule(rule_id):
            return
        findings.append(SecurityFinding(
            rule_id=rule_id,
            title=title,
            severity=severity,
            category=category,
            reason=f"Detected {title.lower()} in the payload",
            path=path,
            line=_line_of(payload, start),
            excerpt=_excerpt(payload, start, end, policy.max_excerpt_chars),
            evidence=_redact(evidence),
            remediation=remediation,
            confidence=0.95,
        ))

    for rule_id, title, severity, pattern in _TOKEN_PATTERNS:
        for match in pattern.finditer(payload):
            _add(
                rule_id=rule_id,
                title=title,
                severity=severity,
                category=SecurityCategory.SECRET,
                start=match.start(),
                end=match.end(),
                evidence=match.group(0),
                remediation=(
                    "Remove the credential from the file, rotate it at the provider "
                    "and load it from the environment or the project secret store."
                ),
            )

    for match in _ASSIGNMENT_PATTERN.finditer(payload):
        value = match.group("value")
        if is_secret_placeholder(value):
            continue
        key = match.group("key")
        severity = SecuritySeverity.HIGH
        if (match.group("quote") == '"' or match.group("quote") == "'") and len(value) >= 16:
            severity = SecuritySeverity.CRITICAL
        _add(
            rule_id="secret.hardcoded-credential",
            title=f"Hardcoded credential in '{key}'",
            severity=severity,
            category=SecurityCategory.SECRET,
            start=match.start("value"),
            end=match.end("value"),
            evidence=value,
            remediation=(
                "Read the value from an environment variable or a secret manager "
                "and keep only a placeholder in the source file."
            ),
        )

    for match in _URL_CREDENTIALS_PATTERN.finditer(payload):
        password = match.group("password")
        if is_secret_placeholder(password):
            continue
        _add(
            rule_id="secret.url-embedded-credentials",
            title="Credentials embedded in a URL",
            severity=SecuritySeverity.CRITICAL,
            category=SecurityCategory.SECRET,
            start=match.start("password"),
            end=match.end("password"),
            evidence=password,
            remediation=(
                "Remove the user:password pair from the URL and pass the "
                "credential through a header or a secret reference."
            ),
        )

    if policy.entropy_threshold > 0:
        for match in _ENTROPY_CANDIDATE_PATTERN.finditer(payload):
            token = match.group(0)
            if len(token) < policy.min_secret_length:
                continue
            if is_secret_placeholder(token):
                continue
            # A long run of the same character class is usually an identifier,
            # a hash of a non-secret or an already redacted value.
            if REDACTED_MARKER in token:
                continue
            if shannon_entropy(token) < policy.entropy_threshold:
                continue
            _add(
                rule_id="secret.high-entropy-token",
                title="High entropy string (possible unknown token format)",
                severity=SecuritySeverity.MEDIUM,
                category=SecurityCategory.SECRET,
                start=match.start(),
                end=match.end(),
                evidence=token,
                remediation=(
                    "Confirm what this value is. If it is a credential, rotate it "
                    "and load it from the environment."
                ),
            )

    redacted, _ = redact_text(payload, policy)
    return findings, redacted, truncated

# `password = "hunter2"` style. Kept separate so the placeholder filter and the
# minimum length can be applied to the captured value.
_ASSIGNMENT_PATTERN = re.compile(
    r"(?P<key>[A-Za-z0-9_.\-]*(?:passw(?:or)?d|passwd|pwd|secret|token|api[_\-]?key|"
    r"apikey|access[_\-]?key|private[_\-]?key|client[_\-]?secret|auth[_\-]?key|"
    r"credentials?|bearer|session[_\-]?id)[A-Za-z0-9_.\-]*)"
    r"\s*(?P<sep>[:=]|=>)\s*"
    r"(?P<quote>['\"`])(?P<value>[^'\"`\n]{3,})['\"`]",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

_URL_CREDENTIALS_PATTERN = re.compile(
    r"\b(?P<scheme>https?|ftp|smtp|ssh|ldap)://(?P<user>[^\s:@/{]{1,64}):(?P<password>[^\s@/{]{3,64})@[^\s/]+",

_ENTROPY_CANDIDATE_PATTERN = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9+/=_\-]{20,}")

_PLACEHOLDER_PATTERNS: List[re.Pattern] = [
    re.compile(r"^(?:x{3,}|\*{3,}|\.{3,}|-{3,})$", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"^(?:your|my|the)[_\- ]?(?:api|secret|access|private)?[_\- ]?(?:key|token|password|secret|here)", re.IGNORECASE),

    re.compile(r"\{\{?[^}]+\}?\}"),               # {{token}} / {token}
    re.compile(r"\$\{?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\}?"),  # ${VAR} / $VAR
    # NAME=value: prose, documentation examples and command lines
    # (``PYTHONPATH=/home/x/y``) are long and random enough to look like a
    # token. An actual assignment is caught by the assignment rules instead.
    re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*="),
    re.compile(r"%(?:s|d|\()"),                   # printf placeholder
    re.compile(r"^(?:os\.environ|process\.env|env\(|getenv)", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"^(?:redacted|masked|removed|hidden|encrypted|not[_\-]?set|no[_\-]?value)$", re.IGNORECASE),

    re.compile(r"^[a-z]+(?:_[a-z]+){2,}$"),       # snake_case identifier, not a value
    re.compile(r"^[A-Z][a-z]+(?:[A-Z][a-z]+){1,}$"),  # CamelCase identifier

_SECRET_FILE_PATTERNS: List[re.Pattern] = [
    re.compile(r"(^|/)\.env(\..+)?$"),
    re.compile(r"(^|/)\.envrc$"),
    re.compile(r"\.pem$"), re.compile(r"\.p12$"), re.compile(r"\.pfx$"),

    re.compile(r"(^|/)credentials(?:\.json)?$"),

    re.compile(r"(^|/)secrets?\.(?:json|ya?ml|toml)$"),

# Redaction marker kept short so it survives excerpt truncation.
REDACTED_MARKER = "[REDACTED]"


def shannon_entropy(value: str) -> float:
    """Return the Shannon entropy (bits per character) of *value*.

    Args:
        value: Text to measure.

    Returns:
        float: Entropy in bits/char; ``0.0`` for an empty string.

    Example:
        >>> round(shannon_entropy("aaaaaaaa"), 2)
        0.0
        >>> shannon_entropy("aB3$xY9!qW2&zR5%") > 3
        True
    """
    if not value:
        return 0.0
    counts = Counter(value)
    length = len(value)
    return -sum((count / length) * math.log2(count / length) for count in counts.values())


def is_secret_file(path: Optional[str]) -> bool:
    """Return True when *path* is a file conventionally holding credentials.

    Args:
        path: File path (relative or absolute).

    Returns:
        bool: True for ``.env``, ``*.pem``, ``id_rsa``, ``.npmrc``, ...

    Example:
        >>> is_secret_file("config/.env.production")
        True
        >>> is_secret_file("src/app.py")
        False
    """
    if not path:
        return False
    normalised = path.replace("\\", "/")
    return any(pattern.search(normalised) for pattern in _SECRET_FILE_PATTERNS)


def is_secret_placeholder(value: str) -> bool:
    """Return True when *value* looks like a placeholder instead of a secret.

    Filters documentation examples, environment variable references and
    identifiers, which are the main source of false positives.

    Paths are also rejected: a long absolute project path
    (``/home/user/projects/my-project-api``) has enough entropy to look like a
    token, and every settings or config file written by the platform contains
    dozens of them.

    Args:
        value: Candidate secret value.

    Returns:
        bool: True when the value must not be reported.
    """
    candidate = (value or "").strip()
    if not candidate:
        return True
    if len(candidate) < 8:
        return True
    if candidate.startswith(("/", "~/", "./", "../")):
        # Filesystem path, not a credential.
        return True
    return any(pattern.search(candidate) for pattern in _PLACEHOLDER_PATTERNS)


def _redact(value: str) -> str:
    """Render a detected secret in a shape that cannot be reused.

    A short prefix is kept so a human can tell *which* credential leaked in a
    report, while the remainder is unrecoverable.

    Args:
        value: Raw secret.

    Returns:
        str: Redacted representation.
    """
    text = (value or "").strip()
    if not text:
        return REDACTED_MARKER
    if len(text) <= 8:
        return REDACTED_MARKER
    return f"{text[:4]}{REDACTED_MARKER}({len(text)} chars)"


def _line_of(text: str, index: int) -> int:
    """Return the 1-based line number of *index* inside *text*."""
    return text.count("\n", 0, index) + 1


def _excerpt(text: str, start: int, end: int, max_chars: int) -> str:
    """Build a redacted, bounded excerpt around a match."""
    radius = max(20, max_chars // 2)
    left = max(0, start - radius)
    right = min(len(text), end + radius)
    excerpt = text[left:right].replace("\n", " ⏎ ")
    if len(excerpt) > max_chars:
        excerpt = excerpt[:max_chars] + "…"
    return excerpt


def redact_text(text: str, policy: Optional[CisoPolicy] = None) -> Tuple[str, int]:
    """Neutralise every detected secret inside *text*.

    Args:
        text: Payload to sanitise.
        policy: Optional policy (size and excerpt limits).

    Returns:
        tuple: ``(redacted_text, replacements)``. When nothing matched the
        original string is returned unchanged and replacements is ``0``.

    Example:
        >>> redact_text('password = "s3cr3t-value-1234"')[0]
        'password = "s3cr…'
    """
    policy = policy or CisoPolicy()
    result = text or ""
    replacements = 0

    def _replace(match: re.Match) -> str:
        nonlocal replacements
        raw = match.group(0)
        if is_secret_placeholder(raw):
            return raw
        replacements += 1
        return _redact(raw)

    for _, _, _, pattern in _TOKEN_PATTERNS:
        result = pattern.sub(_replace, result)

    def _replace_assignment(match: re.Match) -> str:
        nonlocal replacements
        value = match.group("value")
        if is_secret_placeholder(value):
            return match.group(0)
        replacements += 1
        return match.group(0).replace(value, _redact(value))

    result = _ASSIGNMENT_PATTERN.sub(_replace_assignment, result)

    def _replace_url(match: re.Match) -> str:
        nonlocal replacements
        password = match.group("password")
        if is_secret_placeholder(password):
            return match.group(0)
        replacements += 1
        return match.group(0).replace(f":{password}@", f":{_redact(password)}@", 1)

    result = _URL_CREDENTIALS_PATTERN.sub(_replace_url, result)
    return result, replacements


def scan_text(
    text: str,
    path: Optional[str] = None,
    policy: Optional[CisoPolicy] = None,
) -> Tuple[List[SecurityFinding], str, bool]:
    """Detect secrets in *text*.

    Args:
        text: Payload to scan.
        path: File the payload belongs to (used for reporting and for the
            entropy relaxation inside documentation files).
        policy: Optional policy.

    Returns:
        tuple: ``(findings, redacted_text, truncated)``. The redacted text is
        safe to log and is what callers must store when they only need to keep
        a record of the payload.
    """
    policy = policy or CisoPolicy()
    payload = text or ""
    truncated = False
    if len(payload.encode("utf-8", errors="replace")) > policy.max_scan_bytes:
        payload = payload.encode("utf-8", errors="replace")[: policy.max_scan_bytes].decode(
            "utf-8", errors="replace"
        )
        truncated = True

    findings: List[SecurityFinding] = []

    def _add(
        rule_id: str,
        title: str,
        severity: SecuritySeverity,
        category: SecurityCategory,
        start: int,
        end: int,
        evidence: str,
        remediation: str,
    ) -> None:
        if policy.ignores_rule(rule_id):
            return
        findings.append(SecurityFinding(
            rule_id=rule_id,
            title=title,
            severity=severity,
            category=category,
            reason=f"Detected {title.lower()} in the payload",
            path=path,
            line=_line_of(payload, start),
            excerpt=_excerpt(payload, start, end, policy.max_excerpt_chars),
            evidence=_redact(evidence),
            remediation=remediation,
            confidence=0.95,
        ))

    for rule_id, title, severity, pattern in _TOKEN_PATTERNS:
        for match in pattern.finditer(payload):
            _add(
                rule_id=rule_id,
                title=title,
                severity=severity,
                category=SecurityCategory.SECRET,
                start=match.start(),
                end=match.end(),
                evidence=match.group(0),
                remediation=(
                    "Remove the credential from the file, rotate it at the provider "
                    "and load it from the environment or the project secret store."
                ),
            )

    for match in _ASSIGNMENT_PATTERN.finditer(payload):
        value = match.group("value")
        if is_secret_placeholder(value):
            continue
        key = match.group("key")
        severity = SecuritySeverity.HIGH
        if (match.group("quote") == '"' or match.group("quote") == "'") and len(value) >= 16:
            severity = SecuritySeverity.CRITICAL
        _add(
            rule_id="secret.hardcoded-credential",
            title=f"Hardcoded credential in '{key}'",
            severity=severity,
            category=SecurityCategory.SECRET,
            start=match.start("value"),
            end=match.end("value"),
            evidence=value,
            remediation=(
                "Read the value from an environment variable or a secret manager "
                "and keep only a placeholder in the source file."
            ),
        )

    for match in _URL_CREDENTIALS_PATTERN.finditer(payload):
        password = match.group("password")
        if is_secret_placeholder(password):
            continue
        _add(
            rule_id="secret.url-embedded-credentials",
            title="Credentials embedded in a URL",
            severity=SecuritySeverity.CRITICAL,
            category=SecurityCategory.SECRET,
            start=match.start("password"),
            end=match.end("password"),
            evidence=password,
            remediation=(
                "Remove the user:password pair from the URL and pass the "
                "credential through a header or a secret reference."
            ),
        )

    if policy.entropy_threshold > 0:
        for match in _ENTROPY_CANDIDATE_PATTERN.finditer(payload):
            token = match.group(0)
            if len(token) < policy.min_secret_length:
                continue
            if is_secret_placeholder(token):
                continue
            # A long run of the same character class is usually an identifier,
            # a hash of a non-secret or an already redacted value.
            if REDACTED_MARKER in token:
                continue
            if shannon_entropy(token) < policy.entropy_threshold:
                continue
            _add(
                rule_id="secret.high-entropy-token",
                title="High entropy string (possible unknown token format)",
                severity=SecuritySeverity.MEDIUM,
                category=SecurityCategory.SECRET,
                start=match.start(),
                end=match.end(),
                evidence=token,
                remediation=(
                    "Confirm what this value is. If it is a credential, rotate it "
                    "and load it from the environment."
                ),
            )

    redacted, _ = redact_text(payload, policy)
    return findings, redacted, truncated

    """Drop findings located inside the CISO package itself.

    The detectors, their rule tables and their documentation have to CONTAIN
    the patterns they look for: the literal token shape, the private-key header
    and ``rm -rf /`` appear in this package by construction. Scanning it would
    block every change to the security module and train people to use
    ``--no-verify``, which is worse than the blind spot.

    The blind spot is bounded and covered elsewhere: ``tests/security``
    exercises the detectors against generated values, and the package holds no
    deployable code — a credential written next to a rule is caught by the same
    gate in the next file that uses it.

    Args:
        findings: Findings produced by :func:`guard_diff`.

    Returns:
        List: Findings that must still block the commit.
    """
    prefix = package_prefix()
    if not prefix:
        return list(findings)
    return [
        finding
        for finding in findings
        if not (getattr(finding, "path", "") or "")
        .replace(os.sep, "/")
        .startswith(prefix)
    ]

"""Pre-commit secret gate.

Run it from a git hook::

    PYTHONPATH=<repo>/api python -m codx.junior.security.ciso.precommit

Exit codes
    0   the staged diff is clean (or has nothing to scan),
    1   a credential was found: the commit must be stopped,
    3   the scanner could not run (missing dependencies, no git): the hook
        decides whether that is fatal (``CISO_PRECOMMIT_STRICT=1``).

Why the check belongs here
    Remote push protection fires *after* the commit exists: the secret is
    already a blob in the local object database, reachable from any branch and
    from the reflog, and stopping it then costs a history rewrite plus a
    credential rotation. This gate runs before the object is created, needs no
    network, works with any remote (GitHub, GitLab, self-hosted) and scans
    source files, not only committed history.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import os
import subprocess
import sys
from typing import List, Optional

#: Exit code when the staged changes are clean.
EXIT_OK = 0
#: Exit code when a finding blocks the commit.
EXIT_BLOCKED = 1
#: Exit code when the gate could not run at all.
EXIT_UNAVAILABLE = 3

#: ``--unified=0`` keeps the diff small; ``scan_diff`` reads added lines only.
DIFF_COMMAND = ["git", "diff", "--cached", "--unified=0", "--no-color"]


def staged_diff() -> str:
    """Return the staged patch (``git diff --cached``).

    Returns:
        str: Unified diff of the changes the next commit would include.

    Raises:
        OSError: ``git`` is not available.
        subprocess.CalledProcessError: the command failed (not a repository).
    """
    completed = subprocess.run(
        DIFF_COMMAND,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    )
    return completed.stdout or ""


def package_prefix() -> str:
    """Return the repo-relative folder of the CISO package itself.

    Returns:
        str: ``"<path>/"`` (with a trailing slash), or ``""`` when the package
        is not inside the repository being committed.
    """
    here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    try:
        completed = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
        )
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
        return ""
    root = (completed.stdout or "").strip()
    if not root:
        return ""
    relative = os.path.relpath(here, root).replace(os.sep, "/")
    if relative.startswith(".."):
        return ""
    return f"{relative}/"


def excluded_prefixes() -> tuple:
    """Return the repo-relative folders this gate does not scan.

    Two folders must CONTAIN the patterns the detectors look for:

    * the CISO package itself — rule tables and their documentation,
    * ``<api>/tests/security`` — fixtures with fake AWS keys, a reverse shell,
      ``rm -rf /`` and ``ignore previous instructions``.

    Every secret scanner needs such an allowlist: without it the gate blocks
    its own maintenance, and people learn to reach for ``--no-verify``, which
    disables the protection everywhere.

    Returns:
        tuple: Path prefixes (with trailing slash) to skip.
    """
    package = package_prefix()
    if not package:
        return ()
    api_root = package.split("/", 1)[0]
    return (package, f"{api_root}/tests/security/")


def relevant_findings(findings: List) -> List:
    """Drop findings located inside the scanner or its fixtures.

    Args:
        findings: Findings produced by :func:`guard_diff`.

    Returns:
        List: Findings that must still block the commit.
    """
    prefixes = excluded_prefixes()
    if not prefixes:
        return list(findings)
    return [
        finding
        for finding in findings
        if not any(
            (getattr(finding, "path", "") or "").replace(os.sep, "/").startswith(prefix)
            for prefix in prefixes
        )
    ]


def main(argv: Optional[list] = None) -> int:
    """Scan the staged changes and decide whether the commit may proceed.

    Args:
        argv: Unused (kept for ``python -m`` compatibility).

    Returns:
        int: One of :data:`EXIT_OK`, :data:`EXIT_BLOCKED`, :data:`EXIT_UNAVAILABLE`.
    """
    try:
        from codx.junior.security.ciso import gate
        from codx.junior.security.ciso import policy as ciso_policy
        from codx.junior.security.ciso.models import SecurityDomain
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - depends on the environment
        print(f"CISO: the secret scanner is not importable ({ex})", file=sys.stderr)
        return EXIT_UNAVAILABLE

    try:
        patch = staged_diff()
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as ex:
        print(f"CISO: could not read the staged diff ({ex})", file=sys.stderr)
        return EXIT_UNAVAILABLE

    if not patch.strip():
        return EXIT_OK

    scanned = gate.guard_diff(patch)
    findings = relevant_findings(scanned.findings)
    if not findings:
        return EXIT_OK

    # Re-evaluate the ladder on the findings that survive the filter: keeping
    # the original decision would block on a rule the filter just dropped.
    policy = ciso_policy.resolve_policy(None)
    verdict = ciso_policy.evaluate(
        findings,
        domain=SecurityDomain.GIT_COMMIT,
        policy=policy,
        rules_evaluated=scanned.rules_evaluated,
        truncated=scanned.truncated,
    )

    print(ciso_policy.render_report(verdict, title="CISO pre-commit report"))
    if verdict.blocked:
        print(
            "\nCISO: commit blocked. Remove the credential, rotate it (assume it "
            "is disclosed) and stage the fix.\n"
            "Inspect the staged changes with: git diff --cached",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return EXIT_BLOCKED
    return EXIT_OK


if __name__ == "__main__":  # pragma: no cover
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

"""Repository audit: what is already committed?

The gates stop new secrets, the pre-commit hook stops a commit. Neither can
clean a repository that already contains them, and the most valuable artifact of
a security review is the list of what is *there today*.

Scope it at a tracked data plane, not the whole tree::

    PYTHONPATH=<repo>/api python -m codx.junior.security.ciso.audit .codx --max-files 2000

The audit reports findings only — the evidence is redacted, so the report can be
attached to a ticket. It never modifies anything.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import argparse
import sys
from typing import List, Optional, Sequence

from codx.junior.security.ciso import policy as ciso_policy
from codx.junior.security.ciso import scanner
from codx.junior.security.ciso.models import SecurityDomain


def audit(
    paths: Sequence[str],
    project_path: str = ".",
    max_files: int = 2000,
    domain: SecurityDomain = SecurityDomain.FILE_READ,
) -> str:
    """Scan *paths* and return a Markdown report.

    Args:
        paths: Project-relative folders or files to audit.
        project_path: Project root.
        max_files: Global file budget (the scan is bounded on purpose).
        domain: Domain recorded in the report.

    Returns:
        str: Markdown report (``"clean"`` style summary when nothing matched).
    """
    policy = ciso_policy.resolve_policy(None)
    budget = max_files
    reports: List[str] = []
    findings = 0

    for path in paths:
        target = path
        if not target.startswith("/"):
            target = f"{project_path.rstrip('/')}/{path.lstrip('./')}" if project_path != "." else path
        verdict = scanner.scan_project(
            project_path=project_path,
            max_files=max(budget, 1),
            domain=domain,
            policy=policy,
            paths=[target],
        )
        findings += len(verdict.findings)
        if not verdict.findings:
            continue
        reports.append(
            ciso_policy.render_report(
                verdict,
                title=f"CISO audit — {path}",
                max_findings=25,
            )
        )

    if not reports:
        return f"## CISO audit\n\nNo finding in: {', '.join(f'`{p}`' for p in paths)}"
    return "\n\n".join(reports)


def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
    """CLI entry point.

    Args:
        argv: Command line arguments (defaults to ``sys.argv[1:]``).

    Returns:
        int: ``0`` when nothing was found, ``1`` when the audit reported
        findings (so it can fail a pipeline).
    """
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="ciso.audit",
        description="Scan project paths for credentials and malicious content.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("paths", nargs="+", help="Paths to audit (project relative).")
    parser.add_argument("--project-path", default=".", help="Project root.")
    parser.add_argument("--max-files", type=int, default=2000, help="File budget.")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    report = audit(
        paths=args.paths,
        project_path=args.project_path,
        max_files=args.max_files,
    )
    print(report)
    return 0 if "No finding in" in report else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":  # pragma: no cover
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

"""Repository audit: what is already committed?

The gates stop new secrets and the pre-commit hook stops a commit. Neither can
clean a repository that already contains them, and the most valuable artifact of
a security review is the list of what is *there today*.

Scope it at a tracked data plane, not the whole tree::

    PYTHONPATH=<repo>/api python -m codx.junior.security.ciso.audit .codx \
        --project-path . --max-files 2000

The audit only reads: nothing is modified and every finding carries redacted
evidence, so the report can be attached to a ticket as it is.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import argparse
import os
import sys
from typing import List, Optional, Sequence

from codx.junior.security.ciso import policy as ciso_policy
from codx.junior.security.ciso import scanner
from codx.junior.security.ciso.models import SecurityDomain


def collect_targets(
    paths: Sequence[str],
    project_path: str = ".",
    max_files: int = 2000,
) -> List[str]:
    """Expand *paths* (files or folders) into a bounded list of files.

    Args:
        paths: Project-relative or absolute files/folders.
        project_path: Project root used to resolve relative paths.
        max_files: Maximum number of files returned.

    Returns:
        List[str]: Absolute file paths.
    """
    policy = ciso_policy.resolve_policy(None)
    targets: List[str] = []
    for path in paths:
        absolute = path if os.path.isabs(path) else os.path.join(project_path, path)
        absolute = os.path.abspath(absolute)
        if os.path.isdir(absolute):
            targets.extend(
                scanner.iter_project_files(absolute, max_files=max_files, policy=policy)
            )
        elif os.path.isfile(absolute):
            targets.append(absolute)
        else:
            print(f"CISO audit: '{path}' does not exist", file=sys.stderr)
        if len(targets) >= max_files:
            break
    return targets[:max_files]


def audit(
    paths: Sequence[str],
    project_path: str = ".",
    max_files: int = 2000,
    domain: SecurityDomain = SecurityDomain.FILE_READ,
) -> str:
    """Scan *paths* and return a Markdown report.

    Args:
        paths: Project-relative folders or files to audit.
        project_path: Project root (findings are reported relative to it).
        max_files: Global file budget (the scan is bounded on purpose).
        domain: Domain recorded in the report.

    Returns:
        str: Markdown report; a single "No finding in" line when clean.
    """
    policy = ciso_policy.resolve_policy(None)
    targets = collect_targets(paths, project_path=project_path, max_files=max_files)
    scope = ", ".join(f"`{path}`" for path in paths)

    if not targets:
        return f"## CISO audit\n\nNothing to scan in {scope}"

    verdict = scanner.scan_project(
        project_path=os.path.abspath(project_path),
        max_files=max_files,
        domain=domain,
        policy=policy,
        paths=targets,
    )
    if not verdict.findings:
        return (
            f"## CISO audit\n\nNo finding in {scope} "
            f"({len(targets)} file(s) scanned)."
        )

    r"credentials?|bearer|session[_\-]?id)[A-Za-z0-9_.\-]*)"

    r"(?P<quote>['\"`])(?P<value>[^'\"`\n]{3,})['\"`]",
    re.IGNORECASE,

# URL embedded basic auth: scheme://user:password@host
_URL_CREDENTIALS_PATTERN = re.compile(
    r"\b(?P<scheme>https?|ftp|smtp|ssh|ldap)://(?P<user>[^\s:@/{]{1,64}):(?P<password>[^\s@/{]{3,64})@[^\s/]+",
    re.IGNORECASE,

# High entropy candidates: long runs without separators.
_ENTROPY_CANDIDATE_PATTERN = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9+/=_\-]{20,}")

# Values that look like secrets but are obviously placeholders / references.
_PLACEHOLDER_PATTERNS: List[re.Pattern] = [
    re.compile(r"^(?:x{3,}|\*{3,}|\.{3,}|-{3,})$", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"^(?:your|my|the)[_\- ]?(?:api|secret|access|private)?[_\- ]?(?:key|token|password|secret|here)", re.IGNORECASE),

_SECRET_FILE_PATTERNS: List[re.Pattern] = [
