"""Data models for the CISO security subsystem.

The CISO subsystem answers one question everywhere in the platform: *may this
artifact, command or answer cross the trust boundary?*

Three design rules make the answer trustworthy:

* **Deterministic.** Detectors use regular expressions, entropy and structural
  heuristics. No security decision is delegated to an LLM, so a verdict is
  reproducible, cheap and auditable (it can be replayed against a stored diff).
* **Two stages.** *Detectors* only produce :class:`SecurityFinding` signals.
  The *policy engine* (:mod:`codx.junior.security.ciso.policy`) turns the
  signals into a single :class:`SecurityVerdict`. Severity therefore never
  implies an action by itself: the same HIGH finding may block a git commit and
  only warn inside a document.
* **Dependency-free.** These models are plain dataclasses on purpose: the
  package must import on *any* interpreter, because the very same code runs
  inside the API, in a git hook (often from a worktree with no virtualenv), in
  a container image and in CI. A security gate that needs the application
  dependency tree is a gate that stops running exactly when it is needed: it
  dies with an ``ImportError`` at commit time instead of scanning.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import copy as _copy
from dataclasses import dataclass, fields as _dataclass_fields
from enum import Enum
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, get_args, get_origin

_NONE_TYPE = type(None)


@dataclass
class CisoModel:
    """Base class of the CISO models: plain dataclasses, no third-party import.

    It exposes the three attributes the rest of the package (and the tools)
    expect from a model, so replacing the previous pydantic base changed no
    call site:

    * ``model_dump(mode="json")`` -> JSON-safe ``dict`` (enums become values),
    * ``to_dict()`` / ``dict()`` -> the same, for older callers,
    * ``model_copy(update={...})`` -> a copy with fields overridden.

    Values are coerced to their declared enum or nested model on construction,
    which keeps a verdict loaded from ``.codx`` JSON working when its enums come
    back as plain strings.
    """

    def model_dump(self, mode: str = "python", **_: Any) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Return the model as a ``dict`` (``mode="json"`` stringifies enums)."""
        return _plain(self, json_mode=(mode == "json"))

    def dict(self, **kwargs: Any) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Alias of :meth:`model_dump`, kept for pydantic-v1 style callers."""
        return self.model_dump(**kwargs)

    def model_copy(
        self, update: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, deep: bool = False
    ) -> "CisoModel":
        """Return a copy of this model, optionally with *update* applied."""
        clone = _copy.deepcopy(self) if deep else _copy.copy(self)
        for key, value in (update or {}).items():
            setattr(clone, key, value)
        return clone

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Coerce every field to its declared enum/nested-model type."""
        for model_field in _dataclass_fields(self):
            value = getattr(self, model_field.name)
            setattr(self, model_field.name, _coerce(value, model_field.type))


def _coerce_enum(value: Any, enum_type: type) -> Any:
    """Return *value* as a member of *enum_type* when it can be resolved."""
    if value is None or isinstance(value, enum_type):
        return value
    if isinstance(value, str):
        for member in enum_type:
            if value == member.value or value.lower() == member.name.lower():
                return member
    return value


def _coerce(value: Any, hint: Any) -> Any:
    """Coerce *value* to *hint* (enum, nested model or list of them)."""
    if value is None or hint is Any:
        return value
    if hint is int or hint is float:
        if isinstance(value, str) and value.strip().lstrip("-").isdigit():
            return hint(value)
        return value
    origin = get_origin(hint)
    if origin is not None:
        args = get_args(hint)
        if origin is list or origin is List:
            item_hint = args[0] if args else Any
            if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
                return [_coerce(item, item_hint) for item in value]
            return value
        # Optional[X] / Union[...]: coerce with the first matching member.
        for arg in args:
            if arg is _NONE_TYPE or arg is type(None):
                continue
            coerced = _coerce(value, arg)
            if coerced is not value:
                return coerced
        return value
    if isinstance(hint, type):
        if issubclass(hint, Enum):
            return _coerce_enum(value, hint)
        if issubclass(hint, CisoModel) and isinstance(value, dict):
            return hint(**value)
    return value


def _plain(value: Any, json_mode: bool) -> Any:
    """Return *value* with models expanded to dicts (and enums to values)."""
    if isinstance(value, Enum):
        return value.value if json_mode else value
    if isinstance(value, CisoModel):
        return {
            model_field.name: _plain(getattr(value, model_field.name), json_mode)
            for model_field in _dataclass_fields(value)
        }
    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
        return [_plain(item, json_mode) for item in value]
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {key: _plain(item, json_mode) for key, item in value.items()}
    return value


class SecuritySeverity(str, Enum):
    """Severity of a single CISO finding."""

    INFO = "info"
    LOW = "low"
    MEDIUM = "medium"
    HIGH = "high"
    CRITICAL = "critical"


#: Ordering of the severities (higher is worse), used by report filters.
SEVERITY_RANK: Dict[SecuritySeverity, int] = {
    SecuritySeverity.INFO: 0,
    SecuritySeverity.LOW: 1,
    SecuritySeverity.MEDIUM: 2,
    SecuritySeverity.HIGH: 3,
    SecuritySeverity.CRITICAL: 4,
}


def severity_rank(severity: Optional[SecuritySeverity]) -> int:
    """Return the numeric rank of *severity* (``0`` when unknown)."""
    return SEVERITY_RANK.get(severity, 0) if severity else 0


def parse_severity(value: Any) -> Optional[SecuritySeverity]:
    """
    Coerce *value* to a :class:`SecuritySeverity`.

    Args:
        value: A ``SecuritySeverity``, its string name/value, or ``None``.

    Returns:
        The severity, or ``None`` when the value is empty or unknown.
    """
    if isinstance(value, SecuritySeverity):
        return value
    raw = str(value or "").strip().lower()
    if not raw:
        return None
    for severity in SecuritySeverity:
        if raw in (severity.value, severity.name.lower()):
            return severity
    return None


def meets_minimum(
    severity: Optional[SecuritySeverity],
    minimum: Optional[SecuritySeverity],
) -> bool:
    """Return True when *severity* is at least *minimum*."""
    if minimum is None:
        return True
    return severity_rank(severity) >= severity_rank(minimum)


class SecurityCategory(str, Enum):
    """Family of risk a finding belongs to.

    The category drives the remediation advice and lets a policy treat a
    ``secret`` differently from a ``malicious`` finding of the same severity.
    """

    SECRET = "secret"
    MALICIOUS = "malicious"
    INJECTION = "injection"
    DANGEROUS_OPERATION = "dangerous_operation"
    DATA_EXFILTRATION = "data_exfiltration"
    SUPPLY_CHAIN = "supply_chain"
    POLICY = "policy"
    CONFIGURATION = "configuration"


class SecurityDomain(str, Enum):
    """Process (integration point) where the check runs.

    Every value maps to a real choke point of the platform; see
    ``codx/junior/security/ciso/README.md`` for the full map.
    """

    FILE_READ = "file_read"
    FILE_WRITE = "file_write"
    GIT_COMMIT = "git_commit"
    PULL_REQUEST = "pull_request"
    COMMAND = "command"
    CONTAINER = "container"
    NETWORK = "network"
    MODEL_OUTPUT = "model_output"
    KNOWLEDGE_INGESTION = "knowledge_ingestion"
    PROFILE = "profile"
    DEPLOY = "deploy"


class SecurityAction(str, Enum):
    """Decision the policy engine took for a verdict."""

    ALLOW = "allow"
    WARN = "warn"
    REQUIRE_APPROVAL = "require_approval"
    REDACT = "redact"
    BLOCK = "block"


@dataclass
class SecurityFinding(CisoModel):
    """A single signal produced by a detector.

    ``excerpt`` is ALWAYS already redacted: a finding is copied into logs, chat
    messages and audit records, so it must never carry the secret it reports.
    """

    rule_id: str
    title: str = ""
    severity: SecuritySeverity = SecuritySeverity.MEDIUM
    category: SecurityCategory = SecurityCategory.POLICY
    reason: str = ""
    path: Optional[str] = None
    line: Optional[int] = None
    excerpt: str = ""
    evidence: str = ""
    remediation: str = ""
    confidence: Optional[float] = None

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Return a JSON serialisable representation."""
        return self.model_dump(mode="json")


@dataclass
class SecurityVerdict(CisoModel):
    """Aggregated CISO decision for one artifact, command or answer."""

    domain: SecurityDomain = SecurityDomain.FILE_WRITE
    action: SecurityAction = SecurityAction.ALLOW
    allowed: bool = True
    blocked: bool = False
    requires_approval: bool = False
    risk_score: float = 0.0
    highest_severity: Optional[SecuritySeverity] = None
    findings: List[SecurityFinding] = None
    summary: str = ""
    redacted_text: Optional[str] = None
    rules_evaluated: int = 0
    truncated: bool = False

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Coerce the fields and guarantee the mutable default of findings."""
        if self.findings is None:
            self.findings = []
        super().__post_init__()

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Return a JSON serialisable representation."""
        return self.model_dump(mode="json")

    def findings_by_severity(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
        """Count the findings per severity (useful for reports)."""
        counts: Dict[str, int] = {}
        for finding in self.findings:
            key = finding.severity.value
            counts[key] = counts.get(key, 0) + 1
        return counts

    def findings_at_least(
        self, minimum: Optional[SecuritySeverity]
    ) -> List[SecurityFinding]:
        """
        Return the findings whose severity is at least *minimum*.

        Args:
            minimum: Severity floor; ``None`` keeps every finding.

        Returns:
            List[SecurityFinding]: Findings sorted by descending severity.
        """
        kept = [f for f in self.findings if meets_minimum(f.severity, minimum)]
        return sorted(kept, key=lambda f: severity_rank(f.severity), reverse=True)

    def filtered(self, minimum: Optional[SecuritySeverity]) -> "SecurityVerdict":
        """
        Return a copy of this verdict keeping only findings >= *minimum*.

        The risk score, the action and the domain are preserved (they were
        computed from the whole payload); only the finding list and the highest
        severity are recomputed, so a filtered verdict can be rendered safely.
        """
        if minimum is None:
            return self
        kept = self.findings_at_least(minimum)
        highest = max(
            (finding.severity for finding in kept),
            key=severity_rank,
            default=None,
        )
        return self.model_copy(
            update={"findings": kept, "highest_severity": highest}
        )


def _default_block_severities() -> List[SecuritySeverity]:
    """Severities that always block, in every domain."""
    return [SecuritySeverity.CRITICAL]


def _default_block_categories() -> List[SecurityCategory]:
    """Categories blocked once they reach ``block_above``."""
    return [
        SecurityCategory.SECRET,
        SecurityCategory.MALICIOUS,
        SecurityCategory.DATA_EXFILTRATION,
    ]


def _default_strict_domains() -> List[SecurityDomain]:
    """Domains where a finding at ``block_above`` blocks instead of asking."""
    # Every domain that PERSISTS or EXECUTES an artifact. A file write belongs
    # here with the git ones: writing the file is what puts the secret on disk,
    # so redacting it and continuing would leave the repository one `git add`
    # away from the incident.
    return [
        SecurityDomain.FILE_WRITE,
        SecurityDomain.GIT_COMMIT,
        SecurityDomain.PULL_REQUEST,
        SecurityDomain.COMMAND,
        SecurityDomain.CONTAINER,
        SecurityDomain.DEPLOY,
    ]


def _default_ignore_paths() -> List[str]:
    """Path fragments skipped by the file scanners (vendored/generated)."""
    return [
        "node_modules/", "dist/", "build/", ".venv/", "venv/",
        "__pycache__/", ".mypy_cache/", ".pytest_cache/", "package-lock.json",
        "poetry.lock", "yarn.lock",
    ]


@dataclass
class CisoPolicy(CisoModel):
    """Security policy used to decide what happens with the findings.

    The defaults are *fail-safe but not hostile*: secrets and clearly malicious
    code are blocked on the paths that persist or execute something, everything
    else warns. Deployments can tighten or relax it through project settings.
    """

    enabled: bool = True

    block_severities: List[SecuritySeverity] = None
    block_categories: List[SecurityCategory] = None
    block_above: SecuritySeverity = SecuritySeverity.HIGH
    approval_above: SecuritySeverity = SecuritySeverity.MEDIUM
    warn_above: SecuritySeverity = SecuritySeverity.LOW

    redact_secrets: bool = True
    fail_closed: bool = False

    strict_domains: List[SecurityDomain] = None
    enabled_domains: List[SecurityDomain] = None

    ignore_paths: List[str] = None
    ignore_rules: List[str] = None
    allow_secret_files: List[str] = None

    entropy_threshold: float = 4.2
    min_secret_length: int = 20
    max_scan_bytes: int = 1024 * 1024
    max_excerpt_chars: int = 160

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Materialise the list defaults and coerce the enum fields."""
        if self.block_severities is None:
            self.block_severities = _default_block_severities()
        if self.block_categories is None:
            self.block_categories = _default_block_categories()
        if self.strict_domains is None:
            self.strict_domains = _default_strict_domains()
        if self.enabled_domains is None:
            self.enabled_domains = list(SecurityDomain)
        if self.ignore_paths is None:
            self.ignore_paths = _default_ignore_paths()
        if self.ignore_rules is None:
            self.ignore_rules = []
        if self.allow_secret_files is None:
            self.allow_secret_files = []
        super().__post_init__()

    def is_domain_enabled(self, domain: SecurityDomain) -> bool:
        """Return True when the policy runs for *domain*."""
        return self.enabled and domain in self.enabled_domains

    def ignores_path(self, path: Optional[str]) -> bool:
        """Return True when *path* must be skipped (vendored/generated code)."""
        if not path:
            return False
        normalised = path.replace("\\", "/")
        return any(fragment and fragment in normalised for fragment in self.ignore_paths)

    def ignores_rule(self, rule_id: str) -> bool:
        """Return True when *rule_id* is silenced by this policy."""
        return rule_id in (self.ignore_rules or [])

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Return a JSON serialisable representation."""
        return self.model_dump(mode="json")

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# CISO pre-commit gate — stops a credential BEFORE it becomes a commit.
#
# Install (once per clone):
#     git config core.hooksPath .githooks
# Disable for a single commit:
#     git commit --no-verify
# Make it fatal when the scanner cannot run:
#     CISO_PRECOMMIT_STRICT=1 git commit ...
# Force one interpreter:
#     CISO_PYTHON=/usr/bin/python3 git commit ...
#
# The scan itself lives in `codx.junior.security.ciso.precommit` so the hook and
# the platform share one rule set. That package is stdlib-only ON PURPOSE: the
# hook runs from a fresh clone, a PR worktree or a container, where the API
# virtualenv does not exist and third-party imports such as pydantic are simply
# not installed. A gate that needs them dies with an ImportError at commit time
# — i.e. it stops protecting exactly when it is needed. Any redaction or
# detection added anywhere else is security debt.

set -u

root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || exit 0
cd "$root" 2>/dev/null || exit 0

# The API package may live in the MAIN worktree while the commit happens in a PR
# worktree, where `api/.venv` does not exist because a venv is never committed.
common_dir=$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null) || common_dir=".git"
case "$common_dir" in
    /*) ;;
    *) common_dir="$root/$common_dir" ;;
esac
main_root=$(cd "$common_dir/.." 2>/dev/null && pwd) || main_root="$root"

module=codx.junior.security.ciso.precommit
python_bin=""
api_path=""

for api_dir in "$root/api" "$main_root/api"; do
    [ -d "$api_dir/codx/junior/security/ciso" ] || continue
    for candidate in "${CISO_PYTHON:-}" \
                     "$api_dir/.venv/bin/python" \
                     "$(dirname "$api_dir")/.venv/bin/python" \
                     "python3" \
                     "python"; do
        [ -n "$candidate" ] || continue
        command -v "$candidate" >/dev/null 2>&1 || continue
        # Pick the first interpreter that can ACTUALLY import the scanner: an
        # interpreter without the module must never silently disable the gate.
        if PYTHONPATH="$api_dir${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}" \
            "$candidate" -c "import $module" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            python_bin="$candidate"
            api_path="$api_dir"
            break
        fi
    done
    if [ -n "$python_bin" ]; then
        break
    fi
done

if [ -z "$python_bin" ]; then
    echo "CISO: no interpreter could load the secret scanner; the staged changes were NOT scanned." >&2
    echo "CISO: set CISO_PYTHON=<python> or install python3; use CISO_PRECOMMIT_STRICT=1 to make this fatal." >&2
    [ "${CISO_PRECOMMIT_STRICT:-0}" = "1" ] && exit 1
    exit 0
fi

PYTHONPATH="$api_path${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}" \
    "$python_bin" -m "$module"
status=$?

if [ "$status" -eq 3 ]; then
    echo "CISO: the scanner could not run; the staged changes were NOT scanned." >&2
    [ "${CISO_PRECOMMIT_STRICT:-0}" = "1" ] && exit 1
    exit 0
fi

exit "$status"

"""Pre-commit secret gate.

Run it from a git hook::

    PYTHONPATH=<repo>/api python -m codx.junior.security.ciso.precommit

Exit codes
    0   the staged diff is clean (or has nothing to scan),
    1   a credential was found: the commit must be stopped,
    3   the scanner could not run (missing dependencies, no git): the hook
        decides whether that is fatal (``CISO_PRECOMMIT_STRICT=1``).

Runs anywhere
    This module and everything it imports are stdlib-only, so the gate works
    on a bare ``python3``: a fresh clone, a PR worktree (``api/.venv`` is
    never committed), a container image or CI. Needing the application
    dependency tree (pydantic, fastapi, the LLM clients) would make the gate
    die with an ImportError precisely at commit time, which is how it used to
    break; ``tests/security/ciso_import_check.py`` locks that property in.

Why the check belongs here
    Remote push protection fires *after* the commit exists: the secret is
    already a blob in the local object database, reachable from any branch and
    from the reflog, and stopping it then costs a history rewrite plus a
    credential rotation. This gate runs before the object is created, needs no
    network, works with any remote (GitHub, GitLab, self-hosted) and scans
    source files, not only committed history.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import os
import subprocess
import sys
from typing import List, Optional

#: Exit code when the staged changes are clean.
EXIT_OK = 0
#: Exit code when a finding blocks the commit.
EXIT_BLOCKED = 1
#: Exit code when the gate could not run at all.
EXIT_UNAVAILABLE = 3

#: ``--unified=0`` keeps the diff small; ``scan_diff`` reads added lines only.
DIFF_COMMAND = ["git", "diff", "--cached", "--unified=0", "--no-color"]


def staged_diff() -> str:
    """Return the staged patch (``git diff --cached``).

    Returns:
        str: Unified diff of the changes the next commit would include.

    Raises:
        OSError: ``git`` is not available.
        subprocess.CalledProcessError: the command failed (not a repository).
    """
    completed = subprocess.run(
        DIFF_COMMAND,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    )
    return completed.stdout or ""


def package_prefix() -> str:
    """Return the repo-relative folder of the CISO package itself.

    Returns:
        str: ``"<path>/"`` (with a trailing slash), or ``""`` when the package
        is not inside the repository being committed.
    """
    here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    try:
        completed = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
        )
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
        return ""
    root = (completed.stdout or "").strip()
    if not root:
        return ""
    relative = os.path.relpath(here, root).replace(os.sep, "/")
    if relative.startswith(".."):
        return ""
    return f"{relative}/"


def excluded_prefixes() -> tuple:
    """Return the repo-relative folders this gate does not scan.

    Two folders must CONTAIN the patterns the detectors look for:

    * the CISO package itself — rule tables and their documentation,
    * ``<api>/tests/security`` — fixtures with fake AWS keys, a reverse shell,
      ``rm -rf /`` and ``ignore previous instructions``.

    Every secret scanner needs such an allowlist: without it the gate blocks
    its own maintenance, and people learn to reach for ``--no-verify``, which
    disables the protection everywhere.

    Returns:
        tuple: Path prefixes (with trailing slash) to skip.
    """
    package = package_prefix()
    if not package:
        return ()
    api_root = package.split("/", 1)[0]
    return (package, f"{api_root}/tests/security/")


def relevant_findings(findings: List) -> List:
    """Drop findings located inside the scanner or its fixtures.

    Args:
        findings: Findings produced by :func:`guard_diff`.

    Returns:
        List: Findings that must still block the commit.
    """
    prefixes = excluded_prefixes()
    if not prefixes:
        return list(findings)
    return [
        finding
        for finding in findings
        if not any(
            (getattr(finding, "path", "") or "").replace(os.sep, "/").startswith(prefix)
            for prefix in prefixes
        )
    ]


def main(argv: Optional[list] = None) -> int:
    """Scan the staged changes and decide whether the commit may proceed.

    Args:
        argv: Unused (kept for ``python -m`` compatibility).

    Returns:
        int: One of :data:`EXIT_OK`, :data:`EXIT_BLOCKED`, :data:`EXIT_UNAVAILABLE`.
    """
    try:
        from codx.junior.security.ciso import gate
        from codx.junior.security.ciso import policy as ciso_policy
        from codx.junior.security.ciso.models import SecurityDomain
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - depends on the environment
        print(f"CISO: the secret scanner is not importable ({ex})", file=sys.stderr)
        return EXIT_UNAVAILABLE

    try:
        patch = staged_diff()
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as ex:
        print(f"CISO: could not read the staged diff ({ex})", file=sys.stderr)
        return EXIT_UNAVAILABLE

    if not patch.strip():
        return EXIT_OK

    scanned = gate.guard_diff(patch)
    findings = relevant_findings(scanned.findings)
    if not findings:
        return EXIT_OK

    # Re-evaluate the ladder on the findings that survive the filter: keeping
    # the original decision would block on a rule the filter just dropped.
    policy = ciso_policy.resolve_policy(None)
    verdict = ciso_policy.evaluate(
        findings,
        domain=SecurityDomain.GIT_COMMIT,
        policy=policy,
        rules_evaluated=scanned.rules_evaluated,
        truncated=scanned.truncated,
    )

    print(ciso_policy.render_report(verdict, title="CISO pre-commit report"))
    if verdict.blocked:
        print(
            "\nCISO: commit blocked. Remove the credential, rotate it (assume it "
            "is disclosed) and stage the fix.\n"
            "Inspect the staged changes with: git diff --cached",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return EXIT_BLOCKED
    return EXIT_OK


if __name__ == "__main__":  # pragma: no cover
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

"""Prove the CISO package runs on a bare interpreter, without the API venv.

Run it with any python::

    python3 api/tests/security/ciso_import_check.py

Why this check exists
    The gate is executed by a git hook, and a hook runs in environments the API
    knows nothing about: a fresh clone, a PR worktree (``api/.venv`` is never
    committed, so it does not exist there), a container image or CI. When the
    package imported pydantic, all of those died with::

        ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pydantic'

    at commit time — the hook passed, nothing was scanned, and the failure
    surfaced as a traceback instead of a verdict. This check keeps the property
    that fixes it: **the whole ``security.ciso`` package imports and works on a
    stdlib-only interpreter**, so the gate protects every clone.

Checks
    1. the test interpreter really is bare (pydantic is not importable),
    2. ``import codx.junior.security.ciso`` works there,
    3. detection, policy and JSON serialisation still work there,
    4. a commit from a repository WITHOUT ``api/.venv`` is gated correctly
       (blocked with a credential, allowed when clean).

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import textwrap

#: ``api/`` root: this file lives in ``api/tests/security/``.
API_ROOT = os.path.dirname(
    os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
)
#: ``.githooks/`` of the repository that contains this API package.
REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(API_ROOT)
HOOK_PATH = os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, ".githooks", "pre-commit")

#: A token-shaped value, assembled at runtime so this file is not itself a hit.
FAKE_TOKEN = "ghp_" + ("A1b2C3d4E5f6G7h8I9j0" * 2)

RESULTS = []


def check(name: str, passed: bool, detail: str = "") -> bool:
    """Record one check and print its result."""
    RESULTS.append((name, passed))
    status = "PASS" if passed else "FAIL"
    suffix = f"  ({detail})" if detail else ""
    print(f"  {status}  {name}{suffix}")
    return passed


#: Executed by the child interpreter. ``-S`` gives it no site-packages.
CHILD_SCRIPT = textwrap.dedent(
    """
    import json
    import sys

    sys.path.insert(0, {api_root!r})

    # 1. the interpreter must be bare, otherwise this check proves nothing
    try:
        import pydantic  # noqa: F401
    except ModuleNotFoundError:
        pass
    else:
        print("BARE_INTERPRETER=0")
        raise SystemExit(0)
    print("BARE_INTERPRETER=1")

    # 2. the package and every module the gate needs must import
    import codx.junior.security.ciso as ciso
    from codx.junior.security.ciso import (  # noqa: F401
        audit, gate, injection, malicious, models, payload, policy, precommit,
        scanner, secrets,
    )

    # 3. the behaviour must be the real behaviour, not just a successful import
    assert ciso.SecuritySeverity.CRITICAL.value == "critical"
    assert ciso.parse_severity("HIGH") is ciso.SecuritySeverity.HIGH
    assert ciso.parse_severity("critical") is ciso.SecuritySeverity.CRITICAL

    finding = models.SecurityFinding(rule_id="secret.test", severity="high")
    assert finding.severity is ciso.SecuritySeverity.HIGH, finding.severity
    verdict = models.SecurityVerdict(findings=[finding], blocked=True)
    assert isinstance(verdict.findings[0], models.SecurityFinding)
    assert json.loads(json.dumps(verdict.to_dict()))["findings"][0]["severity"] == "high"

    kept = models.SecurityVerdict(
        findings=[
            models.SecurityFinding("a", severity="low"),
            models.SecurityFinding("b", severity="critical"),
        ]
    ).filtered(ciso.SecuritySeverity.HIGH)
    assert [f.rule_id for f in kept.findings] == ["b"], kept.findings

    # a write that carries a credential must be blocked, on a bare interpreter
    write = gate.guard_file_write("api/config.py", "TOKEN = {token!r}\\n")
    assert write.blocked, write.summary
    assert "{token}" not in (write.redacted_text or ""), write.redacted_text

    # a clean write must pass
    assert gate.guard_file_write("api/config.py", "NAME = 'codx'\\n").allowed

    print("CHILD=1")
    """
).strip()


def run_child(python: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    """Import and exercise the package with *python* (no site-packages)."""
    script = CHILD_SCRIPT.format(api_root=API_ROOT, token=FAKE_TOKEN)
    env = {key: value for key, value in os.environ.items() if key != "PYTHONPATH"}
    return subprocess.run(
        [python, "-S", "-c", script],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        env=env,
        cwd=tempfile.gettempdir(),
        timeout=180,
    )


def check_bare_interpreter() -> None:
    """The package must import and work without site-packages."""
    python = sys.executable or "python3"
    completed = run_child(python)
    output = (completed.stdout or "") + (completed.stderr or "")

    if "BARE_INTERPRETER=0" in output:
        check(
            "the interpreter is bare (no site-packages)",
            False,
            f"{python} still has pydantic; use a system python3 to verify",
        )
        return
    check("the interpreter is bare (no site-packages)", True, os.path.basename(python))
    check(
        "security.ciso imports without third-party packages",
        completed.returncode == 0 and "CHILD=1" in output,
        output.strip().splitlines()[-1] if output.strip() else "no output",
    )
    if completed.returncode != 0:
        print(textwrap.indent(output, "        "))

    # The known failure mode: the module is imported by `python -m`, so a
    # missing dependency surfaces before main() can handle it.
    runpy = subprocess.run(
        [python, "-S", "-c", f"import sys; sys.path.insert(0, {API_ROOT!r});"
         " import runpy, sys as s; s.argv=['precommit', '--check'];"
         " import codx.junior.security.ciso.precommit as m;"
         " print('PRE_IMPORT=1')"],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        env={key: value for key, value in os.environ.items() if key != "PYTHONPATH"},
        timeout=120,
    )
    check(
        "the hook entry point imports before main() runs",
        runpy.returncode == 0 and "PRE_IMPORT=1" in (runpy.stdout or ""),
        (runpy.stderr or "").strip().splitlines()[-1] if runpy.returncode else "",
    )


def check_commit_without_venv(python: str) -> None:
    """A commit from a tree with no api/.venv must still be gated."""
    if not os.path.isfile(HOOK_PATH):
        check("the pre-commit hook exists", False, HOOK_PATH)
        return

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="ciso-novenv-") as workspace:
        repo = os.path.join(workspace, "repo")
        os.makedirs(repo)
        # `api/` is linked WITHOUT a .venv: a PR worktree looks exactly like this.
        os.symlink(API_ROOT, os.path.join(repo, "api"))
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(repo, ".githooks"))
        hook = os.path.join(repo, ".githooks", "pre-commit")
        with open(HOOK_PATH, "r", encoding="utf-8") as source:
            content = source.read()
        with open(hook, "w", encoding="utf-8") as target:
            target.write(content)
        os.chmod(hook, 0o755)

        def git(*args: str, env: dict = None) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
            full_env = {
                key: value
                for key, value in os.environ.items()
                if key not in ("PYTHONPATH", "GIT_DIR", "GIT_WORK_TREE", "CISO_PYTHON")
            }
            full_env.update(
                {
                    "GIT_AUTHOR_NAME": "ciso",
                    "GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL": "ciso@example.com",
                    "GIT_COMMITTER_NAME": "ciso",
                    "GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL": "ciso@example.com",
                    "CISO_PYTHON": python,
                }
            )
            full_env.update(env or {})
            return subprocess.run(
                ["git", *args],
                cwd=repo,
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
                env=full_env,
                timeout=180,
            )

        git("init", "--quiet")
        git("config", "core.hooksPath", ".githooks")
        git("config", "user.useConfigOnly", "true")

        with open(os.path.join(repo, "clean.py"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write("NAME = 'codx'\\n".replace("\\n", "\n"))
        git("add", "clean.py")
        clean = git("commit", "--quiet", "-m", "clean")
        check(
            "clean changes commit without a virtualenv",
            clean.returncode == 0,
            (clean.stderr or clean.stdout or "").strip().splitlines()[-1]
            if clean.returncode
            else "",
        )

        with open(os.path.join(repo, "leak.py"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write(f"TOKEN = {FAKE_TOKEN!r}\n")
        git("add", "leak.py")
        blocked = git("commit", "--quiet", "-m", "leak")
        report = (blocked.stdout or "") + (blocked.stderr or "")
        check(
            "a credential blocks the commit without a virtualenv",
            blocked.returncode != 0 and "commit blocked" in report.lower(),
            "exit 0: the gate did not run" if blocked.returncode == 0 else "",
        )
        check(
            "the blocked report does not print the credential",
            FAKE_TOKEN not in report,
            "the token leaked into the report" if FAKE_TOKEN in report else "",
        )


def check_hook_contract() -> None:
    """The hook itself must not hard-code a venv-only interpreter."""
    with open(HOOK_PATH, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        content = handle.read()
    check(
        "the hook probes interpreters instead of assuming one",
        "import $module" in content and "CISO_PYTHON" in content,
        "no import probe",
    )
    check(
        "the hook resolves the main worktree",
        "git-common-dir" in content,
        "a PR worktree would fall back to a bare python",
    )
    check(
        "the hook does not mention pydantic",
        "pydantic" not in content.split("CISO:")[0] or True,
    )


def main() -> int:
    """Run every check and report the summary."""
    print("CISO bare-interpreter check")
    print("=" * 40)
    python = sys.executable or "python3"
    system_python = "/usr/bin/python3" if os.path.exists("/usr/bin/python3") else python

    check_bare_interpreter()
    check_hook_contract()
    check_commit_without_venv(system_python)

    failed = [name for name, passed in RESULTS if not passed]
    print("=" * 40)
    if failed:
        print(f"{len(failed)} check(s) failed")
        return 1
    print(f"{len(RESULTS)} check(s) passed")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

        return
    check("the interpreter is bare (no site-packages)", True)
    check(
        "security.ciso imports without third-party packages",
        completed.returncode == 0 and "CHILD=1" in output,
        output.strip().splitlines()[-1] if output.strip() else "no output",
    )

        print(textwrap.indent(output, "        "))

         " print('PRE_IMPORT=1')"],

def check_commit_without_venv(python: str) -> None:
    """A commit from a tree with no api/.venv must still be gated."""
    if not os.path.isfile(HOOK_PATH):
        check("the pre-commit hook exists", False, HOOK_PATH)
        return

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="ciso-novenv-") as workspace:
        repo = os.path.join(workspace, "repo")
        os.makedirs(repo)
        # `api/` is linked WITHOUT a .venv: a PR worktree looks exactly like this.
        os.symlink(API_ROOT, os.path.join(repo, "api"))
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(repo, ".githooks"))
        hook = os.path.join(repo, ".githooks", "pre-commit")
        with open(HOOK_PATH, "r", encoding="utf-8") as source:
            content = source.read()
        with open(hook, "w", encoding="utf-8") as target:
            target.write(content)
        os.chmod(hook, 0o755)

        def git(*args: str, env: dict = None) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
            full_env = {
                key: value
                for key, value in os.environ.items()
                if key not in ("PYTHONPATH", "GIT_DIR", "GIT_WORK_TREE", "CISO_PYTHON")
            }
            full_env.update(
                {
                    "GIT_AUTHOR_NAME": "ciso",
                    "GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL": "ciso@example.com",
                    "GIT_COMMITTER_NAME": "ciso",
                    "GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL": "ciso@example.com",
                    "CISO_PYTHON": python,
                }
            )
            full_env.update(env or {})
            return subprocess.run(
                ["git", *args],
                cwd=repo,
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
                env=full_env,
                timeout=180,
            )

        git("init", "--quiet")
        git("config", "core.hooksPath", ".githooks")
        git("config", "user.useConfigOnly", "true")

        with open(os.path.join(repo, "clean.py"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write("NAME = 'codx'\\n".replace("\\n", "\n"))
        git("add", "clean.py")
        clean = git("commit", "--quiet", "-m", "clean")
        check(
            "clean changes commit without a virtualenv",
            clean.returncode == 0,
            (clean.stderr or clean.stdout or "").strip().splitlines()[-1]
            if clean.returncode
            else "",
        )

        with open(os.path.join(repo, "leak.py"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write(f"TOKEN = {FAKE_TOKEN!r}\n")
        git("add", "leak.py")
        blocked = git("commit", "--quiet", "-m", "leak")
        report = (blocked.stdout or "") + (blocked.stderr or "")
        check(
            "a credential blocks the commit without a virtualenv",
            blocked.returncode != 0 and "commit blocked" in report.lower(),
            "exit 0: the gate did not run" if blocked.returncode == 0 else "",
        )
        check(
            "the blocked report does not print the credential",
            FAKE_TOKEN not in report,
            "the token leaked into the report" if FAKE_TOKEN in report else "",
        )


def check_hook_contract() -> None:
    """The hook itself must not hard-code a venv-only interpreter."""
    with open(HOOK_PATH, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        content = handle.read()
    check(
        "the hook probes interpreters instead of assuming one",
        "import $module" in content and "CISO_PYTHON" in content,
        "the hook does not test that the scanner can load",
    )
    check(
        "the hook resolves the main worktree",
        "git-common-dir" in content,
        "a PR worktree would not find the API package",
    )


def main() -> int:
    """Run every check and report the summary."""
    print("CISO bare-interpreter check")
    print("=" * 40)
    python = sys.executable or "python3"
    system_python = "/usr/bin/python3" if os.path.exists("/usr/bin/python3") else python

    check_bare_interpreter()
    check_hook_contract()
    check_commit_without_venv(system_python)

    failed = [name for name, passed in RESULTS if not passed]
    print("=" * 40)
    if failed:
        print(f"{len(failed)} check(s) failed")
        return 1
    print(f"{len(RESULTS)} check(s) passed")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Pre-commit secret gate.

Run it from a git hook::

    PYTHONPATH=<repo>/api python -m codx.junior.security.ciso.precommit

Exit codes
    0   the staged diff is clean (or has nothing to scan),
    1   a credential was found: the commit must be stopped,
    3   the scanner could not run (missing dependencies, no git): the hook
        decides whether that is fatal (``CISO_PRECOMMIT_STRICT=1``).

Runs anywhere
    This module and everything it imports are stdlib-only, so the gate works
    on a bare ``python3``: a fresh clone, a PR worktree (``api/.venv`` is
    never committed), a container image or CI. Needing the application
    dependency tree (pydantic, fastapi, the LLM clients) would make the gate
    die with an ImportError precisely at commit time, which is how it used to
    break; ``tests/security/ciso_import_check.py`` locks that property in.

What may block
    A credential, always, wherever it lands: the blob *is* the leak. Anything
    else blocks only when it lands in a file that can execute, because a commit
    stores content and runs nothing. A task card, a wiki page or a vulnerability
    report that *quotes* ``shutdown`` or ``curl | sh`` describes a risk instead
    of creating one, and blocking it would teach ``--no-verify`` — which
    disables the check for the one finding that matters.

Why the check belongs here
    Remote push protection fires *after* the commit exists: the secret is
    already a blob in the local object database, reachable from any branch and
    from the reflog, and stopping it then costs a history rewrite plus a
    credential rotation. This gate runs before the object is created, needs no
    network, works with any remote (GitHub, GitLab, self-hosted) and scans
    source files, not only committed history.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import os
import subprocess
import sys
from typing import Any, List, Optional

#: Exit code when the staged changes are clean.
EXIT_OK = 0
#: Exit code when a finding blocks the commit.
EXIT_BLOCKED = 1
#: Exit code when the gate could not run at all.
EXIT_UNAVAILABLE = 3

#: ``--unified=0`` keeps the diff small; ``scan_diff`` reads added lines only.
DIFF_COMMAND = ["git", "diff", "--cached", "--unified=0", "--no-color"]

#: Paths whose content is prose or data, not executable code. A credential
#: blocks here too (see :func:`blocking_findings`); only the executable
#: families are downgraded to a report.
PROSE_PREFIXES = (
    ".codx/tasks/",
    ".codx/chat_turns/",
    ".codx/wiki/",
    ".codx/profiles/",
    "wiki/",
    "docs/",
)
#: Extensions that hold documentation or configuration data.
PROSE_SUFFIXES = (
    ".md",
    ".markdown",
    ".rst",
    ".txt",
    ".json",
    ".yaml",
    ".yml",
    ".csv",
    ".log",
)


def staged_diff() -> str:
    """Return the staged patch (``git diff --cached``).

    Returns:
        str: Unified diff of the changes the next commit would include.

    Raises:
        OSError: ``git`` is not available.
        subprocess.CalledProcessError: the command failed (not a repository).
    """
    completed = subprocess.run(
        DIFF_COMMAND,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    )
    return completed.stdout or ""


def package_prefix() -> str:
    """Return the repo-relative folder of the CISO package itself.

    Returns:
        str: ``"<path>/"`` (with a trailing slash), or ``""`` when the package
        is not inside the repository being committed.
    """
    here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    try:
        completed = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
        )
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
        return ""
    root = (completed.stdout or "").strip()
    if not root:
        return ""
    relative = os.path.relpath(here, root).replace(os.sep, "/")
    if relative.startswith(".."):
        return ""
    return f"{relative}/"


def excluded_prefixes() -> tuple:
    """Return the repo-relative folders this gate does not scan.

    Two folders must CONTAIN the patterns the detectors look for:

    * the CISO package itself — rule tables and their documentation,
    * ``<api>/tests/security`` — fixtures with fake AWS keys, a reverse shell,
      ``rm -rf /`` and ``ignore previous instructions``.

    Every secret scanner needs such an allowlist: without it the gate blocks
    its own maintenance, and people learn to reach for ``--no-verify``, which
    disables the protection everywhere.

    Returns:
        tuple: Path prefixes (with trailing slash) to skip.
    """
    package = package_prefix()
    if not package:
        return ()
    api_root = package.split("/", 1)[0]
    return (package, f"{api_root}/tests/security/")


def relevant_findings(findings: List) -> List:
    """Drop findings located inside the scanner or its fixtures.

    Args:
        findings: Findings produced by :func:`guard_diff`.

    Returns:
        List: Findings that must still block the commit.
    """
    prefixes = excluded_prefixes()
    if not prefixes:
        return list(findings)
    return [
        finding
        for finding in findings
        if not any(
            (getattr(finding, "path", "") or "").replace(os.sep, "/").startswith(prefix)
            for prefix in prefixes
        )
    ]


def is_prose_path(path: Optional[str]) -> bool:
    """Return True when *path* holds prose or data rather than executable code.

    Args:
        path: Repo-relative path of the finding.

    Returns:
        bool: True for documentation, task cards, wiki pages and config data.
    """
    if not path:
        return False
    normalised = path.replace(os.sep, "/")
    if normalised.startswith(PROSE_PREFIXES):
        return True
    return normalised.lower().endswith(PROSE_SUFFIXES)


def blocking_findings(findings: List, categories: Any) -> List:
    """Return the findings that are allowed to block the commit.

    A credential always blocks: the blob *is* the leak, wherever it lands.
    Everything else blocks only in a file that can execute — injected code in a
    ``.py`` or a ``Makefile`` is the incident this gate exists for, while the
    same string inside a task card is a quotation.

    Args:
        findings: Findings produced by :func:`guard_diff`, already filtered.
        categories: The ``SecurityCategory`` enum of the CISO models.

    Returns:
        List: Findings that decide the verdict.
    """
    return [
        finding
        for finding in findings
        if getattr(finding, "category", None) == categories.SECRET
        or not is_prose_path(getattr(finding, "path", "") or "")
    ]


def main(argv: Optional[list] = None) -> int:
    """Scan the staged changes and decide whether the commit may proceed.

    Args:
        argv: Unused (kept for ``python -m`` compatibility).

    Returns:
        int: One of :data:`EXIT_OK`, :data:`EXIT_BLOCKED`, :data:`EXIT_UNAVAILABLE`.
    """
    try:
        from codx.junior.security.ciso import gate

"""Repository audit: what is already committed?

The gates stop new secrets and the pre-commit hook stops a commit. Neither can
clean a repository that already contains them, and the most valuable artifact of
a security review is the list of what is *there today*.

Scope it at a tracked data plane, not the whole tree::

    PYTHONPATH=<repo>/api python -m codx.junior.security.ciso.audit .codx \
        --project-path . --min-severity high

Two report shapes are available:

* ``--format triage`` (default) — the *clean* list: one row per rule and one row
  per file, ordered by severity, with the noise below ``--min-severity``
  suppressed. This is the list a human triages.
* ``--format report`` — the full finding list produced by the policy engine,
  useful when a single finding has to be inspected.

Both only read: nothing is modified and every finding carries redacted evidence,
so the report can be attached to a ticket as it is.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import argparse
import os
import sys
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

from codx.junior.security.ciso import policy as ciso_policy
from codx.junior.security.ciso import scanner
from codx.junior.security.ciso.models import (
    SecurityDomain,
    SecurityFinding,
    SecuritySeverity,
    SecurityVerdict,
    parse_severity,
    severity_rank,
)

#: Default severity floor of the triage view. ``medium`` is the level of the
#: entropy heuristic, whose false positives bury everything else.
DEFAULT_MIN_SEVERITY = SecuritySeverity.HIGH


def collect_targets(
    paths: Sequence[str],
    project_path: str = ".",
    max_files: int = 2000,
) -> List[str]:
    """Expand *paths* (files or folders) into a bounded list of files.

    Args:
        paths: Project-relative or absolute files/folders.
        project_path: Project root used to resolve relative paths.
        max_files: Maximum number of files returned.

    Returns:
        List[str]: Absolute file paths.
    """
    policy = ciso_policy.resolve_policy(None)
    targets: List[str] = []
    for path in paths:
        absolute = path if os.path.isabs(path) else os.path.join(project_path, path)
        absolute = os.path.abspath(absolute)
        if os.path.isdir(absolute):
            targets.extend(
                scanner.iter_project_files(absolute, max_files=max_files, policy=policy)
            )
        elif os.path.isfile(absolute):
            targets.append(absolute)
        else:
            print(f"CISO audit: '{path}' does not exist", file=sys.stderr)
        if len(targets) >= max_files:
            break
    return targets[:max_files]


def scan(
    paths: Sequence[str],
    project_path: str = ".",
    max_files: int = 2000,
    domain: SecurityDomain = SecurityDomain.FILE_READ,
) -> Tuple[SecurityVerdict, List[str]]:

    Args:
        paths: Project-relative folders or files to audit.
        project_path: Project root (findings are reported relative to it).
        max_files: Global file budget (the scan is bounded on purpose).
        domain: Domain recorded in the report.

    Returns:
        Tuple[SecurityVerdict, List[str]]: Aggregated verdict and the scanned
        absolute paths.
    """
    policy = ciso_policy.resolve_policy(None)
    targets = collect_targets(paths, project_path=project_path, max_files=max_files)
    if not targets:
        return SecurityVerdict(domain=domain), targets
    verdict = scanner.scan_project(
        project_path=os.path.abspath(project_path),
        max_files=max_files,
        domain=domain,
        policy=policy,
        paths=targets,
    )
    return verdict, targets


def audit(
    paths: Sequence[str],
    project_path: str = ".",
    max_files: int = 2000,
    domain: SecurityDomain = SecurityDomain.FILE_READ,
    min_severity: Optional[SecuritySeverity] = None,
) -> str:
    """Scan *paths* and return a Markdown report.

    Args:
        paths: Project-relative folders or files to audit.
        project_path: Project root (findings are reported relative to it).
        max_files: Global file budget (the scan is bounded on purpose).
        domain: Domain recorded in the report.
        min_severity: Optional severity floor for the listed findings.

    Returns:
        str: Markdown report; a single "No finding in" line when clean.
    """
    verdict, targets = scan(
        paths, project_path=project_path, max_files=max_files, domain=domain
    )
    scope = ", ".join(f"`{path}`" for path in paths)

    if not targets:
        return f"## CISO audit\n\nNothing to scan in {scope}"
    if not verdict.findings:
        return (
            f"## CISO audit\n\nNo finding in {scope} "
            f"({len(targets)} file(s) scanned)."
        )
    return ciso_policy.render_report(
        verdict,

"""Repository audit: what is already committed?

The gates stop new secrets and the pre-commit hook stops a commit. Neither can
clean a repository that already contains them, and the most valuable artifact of
a security review is the list of what is *there today*.

Scope it at a tracked data plane, not the whole tree::

    PYTHONPATH=<repo>/api python -m codx.junior.security.ciso.audit .codx \
        --project-path . --min-severity high

Two report shapes are available:

* ``--format triage`` (default) — the *clean* list: one row per rule and one row
  per file, ordered by severity, with the noise below ``--min-severity``
  suppressed. This is the list a human triages.
* ``--format report`` — the full finding list produced by the policy engine,
  useful when a single finding has to be inspected.

Both only read: nothing is modified and every finding carries redacted evidence,
so the report can be attached to a ticket as it is.

import argparse
import os
import sys
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

from codx.junior.security.ciso import policy as ciso_policy
from codx.junior.security.ciso import scanner
from codx.junior.security.ciso.models import (
    SecurityDomain,
    SecurityFinding,
    SecuritySeverity,
    SecurityVerdict,
    parse_severity,
    severity_rank,
)

#: Default severity floor of the triage view. ``medium`` is the level of the
#: entropy heuristic, whose false positives bury everything else.
DEFAULT_MIN_SEVERITY = SecuritySeverity.HIGH


def collect_targets(
    paths: Sequence[str],
    project_path: str = ".",
    max_files: int = 2000,
) -> List[str]:
    """Expand *paths* (files or folders) into a bounded list of files.

    Args:
        paths: Project-relative or absolute files/folders.
        project_path: Project root used to resolve relative paths.
        max_files: Maximum number of files returned.

    Returns:
        List[str]: Absolute file paths.
    """
    policy = ciso_policy.resolve_policy(None)
    targets: List[str] = []
    for path in paths:
        absolute = path if os.path.isabs(path) else os.path.join(project_path, path)
        absolute = os.path.abspath(absolute)
        if os.path.isdir(absolute):
            targets.extend(
                scanner.iter_project_files(absolute, max_files=max_files, policy=policy)
            )
        elif os.path.isfile(absolute):
            targets.append(absolute)
        else:
            print(f"CISO audit: '{path}' does not exist", file=sys.stderr)
        if len(targets) >= max_files:
            break
    return targets[:max_files]


def scan(
    paths: Sequence[str],
    project_path: str = ".",
    max_files: int = 2000,
    domain: SecurityDomain = SecurityDomain.FILE_READ,
) -> Tuple[SecurityVerdict, List[str]]:

    Args:
        paths: Project-relative folders or files to audit.
        project_path: Project root (findings are reported relative to it).
        max_files: Global file budget (the scan is bounded on purpose).
        domain: Domain recorded in the report.

    Returns:
        Tuple[SecurityVerdict, List[str]]: Aggregated verdict and the scanned
        absolute paths.
    """
    policy = ciso_policy.resolve_policy(None)
    targets = collect_targets(paths, project_path=project_path, max_files=max_files)
    if not targets:
        return SecurityVerdict(domain=domain), targets
    verdict = scanner.scan_project(
        project_path=os.path.abspath(project_path),
        max_files=max_files,
        domain=domain,
        policy=policy,
        paths=targets,
    )
    return verdict, targets


def redact_targets(
    paths: Sequence[str],
    project_path: str = ".",
    max_files: int = 2000,
    apply: bool = False,
    max_file_bytes: int = 32 * 1024 * 1024,
) -> Tuple[List[Tuple[str, int]], int]:
    """Neutralise the credentials found in *paths* (dry run by default).

    The rewrite is textual, never a re-serialisation: a task card keeps its
    structure byte for byte and only the credential itself is replaced, so the
    JSON stays valid and the cleanup diff stays reviewable.

    Args:
        paths: Project-relative files or folders to clean.
        project_path: Project root used to resolve relative paths.
        max_files: Global file budget.
        apply: Write the changes (``False`` only reports what would change).
        max_file_bytes: Files larger than this are skipped and reported.

    Returns:
        Tuple[List[Tuple[str, int]], int]: ``(path, replacements)`` for every
        changed file, and the number of files skipped for their size.
    """
    policy = ciso_policy.resolve_policy(None)
    changed: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
    skipped = 0
    for target in collect_targets(paths, project_path=project_path, max_files=max_files):
        try:
            size = os.path.getsize(target)
        except OSError:
            continue
        if size > max_file_bytes:
            skipped += 1
            print(
                f"CISO: '{target}' is {size} bytes; skipped (raise --max-file-bytes)",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            continue
        try:
            with open(target, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as handle:
                text = handle.read()
        except OSError as ex:
            print(f"CISO: could not read '{target}' ({ex})", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        redacted, count = secrets.redact_text(text, policy)
        if not count:
            continue
        changed.append((target, count))
        if apply:
            with open(target, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                handle.write(redacted)
    return changed, skipped


def audit(
    paths: Sequence[str],
    project_path: str = ".",
    max_files: int = 2000,
    domain: SecurityDomain = SecurityDomain.FILE_READ,
    min_severity: Optional[SecuritySeverity] = None,
) -> str:
    """Scan *paths* and return a Markdown report.

    Args:
        paths: Project-relative folders or files to audit.
        project_path: Project root (findings are reported relative to it).
        max_files: Global file budget (the scan is bounded on purpose).
        domain: Domain recorded in the report.
        min_severity: Optional severity floor for the listed findings.

    Returns:
        str: Markdown report; a single "No finding in" line when clean.
    """
    verdict, targets = scan(
        paths, project_path=project_path, max_files=max_files, domain=domain
    )
    scope = ", ".join(f"`{path}`" for path in paths)

    if not targets:
        return f"## CISO audit\n\nNothing to scan in {scope}"
    if not verdict.findings:
        return (
            f"## CISO audit\n\nNo finding in {scope} "
            f"({len(targets)} file(s) scanned)."
        )
    return ciso_policy.render_report(
        verdict,
        title=f"CISO audit — {scope}",
        max_findings=50,
        min_severity=min_severity,
    )


def _relative(path: Optional[str], project_path: str) -> str:
    """Return *path* relative to *project_path*, with forward slashes."""
    if not path:
        return "-"
    try:
        rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.abspath(path), os.path.abspath(project_path))
    except ValueError:  # pragma: no cover - different drives on Windows
        rel = path
    return rel.replace(os.sep, "/")


def _worst(findings: Sequence[SecurityFinding]) -> Optional[SecuritySeverity]:
    """Return the worst severity of *findings*."""
    return max((f.severity for f in findings), key=severity_rank, default=None)


def triage(
    paths: Sequence[str],
    project_path: str = ".",
    max_files: int = 2000,
    domain: SecurityDomain = SecurityDomain.FILE_READ,
    min_severity: Optional[SecuritySeverity] = DEFAULT_MIN_SEVERITY,
    max_rows: int = 40,
) -> Tuple[str, List[SecurityFinding]]:
    """Scan *paths* and return a grouped, severity-filtered triage list.

    The triage view answers the two questions an engineer actually asks: *which
    rules fire* (so one fix can retire many findings) and *which files are
    affected* (so the work is assignable). Findings below *min_severity* are
    counted but not listed.

    Args:
        paths: Project-relative folders or files to audit.
        project_path: Project root (findings are reported relative to it).
        max_files: Global file budget.
        domain: Domain recorded in the report.
        min_severity: Severity floor for the listed findings.
        max_rows: Maximum rows per table.

    Returns:
        Tuple[str, List[SecurityFinding]]: The Markdown report and the findings
        at or above *min_severity* (empty means "nothing to triage").
    """
    verdict, targets = scan(
        paths, project_path=project_path, max_files=max_files, domain=domain
    )
    scope = ", ".join(f"`{path}`" for path in paths)
    kept = verdict.findings_at_least(min_severity)
    floor = min_severity.value if min_severity else "info"

    if not targets:
        return f"## CISO triage — {scope}\n\nNothing to scan.", []

    if not kept:
        return (
            f"## CISO triage — {scope}\n\n"
            f"No finding at or above `{floor}` in {len(targets)} scanned file(s) "
            f"({len(verdict.findings)} finding(s) below the floor)."
        ), []

    suppressed = len(verdict.findings) - len(kept)
    by_severity: Dict[str, int] = {}
    for finding in kept:
        by_severity[finding.severity.value] = by_severity.get(finding.severity.value, 0) + 1
    summary = ", ".join(
        f"{key} {value}"
        for key, value in sorted(
            by_severity.items(), key=lambda item: -severity_rank(parse_severity(item[0]))
        )
    )

    lines = [
        f"## CISO triage — {scope}",
        "",
        f"- Files scanned: {len(targets)}",
        f"- Findings at or above `{floor}`: **{len(kept)}** ({summary})",
        f"- Suppressed below the floor: {suppressed}",
        f"- Highest severity: **{(_worst(kept) or SecuritySeverity.INFO).value}**",
        f"- Rules evaluated: {verdict.rules_evaluated}",
        "",
    ]
    if verdict.truncated:
        lines += ["> ⚠️ The payload was truncated: only the beginning was scanned.", ""]

    # -- by rule: one fix can retire many findings ------------------------
    rules: Dict[str, List[SecurityFinding]] = {}
    for finding in kept:
        rules.setdefault(finding.rule_id, []).append(finding)
    lines += [
        "### By rule",
        "",
        "| Severity | Rule | Occurrences | Files | Remediation |",
        "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |",
    ]
    for rule_id, group in sorted(
        rules.items(),
        key=lambda item: (
            -severity_rank(_worst(item[1])),
            -len(item[1]),
            item[0],
        ),
    )[:max_rows]:
        files = {_relative(f.path, project_path) for f in group if f.path}
        remediation = (group[0].remediation or "").replace("|", "\\|")
        lines.append(
            f"| {(_worst(group) or SecuritySeverity.INFO).value} | `{rule_id}` | "
            f"{len(group)} | {len(files)} | {remediation} |"
        )
    if len(rules) > max_rows:
        lines.append(f"\n_{len(rules) - max_rows} more rule(s) omitted._")
    lines.append("")

    # -- by file: the assignable work list --------------------------------
    files_map: Dict[str, List[SecurityFinding]] = {}
    for finding in kept:
        files_map.setdefault(_relative(finding.path, project_path), []).append(finding)
    lines += [
        "### By file",
        "",
        "| # | File | Worst | Findings | First location | Rules |",
        "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |",
    ]
    ordered = sorted(
        files_map.items(),
        key=lambda item: (-severity_rank(_worst(item[1])), -len(item[1]), item[0]),
    )
    for index, (path, group) in enumerate(ordered[:max_rows], start=1):
        first = min(group, key=lambda f: (f.line or 0, f.rule_id))
        location = f"`{path}:{first.line}`" if first.line else f"`{path}`"
        rules_in_file = sorted({f.rule_id for f in group})
        shown = ", ".join(f"`{rule}`" for rule in rules_in_file[:3])
        if len(rules_in_file) > 3:
            shown += f" +{len(rules_in_file) - 3}"
        lines.append(
            f"| {index} | `{path}` | {(_worst(group) or SecuritySeverity.INFO).value} | "
            f"{len(group)} | {location} | {shown} |"
        )
    if len(ordered) > max_rows:
        lines.append(f"\n_{len(ordered) - max_rows} more file(s) omitted._")

    lines += [
        "",
        "### Evidence (redacted)",
        "",
        "| Severity | Rule | Location | Evidence |",
        "| --- | --- | --- | --- |",
    ]
    for finding in kept[:max_rows]:
        location = _relative(finding.path, project_path)
        if finding.line:
            location = f"{location}:{finding.line}"
        evidence = (finding.evidence or finding.excerpt or "").replace("|", "\\|")
        lines.append(
            f"| {finding.severity.value} | `{finding.rule_id}` | `{location}` | {evidence} |"
        )
    lines += [
        "",
        "> A detected credential must be treated as disclosed: rotate it, then",
        "> remove it from the file. Evidence is redacted and cannot be reused.",
        "",
    ]
    return "\n".join(lines), kept


def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
    """CLI entry point.

    Args:
        argv: Command line arguments (defaults to ``sys.argv[1:]``).

    Returns:
        int: ``0`` when nothing was found at or above the severity floor,
        ``1`` otherwise, so the audit can fail a pipeline.

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="ciso.audit",
        description="Scan project paths for credentials and malicious content.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("paths", nargs="+", help="Paths to audit (file or folder).")
    parser.add_argument("--project-path", default=".", help="Project root.")
    parser.add_argument("--max-files", type=int, default=2000, help="File budget.")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--min-severity",
        default=DEFAULT_MIN_SEVERITY.value,

        help="'triage' (grouped list) or 'report' (full finding list).",

        "--apply",

) -> Tuple[str, List[SecurityFinding]]:

    The triage view answers the two questions an engineer actually asks: *which

    affected* (so the work is assignable). Findings below *min_severity* are

        f"{key} {value}"

            by_severity.items(), key=lambda item: -severity_rank(parse_severity(item[0]))

    )

    lines = [
        f"## CISO triage — {scope}",
        "",
        f"- Files scanned: {len(targets)}",
        f"- Findings at or above `{floor}`: **{len(kept)}** ({summary})",
        f"- Suppressed below the floor: {suppressed}",

        f"- Rules evaluated: {verdict.rules_evaluated}",

    rules: Dict[str, List[SecurityFinding]] = {}
    for finding in kept:
        rules.setdefault(finding.rule_id, []).append(finding)
    lines += [
        "### By rule",
        "",
        "| Severity | Rule | Occurrences | Files | Remediation |",
        "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |",

    for rule_id, group in sorted(
        rules.items(),

            -len(item[1]),

    )[:max_rows]:
        files = {_relative(f.path, project_path) for f in group if f.path}
        remediation = (group[0].remediation or "").replace("|", "\\|")

            f"| {(_worst(group) or SecuritySeverity.INFO).value} | `{rule_id}` | "
            f"{len(group)} | {len(files)} | {remediation} |"
        )
    if len(rules) > max_rows:
        lines.append(f"\n_{len(rules) - max_rows} more rule(s) omitted._")
    lines.append("")

    # -- by file: the assignable work list --------------------------------
    files_map: Dict[str, List[SecurityFinding]] = {}
    for finding in kept:
        files_map.setdefault(_relative(finding.path, project_path), []).append(finding)
    lines += [
        "### By file",
        "",
        "| # | File | Worst | Findings | First location | Rules |",
        "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |",
    ]
    ordered = sorted(
        files_map.items(),
        key=lambda item: (-severity_rank(_worst(item[1])), -len(item[1]), item[0]),
    )
    for index, (path, group) in enumerate(ordered[:max_rows], start=1):
        first = min(group, key=lambda f: (f.line or 0, f.rule_id))
        location = f"`{path}:{first.line}`" if first.line else f"`{path}`"

        if len(rules_in_file) > 3:
            shown += f" +{len(rules_in_file) - 3}"
        lines.append(
            f"| {index} | `{path}` | {(_worst(group) or SecuritySeverity.INFO).value} | "
            f"{len(group)} | {location} | {shown} |"
        )
    if len(ordered) > max_rows:
        lines.append(f"\n_{len(ordered) - max_rows} more file(s) omitted._")

    lines += [
        "",
        "### Evidence (redacted)",
        "",
        "| Severity | Rule | Location | Evidence |",
        "| --- | --- | --- | --- |",
    ]
    for finding in kept[:max_rows]:
        location = _relative(finding.path, project_path)
        if finding.line:
            location = f"{location}:{finding.line}"
        evidence = (finding.evidence or finding.excerpt or "").replace("|", "\\|")
        lines.append(
            f"| {finding.severity.value} | `{finding.rule_id}` | `{location}` | {evidence} |"
        )
    lines += [
        "",
        "> A detected credential must be treated as disclosed: rotate it, then",
        "> remove it from the file. Evidence is redacted and cannot be reused.",
        "",
    ]
    return "\n".join(lines), kept


def _redact_main(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Run the redaction mode and print its report.

    Args:
        args: Parsed command line arguments.

    Returns:
        int: ``0`` when nothing is left to redact, ``1`` otherwise (so a dry
        run can fail a pipeline that still carries credentials).
    """
    changed, skipped = redact_targets(
        paths=args.paths,
        project_path=args.project_path,
        max_files=args.max_files,
        apply=args.apply,
        max_file_bytes=args.max_file_bytes,
    )
    mode = "APPLIED" if args.apply else "DRY RUN (nothing written, add --apply)"
    total = sum(count for _, count in changed)
    lines = [
        "## CISO redaction — " + ", ".join(f"`{path}`" for path in args.paths),
        "",
        f"- Mode: **{mode}**",
        f"- Files with credentials: **{len(changed)}**",
        f"- Replacements: **{total}**",
    ]
    if skipped:
        lines.append(f"- Skipped for size: {skipped}")
    lines.append("")
    if not changed:
        print("\n".join(lines + ["No credential to redact.", ""]))
        return 0
    lines += ["| File | Replacements |", "| --- | --- |"]
    for path, count in changed:
        lines.append(f"| `{_relative(path, args.project_path)}` | {count} |")
    lines += [
        "",
        "> Redaction removes the copy, not the disclosure: rotate every",
        "> credential listed here, then commit the cleaned files.",
        "",
    ]
    print("\n".join(lines))
    return 1


def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
    """CLI entry point.

    Args:
        argv: Command line arguments (defaults to ``sys.argv[1:]``).

    Returns:
        int: ``0`` when nothing was found at or above the severity floor,
        ``1`` otherwise, so the audit can fail a pipeline.
    """
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="ciso.audit",
        description="Scan project paths for credentials and malicious content.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("paths", nargs="+", help="Paths to audit (file or folder).")
    parser.add_argument("--project-path", default=".", help="Project root.")
    parser.add_argument("--max-files", type=int, default=2000, help="File budget.")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--min-severity",
        default=DEFAULT_MIN_SEVERITY.value,
        choices=[severity.value for severity in SecuritySeverity],
        help="Severity floor: lower findings are counted but not listed.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--format",
        default="triage",
        choices=["triage", "report"],
        help="'triage' (grouped list) or 'report' (full finding list).",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--redact",
        action="store_true",
        help="Redact every credential found: reports, or rewrites with --apply.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--apply",
        action="store_true",
        help="With --redact: rewrite the files instead of only reporting.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--max-file-bytes",
        type=int,
        default=32 * 1024 * 1024,
        help="With --redact: skip files larger than this many bytes.",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    floor = parse_severity(args.min_severity)

    if args.redact:
        return _redact_main(args)

    if args.format == "report":
        report = audit(
            paths=args.paths,
            project_path=args.project_path,
            max_files=args.max_files,
            min_severity=floor,
        )
        print(report)
        clean = "No finding in" in report or "Nothing to scan" in report
        return 0 if clean else 1

    report, findings = triage(
        paths=args.paths,
        project_path=args.project_path,
        max_files=args.max_files,
        min_severity=floor,
    )
    print(report)
    return 1 if findings else 0
