        The integrated docs UI only needs the markdown pages, but keeping the
        VitePress template means a project can still build a standalone static
        site. Existing files are never overwritten.

        Returns:
            Absolute path of the wiki folder.
        """
        os.makedirs(self.wiki_path, exist_ok=True)
        template = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "wiki_template")
        if os.path.isdir(template):
            for root, _dirs, files in os.walk(template):
                relative = os.path.relpath(root, template)
                target_dir = self.wiki_path if relative == "." else os.path.join(self.wiki_path, relative)
                os.makedirs(target_dir, exist_ok=True)
                for filename in files:
                    # index.md is generated from docs.json so it stays in sync.
                    if relative == "." and filename in ("index.md",):
                        continue
                    template_relative = (
                        filename if relative == "."
                        else os.path.join(relative, filename).replace(os.sep, "/")
                    )
                    source = os.path.join(root, filename)
                    target = os.path.join(target_dir, filename)
                    if (
                        not os.path.exists(target)
                        or template_relative in MANAGED_WIKI_TEMPLATE_FILES
                    ):
                        shutil.copy2(source, target)
        if not os.path.isfile(self.wiki_home_path):
            write_file(self.wiki_home_path, self._default_home_page())
        return self.wiki_path

    def _default_home_page(self) -> str:
        """Create a useful landing page without calling the AI."""
        project = self.settings.project_name or "Project"
        try:
            description = self.site_builder._project_description(project)
        except Exception:
            description = f"Documentation for {project}."
        _kind, languages = self.site_builder.project_kind()
        language_hint = f" Built with {', '.join(languages)}." if languages else ""
        header = yaml.safe_dump(
            {"title": project, "description": description, "tags": ["overview"]},
            sort_keys=False,
            allow_unicode=True,
        ).strip()
        return (
            f"---\n{header}\n---\n\n"
            f"# {project}\n\n"
            f"{description}\n\n"
            "> [!TIP]\n"
            "> This documentation is generated and kept up to date while the project "
            "changes. Use the navigation or ask the built-in assistant a question.\n\n"
            "## Start here\n\n"
            "- Browse the sections in the sidebar.\n"
            "- Use **Ask AI** for a guided answer with sources.\n"
            "- Every page is generated from the source code, so diagrams and examples "
            "reflect the current project.\n"
            f"{language_hint}\n"
        )

    # ── initial wiki creation (deterministic, no AI) ──────────────────────

    def build_default_tree(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Create a sensible category tree from the repository layout.

        ``create_wiki_tree`` is AI-powered and can be slow. This deterministic
        tree gives a new wiki an immediately navigable structure; the tree can
        be regenerated later from Wiki settings.
        """
        root = os.path.abspath(self.settings.abs_project_path or "")
        wiki_root = os.path.abspath(self.wiki_path)
        groups: Dict[str, List[str]] = {}
        for file_path in self.loader.list_repository_files() or []:
            absolute = os.path.abspath(file_path)
            if absolute.startswith(wiki_root):
                continue
            try:
                relative = os.path.relpath(absolute, root).replace(os.sep, "/")
            except ValueError:
                continue
            if relative.startswith("../") or relative.startswith("."):
                continue
            top = relative.split("/")[0] if "/" in relative else "project-overview"
            if top.startswith(".") or top in ("node_modules", "dist", "build", "coverage"):
                continue
            groups.setdefault(top, []).append(relative)

        if not groups:
            return self.load_wiki_settings()

        ordered = sorted(groups.items(), key=lambda item: (-len(item[1]), item[0]))
        selected = ordered[:8]
        overflow = [path for _group, files in ordered[8:] for path in files]

        categories = []
        for index, (group, files) in enumerate(selected):
            title = humanize(group)
            categories.append({
                "title": title,
                "description": f"Documentation for the {title} area of the project.",
                "icon": icon_for(title),
                "order": (index + 1) * 10,
                "keywords": [group],
                "children": [],
                "files": [
                    {"path": f"/{path}", "name": humanize(os.path.basename(path))}
                    for path in sorted(files)
                ],
            })
        if overflow:
            categories.append({
                "title": "Other",
                "description": "Remaining project files.",
                "icon": icon_for("other"),
                "order": 900,
                "keywords": [],
                "children": [],
                "files": [
                    {"path": f"/{path}", "name": humanize(os.path.basename(path))}
                    for path in sorted(overflow)
                ],
            })

        settings = self.load_wiki_settings()
        settings["categories"] = categories
        return self.save_wiki_settings(settings)

    def _write_category_overview(self, category: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
        """Write a deterministic category landing page (no AI call)."""
        title = str(category.get("title") or "Overview")
        description = str(category.get("description") or f"Documentation for {title}.")
        files = category.get("files", []) or []
        rows = []
        for file in files[:40]:
            path = str(file.get("path", "")).lstrip("/")
            rows.append(f"| `{path}` | {file.get('name') or humanize(path)} |")
        more = "" if len(files) <= 40 else f"\n_…and {len(files) - 40} more files._\n"
        body = (
            f"# {title}\n\n"
            f"> **TL;DR** — {description}\n\n"
            "> [!NOTE]\n"
            "> This overview was generated from the repository layout when the wiki was created. "
            "Detailed pages are generated in the background as files change.\n\n"
            "## What's inside\n\n"
            "| File | Area |\n| --- | --- |\n"
            + "\n".join(rows)
            + f"\n{more}\n"
            "## Suggested reading\n\n"
            "- Start with the files closest to the project entry point.\n"
            "- Ask the assistant for a guided tour of this area.\n"
        )
        header = yaml.safe_dump(
            {
                "title": f"{title} overview",
                "description": description[:300],
                "tags": ["overview", "generated"],
                "category": title,
            },
            sort_keys=False,
            allow_unicode=True,
        ).strip()
        page_path = path_join(self.wiki_path, category["path"], "overview.md")
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(page_path), exist_ok=True)
        write_file(page_path, f"---\n{header}\n---\n\n{body}")
        return page_path

    def _initial_page_files(self, categories: List[Dict[str, Any]], limit: int = 12) -> List[str]:
        """Pick a small, useful set of files for the first AI page batch."""
        candidates: List[str] = []
        preferred = ("readme", "main", "app", "index", "entrypoint", "dockerfile")
        for category in categories:
            for file in category.get("files", []) or []:
                path = str(file.get("path", "")).lstrip("/")
                if path:
                    candidates.append(path)
        def priority(path: str) -> tuple:
            name = os.path.basename(path).lower()
            return (
                0 if name.startswith("readme") else 1,
                0 if any(token in name for token in preferred) else 1,
                len(path),
            )
        seen = set()
        selected = []
        for path in sorted(candidates, key=priority):
            if path in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(path)
            selected.append(os.path.join(self.settings.abs_project_path, path))
            if len(selected) >= limit:
                break
        return selected

    def ensure_initial_wiki(self, queue_pages: bool = False) -> bool:
        """
        Make sure the project has a wiki, creating a lightweight one if needed.

        Returns True when a wiki was created. This is the automatic path used
        for every discovered project; it deliberately does not queue a large AI
        batch unless the caller asks for it.
        """
        try:
            existing = self.site_builder.load()
            if existing and existing.get("pages"):
                return False
        except Exception:
            pass
        if not self.settings.project_wiki:
            self.settings.project_wiki = True
            saved = self.settings.save_project()
            self.settings = saved
            self.wiki_path = saved.get_project_wiki_path()
            self.wiki_home_path = os.path.join(self.wiki_path, "home.md")
            self.site_builder = WikiSiteBuilder(settings=saved)
        self.is_wiki_active = True
        self.create_initial_wiki(queue_pages=queue_pages)
        return True

    def create_initial_wiki(self, queue_pages: bool = True) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Create a usable wiki without waiting for a large AI pipeline.

        * seeds the folder/home,
        * builds a deterministic category tree when none exists,
        * writes one overview page per category,
        * rebuilds the docs manifest,
        * queues a small first batch of detailed pages in the background.
        """
        self.is_wiki_active = True
        self.ensure_wiki_structure()
        settings = self.load_wiki_settings()
        if not settings.get("categories"):
            settings = self.build_default_tree()
        settings = self.load_wiki_settings()
        categories = self._get_all_categories(settings.get("categories", []))
        for category in categories:
            if category.get("files"):
                try:
                    self._write_category_overview(category)
                except Exception as ex:
                    logger.warning("Cannot write category overview for %s: %s", category.get("title"), ex)
        site = self.build_site()
        initial_files = self._initial_page_files(categories) if queue_pages else []
        if initial_files:
            from codx.junior.wiki.scheduler import schedule_wiki_update

            schedule_wiki_update(
                self.settings,
                files=initial_files,
                reason="create-wiki",
                debounce_seconds=1,
            )
        return site

    def create_config(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Initialise the wiki folder and return its settings."""
        self.ensure_wiki_structure()
        if not os.path.isfile(self.wiki_settings_path):
            write_file(
                self.wiki_settings_path,
                json.dumps(self._default_wiki_settings(), indent=2),
            )
        return self.load_wiki_settings()

    def build_site(self, write: bool = True) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Rebuild ``docs.json`` (navigation, landing page, child projects).

        This is cheap and AI-free; it is called after every page update and by
        the parent-project refresh path.
        """
        site = self.site_builder.build(
            wiki_settings=self.load_wiki_settings(),
            write=write,
        )
        return site

    def build_home(self) -> None:
        """Regenerate the landing/overview page and the site manifest."""
        self.ensure_wiki_structure()
        existing = self._read_file(self.wiki_home_path) or ""
        self.build_wiki_home(existing)
        self.build_site()

    def build_wiki(self) -> None:
        """Backward-compatible alias used by older API clients."""
        self.rebuild_wiki()

    def update_files(self, files: List[str], reason: str = "change") -> int:
        """
        Update the wiki pages for a batch of changed files.

        Called by the debounced background scheduler. Only the changed files
        are regenerated; the site manifest is rebuilt once for the whole batch.

        Args:
            files: Absolute paths of changed project files.
            reason: Why the update runs (``change``, ``refresh``, …).

        Returns:
            Number of pages successfully regenerated.
        """
        if not self.is_wiki_active:
            logger.debug("Wiki is not active, skipping batch update")
            return 0
        self.ensure_wiki_structure()
        unique_files = []
        seen = set()
        for file_path in files or []:
            if not file_path:
                continue
            absolute = os.path.abspath(file_path)
            if absolute in seen:
                continue
            if absolute.startswith(os.path.abspath(self.wiki_path)):
                continue
            if not os.path.isfile(absolute):
                continue
            seen.add(absolute)
            unique_files.append(absolute)

        built = 0
        for file_path in unique_files:
            try:
                document = self.create_wiki_document(
                    source=file_path,
                    update_wiki_conf=False,
                )
                if document:
                    built += 1
            except Exception as ex:
                logger.exception("Cannot update wiki page for %s: %s", file_path, ex)

        self._update_wiki_conf()
        self.event_manager.send_event("wiki_updated", {
            "project": self.settings.project_name,
            "reason": reason,
            "files": len(unique_files),
            "pages": built,
        })
        if unique_files:
            logger.info(
                "Wiki batch updated for %s: %d/%d page(s)",
                self.settings.project_name,
                built,
                len(unique_files),
            )
        return built

    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Wiki tree creation
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def create_wiki_tree(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Analyse the repository and ask the AI to build / refresh the category tree.
        The result is persisted via save_wiki_settings and also returned.
        """
        repository_files = self.loader.list_repository_files()
        ignore_patterns = [MKDOCS_YAML_FILE_NAME, self.wiki_path]

        def is_valid_file(file_path: str) -> bool:
            return not any(p in file_path for p in ignore_patterns)

        repository_files = [
            f.replace(self.settings.abs_project_path, '')
            for f in repository_files
            if is_valid_file(f)
        ]

        # Domain hints from dependency graph
        wiki_domains = WikiDomains(settings=self.settings, db=self.db, ai=self._get_ai())
        domain_map = wiki_domains.load_domain_map()
        domain_hints = ""
        if domain_map:
            domain_hints = "<domain_hints>\n"
            for d in domain_map:
                files_sample = ", ".join(d.get("files", [])[:10])
                domain_hints += f"  Domain '{d['name']}' contains: {files_sample}\n"
            domain_hints += "</domain_hints>\n"

        repository_files_str = "\n".join(sorted(repository_files))
        logger.info("Valid wiki files:\n%s", repository_files_str)

        wiki_settings = self.load_wiki_settings()
        user_language = wiki_settings.get("language", "English")
        user_instructions = wiki_settings.get("prompt", "")

        try:
            project_info = profile_text(
                self.profile_manager.read_profile("project"), self.settings
            )
        except Exception:
            project_info = ""

        project_kind, languages = self.site_builder.project_kind()
        try:
            summary_prompt = f"""
            <project_info>
            {project_info}
            </project_info>
            <project_kind>{project_kind}</project_kind>
            <languages>{', '.join(languages)}</languages>
            <project_files>
            {repository_files_str}
            </project_files>
            {domain_hints}
            <wiki_settings>
            {json.dumps(wiki_settings, indent=2)}
            </wiki_settings>
            <wiki_profile>
            {self._get_wiki_profile_text()}
            </wiki_profile>
            <wiki_profile_guard>
            {WIKI_PROFILE_GUARD}
            </wiki_profile_guard>
            <user_instructions>
            {user_instructions}
            </user_instructions>
            <user_language>
            {user_language}
            </user_language>

            Design the navigation of a modern documentation site for this project.
            Think like a senior engineer writing the docs a new teammate needs on day one:
            onboarding, architecture, guides, API/reference and operations.

            Return a wiki_settings JSON object with the updated "categories" tree and
            keep the existing top-level keys (language, mode, prompt, assistant).

            Category rules:
            - 5 to 8 top-level categories, each with a clear purpose.
            - Use children only when it genuinely helps (do not create one-child groups).
            - Every category has:
                * "title": unique, 2-4 words, sentence case, in {user_language}
                * "description": one or two sentences explaining what the reader learns
                * "icon": one Font Awesome class, e.g. "fa-solid fa-rocket"
                * "order": integer used to sort the sidebar (10, 20, 30…)
                * "keywords": list of keywords used to match files
                * "children": array of optional child categories
                * "files": list of WikiFile entries (mandatory)
            - WikiFile: {{"name": 2-4 word friendly title in {user_language}, "path": project-relative path}}.
            - Prefer a "Get started" category first, then "Guides", "Architecture",
              "API reference" (or equivalents for the project kind), then operations.
            - For non-code projects, use sections that make sense (e.g. Policies,
              Research, Processes) instead of forcing code structure.
            - Remove files that are no longer present; assign every project file to a category.

            Return ONLY the JSON object. Generated content must be in {user_language}.
            """
            messages = self._ai_chat(prompt=summary_prompt, clean=False)
            new_settings = next(extract_json_blocks(messages[-1].content))
            # Preserve top-level metadata (language, mode, prompt, assistant…)
            for key in ("language", "mode", "prompt", "assistant"):
                if key in wiki_settings and key not in new_settings:
                    new_settings[key] = wiki_settings[key]
            saved = self.save_wiki_settings(new_settings)
            self.build_site()
            return saved

        except Exception as ex:
            logger.exception("Error creating wiki tree: %s", ex)
            return {**wiki_settings, "error": str(ex)}

    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Document creation
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def create_wiki_document(self, source: str, update_wiki_conf: bool = True) -> Optional[Document]:
        """
        Generate (or refresh) the wiki page for a single source file.

        The generated page uses the modern documentation format: YAML
        frontmatter, a skimmable summary, Mermaid diagrams, runnable examples
        and callout hints. The AI is free to omit a section when it does not
        apply; the page is normalised afterwards so every page always has valid
        metadata and an H1.
        """
        if not self.is_wiki_active:
            logger.debug("Wiki is not active, skipping document creation for %s", source)
            return None

        if source and not os.path.isabs(source):
            source = os.path.join(self.settings.abs_project_path, source)
        source = os.path.abspath(source)

        # Validate source path to prevent malformed filenames
        if not self._is_valid_source_path(source):
            logger.warning("Invalid source path detected: %s", source)
            return None

        file_content = self._read_file(source)
        if not file_content:
            logger.warning("Empty or unreadable file, skipping: %s", source)
            return None

        self.ensure_wiki_structure()
        wiki_settings = self.load_wiki_settings()
        category = self._assign_category_to_file(source, wiki_settings)
        if not category:
            logger.warning(CATEGORY_NOT_FOUND_MESSAGE, source)
            return None

        title = category['title']
        keywords = category.get('keywords') or []
        project_name = self.settings.project_name
        wiki_path = category["path"]
        wiki_file_path = self._determine_wiki_file_path(category, source)

        # Validate wiki file path before attempting to read
        if not self._is_valid_wiki_file_path(wiki_file_path):
            logger.error("Invalid wiki file path generated: %s", wiki_file_path)
            return None

        current_wiki_content = ""
        if os.path.isfile(wiki_file_path):
            try:
                with open(wiki_file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as handle:
                    current_wiki_content = handle.read()
            except OSError as ex:
                logger.debug("Cannot read current wiki page %s: %s", wiki_file_path, ex)

        summary_prompt = self._prepare_summary_prompt(
            current_wiki_content, category, file_content,
            project_name, source, title, keywords, wiki_settings
        )

        messages = self._ai_chat(prompt=summary_prompt)
        page_content = self._normalize_generated_page(
            messages[-1].content,
            category=category,
            source=source,
            wiki_settings=wiki_settings,
        )

        # Append a related-pages / dependency section from the graph. This is
        # deterministic (no AI) and helps the reader jump to connected code.
        try:
            graph = DependencyGraph(settings=self.settings)
            if graph.load():
                deps = graph.get_file_deps(source)
                dep_section = self._build_dependency_section(deps, source)
                if dep_section:
                    page_content = f"{page_content.rstrip()}\n\n{dep_section}\n"
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.debug("Cannot append dependency section for %s: %s", source, ex)

        logger.info("Writing wiki document to %s", wiki_file_path)
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(wiki_file_path), exist_ok=True)
        write_file(wiki_file_path, page_content)

        metadata = {
            "keywords": keywords,
            "category": title,
            "source": source,
            "language": "md",
            "wiki_path": wiki_path,
            "page_path": os.path.splitext(os.path.relpath(wiki_file_path, self.wiki_path))[0].replace(os.sep, "/"),
            "updated_at": int(datetime.datetime.now().timestamp()),
        }

        if update_wiki_conf:
            self._update_wiki_conf()

        return Document(page_content, metadata=metadata)

    def _normalize_generated_page(
        self,
        content: str,
        category: Dict[str, Any],
        source: str,
        wiki_settings: Dict[str, Any],
    ) -> str:
        """
        Make an AI answer a valid, self-describing wiki page.

        * strips accidental outer code fences,
        * guarantees YAML frontmatter (title, description, tags, category, source),
        * guarantees an H1 heading,
        * keeps the body intact.
        """
        text = (content or "").strip()
        if text.startswith("```"):
            lines = text.splitlines()
            if len(lines) >= 2 and lines[-1].strip().startswith("```"):
                text = "\n".join(lines[1:-1]).strip()
        if not text:
            text = f"# {humanize(category.get('title') or source)}"

        frontmatter, body = parse_frontmatter(text)
        body = body.strip()
        title = str(
            frontmatter.get("title")
            or first_heading(body)
            or humanize(os.path.basename(source))
        )
        description = str(
            frontmatter.get("description")
            or first_paragraph(body)
            or f"Documentation for {os.path.relpath(source, self.settings.abs_project_path)}."
        )
        tags = frontmatter.get("tags") or frontmatter.get("keywords") or category.get("keywords") or []
        if isinstance(tags, str):
            tags = [tag.strip() for tag in tags.split(",") if tag.strip()]
        updated = datetime.date.today().isoformat()
        rel_source = os.path.relpath(source, self.settings.abs_project_path).replace(os.sep, "/")
        meta = {
            "title": title,
            "description": description[:300],
            "tags": list(tags),
            "category": category.get("title", ""),
            "source": rel_source,
            "updated": updated,
        }
        if not first_heading(body):
            body = f"# {title}\n\n{body}".strip()
        try:
            header = yaml.safe_dump(meta, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True).strip()
        except Exception:
            header = (
                f"title: {json.dumps(title)}\n"
                f"description: {json.dumps(description[:300])}\n"
                f"category: {json.dumps(category.get('title', ''))}\n"
                f"source: {json.dumps(rel_source)}\n"
                f"updated: {updated}"
            )
        return f"---\n{header}\n---\n\n{body.strip()}\n"

    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Category / bulk build
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def build_wiki_category(self, path: str) -> None:
        """Build wiki documents for all files in the category at *path*."""
        wiki_settings = self.load_wiki_settings(with_files=True)
        categories = self._get_all_categories(wiki_settings["categories"])
        category = next((c for c in categories if c.get("path") == path), None)

        if not category:
            logger.warning("No category found for path: %s", path)
            return

        files = category.get("files", [])
        if not files:
            logger.info("Category '%s' has no files, skipping.", path)
            return

        logger.info("Building wiki category '%s' (%d files)", path, len(files))
        # Warm the repository scan before the worker threads start so parallel
        # page generation does not repeat it.
        self.site_builder.project_kind()
        self.event_manager.send_event(
            "wiki_category_start", {"path": path, "total": len(files)}
        )

        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=WIKI_BUILD_WORKERS) as executor:
            future_to_file = {
                executor.submit(self.create_wiki_document, f["path"], False): f["path"]
                for f in files
            }
            for future in as_completed(future_to_file):
                file_path = future_to_file[future]
                try:
                    future.result()
                    logger.info("Wiki document built: %s", file_path)
                except Exception as e:
                    logger.exception("Failed to build wiki document for %s: %s", file_path, e)

        self._update_wiki_conf()
        self.event_manager.send_event("wiki_category_done", {"path": path})

    def rebuild_wiki(self) -> None:
        """Rebuild all wiki documents for every category."""
        self.ensure_wiki_structure()
        wiki_settings = self.load_wiki_settings()
        categories = self._get_all_categories(wiki_settings["categories"])
        logger.info("Rebuilding entire wiki (%d categories)", len(categories))

        for category in categories:
            self.build_wiki_category(category["path"])

        # Final home + manifest update after all categories are done.
        self.build_wiki_home(self._read_file(self.wiki_home_path) or "")
        self.build_site()
        logger.info("Wiki rebuild complete.")

    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Home page
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def build_wiki_home(self, markdown_content: str) -> None:
        """

    def compile_wiki(self) -> None:

    def _update_mkdocs(self, site: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> None:
        """
        Keep the MkDocs navigation in sync with the docs-site manifest.

        The old implementation asked the AI to rewrite the nav on every update.
        Navigation is deterministic data, so this is now cheap and correct.
        """
        mkdocs_file_path = Path(self.settings.abs_project_path) / MKDOCS_YAML_FILE_NAME
        site = site or self.site_builder.load() or self.build_site(write=False)
        nav: List[Any] = []
        for section in site.get("navigation", []):
            items = section.get("items", [])
            if not items:
                continue
            entries = []
            for item in items:
                title = item.get("title", "")
                path = item.get("path", "")
                if path:
                    entries.append({title: f"{path}.md"})
            if entries:
                nav.append({section.get("title", "Docs"): entries})

        current: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        if mkdocs_file_path.exists():
            try:
                with open(mkdocs_file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                    loaded = yaml.safe_load(handle)
                if isinstance(loaded, dict):
                    current = loaded
            except Exception as ex:
                logger.warning("Cannot read existing mkdocs.yml: %s", ex)
        current.setdefault("site_name", self.settings.project_name)
        current["nav"] = nav
        try:
            with open(mkdocs_file_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                yaml.dump(current, handle, default_flow_style=False, allow_unicode=True)
            logger.info("mkdocs.yml updated at %s", mkdocs_file_path)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.exception("Error updating mkdocs.yml: %s", e)

    def build_dependency_graph(self) -> DependencyGraph:
        """Build and save the project dependency graph."""
        graph = DependencyGraph(settings=self.settings)
        file_paths = self.loader.list_repository_files()
        ignore_patterns = [self.wiki_path, MKDOCS_YAML_FILE_NAME]
        file_paths = [f for f in file_paths if not any(p in f for p in ignore_patterns)]
        graph.build(file_paths)
        graph.save()
        return graph

    def build_domains(self, graph: DependencyGraph = None) -> List[Dict]:
        """Build domain-based wiki pages."""
        if graph is None:
            graph = DependencyGraph(settings=self.settings)
            if not graph.load():
                graph = self.build_dependency_graph()

        source_map = self.db.get_all_sources()
        wiki_domains = WikiDomains(settings=self.settings, db=self.db, ai=self._get_ai())
        domains = wiki_domains.detect_domains(graph=graph, source_map=source_map)

        domains_dir = os.path.join(self.wiki_path, "domains")
        os.makedirs(domains_dir, exist_ok=True)

        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=WIKI_BUILD_WORKERS) as executor:
            def _build_page(domain: Dict) -> None:
                try:
                    content = wiki_domains.build_domain_page(domain=domain, graph=graph)
                    content = self._ensure_domain_frontmatter(content, domain)
                    page_path = os.path.join(domains_dir, f"{domain['slug']}.md")
                    write_file(page_path, content)
                except Exception as ex:
                    logger.exception("Error building domain page for %s: %s", domain.get("name"), ex)

            futures = [executor.submit(_build_page, d) for d in domains]
            for f in as_completed(futures):
                try:
                    f.result()
                except Exception as ex:
                    logger.exception("build_domains future error: %s", ex)

        wiki_domains.save_domain_map(domains)
        self.build_site()
        return domains

    def build_wiki_index(self, graph: DependencyGraph = None, domains: List[Dict] = None) -> Dict:
        """Build and index wiki content."""
        if graph is None:
            graph = DependencyGraph(settings=self.settings)
            if not graph.load():
                graph = self.build_dependency_graph()
        if domains is None:
            wiki_domains = WikiDomains(settings=self.settings, db=self.db, ai=self._get_ai())
            domains = wiki_domains.load_domain_map()

        wiki_settings = self.load_wiki_settings()
        self.build_site()
        wiki_index = WikiIndex(settings=self.settings, db=self.db)
        index = wiki_index.build(wiki_settings=wiki_settings, domain_map=domains, graph=graph)
        wiki_index.save(index)
        wiki_index.index_to_milvus(index)
        return index

        """Guarantee frontmatter/description on an AI-generated domain page."""
        text = (content or "").strip()

        return f"---\n{yaml.safe_dump(frontmatter, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True).strip()}\n---\n\n{body.strip()}\n"

    def _is_valid_source_path(self, file_path: str) -> bool:
        """
        Validate that the source path is a legitimate file path.
        Reject paths that contain invalid characters or patterns from code/markdown.

        Checks for:
        - Non-string types
        - Markdown/code syntax patterns (```, [, etc.)
        - Invalid filesystem characters (brackets, pipes, etc.)
        - Path traversal attempts
        - Paths that don't end with file extensions

        Args:
            file_path: The path to validate.

        Returns:
            True if the path is valid, False otherwise.
        """
        if not isinstance(file_path, str):
            logger.error("Source path must be a string, got %s", type(file_path))
            return False

        # Check for empty or whitespace-only paths
        if not file_path or not file_path.strip():
            logger.warning("Source path is empty or whitespace-only: %s", file_path)
            return False

        # Check for markdown/code patterns that shouldn't be file paths
        if file_path.startswith("```"):
            logger.warning("Source path looks like code block start: %s", file_path)
            return False

        if file_path.startswith("["):
            logger.warning("Source path looks like markdown link: %s", file_path)
            return False

        # Check for any markdown inline code or other special markup
        if file_path.startswith("`") or file_path.startswith("*"):
            logger.warning("Source path looks like markdown formatting: %s", file_path)
            return False

        # Normalize path to catch various forms
        try:
            normalized = os.path.normpath(file_path)
        except (ValueError, TypeError) as e:
            logger.warning("Failed to normalize path %s: %s", file_path, e)
            return False

        # Check for path traversal attempts
        if ".." in normalized or normalized.startswith(".."):
            logger.warning("Path traversal attempt detected: %s", file_path)
            return False

        # Check for invalid filesystem characters that might slip through
        if INVALID_FILENAME_CHARS.search(file_path):
            logger.warning("Invalid filesystem characters in path: %s", file_path)
            return False

        # Reject paths without extensions (likely malformed)
        # Exception: allow paths that are clearly directories (should have slashes)
        if os.path.sep in file_path or "/" in file_path:
            # It's a path with directories, which is ok
            pass
        elif "." not in os.path.basename(file_path):
            # Single filename without extension - reject it
            logger.warning("Path has no file extension (likely malformed): %s", file_path)
            return False

        return True

    def _is_valid_wiki_file_path(self, file_path: str) -> bool:
        """
        Validate that the wiki file path is safe to write to.
        Check for invalid filename characters and excessive length.

        Args:
            file_path: The wiki file path to validate.

        Returns:
            True if the path is safe to use, False otherwise.
        """
        try:
            # Ensure path is normalized
            normalized = os.path.normpath(file_path)

            # Check each component for invalid characters
            for part in normalized.split(os.sep):
                if not part:
                    # Empty component (e.g., from double slashes) - skip
                    continue

                # Check for invalid characters
                if INVALID_FILENAME_CHARS.search(part):
                    logger.warning("Invalid characters in wiki file path component '%s'", part)
                    return False

                # Check for excessive length
                if len(part) > MAX_FILENAME_LENGTH:
                    logger.warning(
                        "Wiki file path component too long: '%s' (%d chars, max %d)",
                        part,
                        len(part),
                        MAX_FILENAME_LENGTH
                    )
                    return False

            return True
        except Exception as e:
            logger.exception("Error validating wiki file path %s: %s", file_path, e)
            return False

    def _find_category_for_file(
        self, file_path: str, all_categories: List[Dict[str, Any]]
    ) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Find the category that contains the given file."""
        file_path = file_path.replace(self.settings.abs_project_path, '')
        for category in all_categories:
            for f in category.get("files", []):
                if f.get("path", "") == file_path:
                    return category
        return None

    def _assign_category_to_file(
        self, source: str, wiki_settings: Dict[str, Any]
    ) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Assign a file to a category, using AI if necessary."""
        all_categories = self._get_all_categories(wiki_settings["categories"])
        category = self._find_category_for_file(file_path=source, all_categories=all_categories)
        user_language = wiki_settings.get("language", "English")
        user_instructions = wiki_settings.get("prompt", "")

        if not category:
            if not all_categories:
                logger.warning("No categories defined in wiki_settings, cannot assign file: %s", source)
                return None

            categories_and_keywords = [
                {"path": c["path"], "title": c["title"], "keywords": c["keywords"]}
                for c in all_categories
            ]

            summary_prompt = f"""
            <document>
            {self._read_file(source)}
            </document>
            <categories>
            {json.dumps(categories_and_keywords, indent=2)}
            </categories>
            <user_instructions>
            {user_instructions}
            </user_instructions>
            <user_language>
            {user_language}
            </user_language>

            Analyze this document and match the best category from the list of categories for this document.
            Only categories from the list are valid responses.
            Return a JSON dictionary with a single field "path" containing the chosen category path.
            Generated content must be in user_language: {user_language}
            """
            try:
                messages = self._ai_chat(prompt=summary_prompt, clean=False)
                metadata = next(extract_json_blocks(messages[-1].content))
                wiki_path = metadata["path"]
                category = next(
                    (c for c in all_categories if c["path"] == wiki_path), None
                )
                if category is None:
                    logger.warning("AI returned unknown category path '%s' for %s", wiki_path, source)
                    # Fall back to first category
                    category = all_categories[0]
            except Exception as ex:
                logger.exception("Error assigning category to %s: %s", source, ex)
                category = all_categories[0] if all_categories else None

            if category is not None:
                # Register file in category and persist
                if "files" not in category:
                    category["files"] = []
                rel_source = source.replace(self.settings.abs_project_path, '')
                if not any(f.get("path") == rel_source for f in category["files"]):
                    category["files"].append({
                        "path": rel_source,
                        "name": humanize(os.path.basename(rel_source)),
                    })
                    self.save_wiki_settings(wiki_settings)

        return category

    def _determine_wiki_file_path(self, category: Dict[str, Any], source: str) -> str:
        """
        Determine the wiki file path for a source file.

        Args:
            category: The category containing the file.
            source: The source file path.

        Returns:
            The full wiki file path.
        """
        if category.get("single_file", False):
            return path_join(self.wiki_path, f"{category['path']}.md")
        rel_source = os.path.relpath(source, self.settings.abs_project_path).replace(os.sep, "/")
        self._assign_category_file_slugs(category)
        entry = next(
            (file for file in category.get("files", [])
             if str(file.get("path", "")).lstrip("/") == rel_source),
            None,
        )
        filename = entry.get("slug") if entry else self._get_file_wiki_name(source)
        return path_join(self.wiki_path, category["path"], filename)

        Basenames are used when unique. When two files in the same category
        share a basename (``src/api/index.ts`` and ``src/web/index.ts``), the
        project-relative path is slugified instead, and a numeric suffix is
        appended as a last resort. This prevents one page silently overwriting
        another.
        """
        files = [file for file in (category.get("files") or []) if file.get("path")]
        base_counts = Counter(
            slugify(os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(str(file["path"])))[0]) or "document"
            for file in files
        )
        used = set()
        for file in files:
            path = str(file["path"]).replace(os.sep, "/")
            base = slugify(os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(path))[0]) or "document"
            if base_counts[base] > 1:
                base = slugify(os.path.splitext(path)[0]) or base
            candidate = base
            suffix = 2
            while candidate in used:
                candidate = f"{base}-{suffix}"
                suffix += 1
            used.add(candidate)
            file["slug"] = f"{candidate}.md"
            file["wiki_file"] = path_join(
                self.wiki_path, category["path"], file["slug"]

    def _get_file_wiki_name(self, source: str) -> str:
        """Generate a safe wiki filename from a source file path."""
        filename = os.path.basename(source)
        name_without_ext = os.path.splitext(filename)[0]
        safe_slug = slugify(name_without_ext)
        if not safe_slug:
            safe_slug = "document"
        return f"{safe_slug}.md"

        Only new/modified files are indexed (mtime newer than the indexed
        ``last_update``) and files that no longer exist are removed.

        Args:
            root: ``{"source", "path"}`` entry from
                :meth:`ProfileManager.profile_knowledge_roots`.
            profile_name: Profile the folder belongs to.
            force: Reindex every file.

        Returns:
            Number of documents indexed.

        files = self._list_files(folder)
        db = self.get_db(folder)
        indexed_sources = db.get_all_sources() or {}

        documents: List[Document] = []
        for file_path in files:
            entry = indexed_sources.get(file_path)
            if entry and not force:
                last_update = int(entry.metadata.get("last_update") or 0)
                if last_update >= int(os.path.getmtime(file_path)):
                    continue

            text = self._read_text(file_path)
            if not text.strip():
                continue

            relative_file = os.path.relpath(file_path, folder)
            for chunk in self._split_text(text):
                documents.append(Document(
                    page_content=chunk,
                    metadata={
                        "source": file_path,
                        "category": KNOWLEDGE_CATEGORY,
                        "keywords": [profile_name, root.get("source", "")],
                        "profile": profile_name,
                        "knowledge_source": root.get("source", ""),
                        "file": relative_file,

            db.delete_documents(
                sources=sorted({doc.metadata["source"] for doc in documents})

            db.index_documents(documents)

        removed = [source for source in indexed_sources if source not in files]
        if removed:
            db.delete_documents(sources=removed)

            logger.info(

    @staticmethod
    def _list_files(folder: str) -> List[str]:
        """
        List the text files of a knowledge folder.

        Args:
            folder: Absolute folder path.

        Returns:
            Sorted absolute file paths (text extensions only).
        """
        files: List[str] = []
        if not os.path.isdir(folder):
            return files
        for current, _, file_names in os.walk(folder):
            for name in file_names:
                if os.path.splitext(name)[1].lower() not in TEXT_KNOWLEDGE_EXTENSIONS:
                    continue
                files.append(os.path.join(current, name))
        return sorted(files)

    def _read_text(file_path: str) -> str:
        """
        Read a knowledge file as text.

        Delegates to ``ProfileManager`` so the size guard and the error
        handling are shared with the plain (non indexed) knowledge tools.

        Args:
            file_path: Absolute file path.

        Returns:
            File content, empty when it cannot be read.
        """
        return ProfileManager._read_text(file_path, max_size=MAX_KNOWLEDGE_FILE_SIZE)

    @staticmethod
    def _split_text(text: str) -> List[str]:
        """
        Split a document into overlapping chunks.

        Args:
            text: Document content.

        Returns:
            List of non-empty chunks.
        """
        if len(text) <= CHUNK_SIZE:
            return [text]

        chunks: List[str] = []
        step = CHUNK_SIZE - CHUNK_OVERLAP
        for start in range(0, len(text), step):
            chunk = text[start:start + CHUNK_SIZE]
            if chunk.strip():
                chunks.append(chunk)
            if start + CHUNK_SIZE >= len(text):
                break
        return chunks

    # Search
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def search(

        query: str,
        profile_names: Optional[List[str]] = None,
        limit: int = 10
    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Search the knowledge of one or more profiles.

        Every knowledge folder of every requested profile is searched (base +
        every project level), results are merged and sorted by relevance.

        Args:
            query: Natural-language query.
            profile_names: Profiles to search. Defaults to every profile that
                has a knowledge folder.
            limit: Maximum number of results.

        Returns:
            List of result dicts with ``profile``, ``knowledge_source``,
            ``file``, ``source``, ``score`` and ``content``.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the query is empty.
        """
        query = (query or "").strip()
        if not query:
            raise ValueError("query is required")

        names = profile_names or self.profile_names_with_knowledge()
        names = [name for name in names if name][:MAX_SEARCH_PROFILES]
        limit = max(1, min(int(limit or 10), 50))

        if not names:
            return []

        results: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        for profile_name in names:
            for root in self.profile_manager.profile_knowledge_roots(
                profile_name=profile_name
            ):
                try:
                    self.index_folder(root=root, profile_name=profile_name)
                    documents = self.get_db(root["path"]).search(
                        query=query, _limit=limit
                    )
                except Exception as ex:
                    logger.error(
                        "Error searching profile knowledge '%s' (%s): %s",
                        profile_name,
                        root.get("path"),
                        ex,
                    )
                    continue

                for document in documents:
                    metadata = document.metadata or {}
                    results.append({
                        "profile": profile_name,
                        "knowledge_source": metadata.get(
                            "knowledge_source", root.get("source", "")
                        ),
                        "file": metadata.get("file", ""),
                        "source": metadata.get("source", ""),
                        "score": metadata.get("score", 0.0),
                        "content": (document.page_content or "").strip(),
                    })

        results.sort(key=lambda result: result["score"], reverse=True)
        return results[:limit]

    words = re.findall(r"[a-zA-Z0-9_./-]+", (text or "").lower())

    section = str(page.get("section", "")).lower()
    path = str(page.get("path", "")).lower()
    score = 0
    for token in question_tokens:
        if token in title:
            score += 8
        if token in description:
            score += 4
        if token in tags:
            score += 3
        if token in section:
            score += 2
        if token in path:
            score += 2
    if current_page and page.get("path") == current_page:
        score += 5
    if page.get("kind") == "overview":
        score += 2
    return score


def _trim(text: str, limit: int) -> str:
    """Trim a string to a maximum number of characters."""
    if len(text) <= limit:
        return text
    return text[:limit].rstrip() + "\n\n… (truncated)"


class WikiAssistant:
    """Answer questions about one project using its documentation."""

    def __init__(self, settings: Any) -> None:
        self.settings = settings
        self.site_builder = WikiSiteBuilder(settings=settings)
        self._ai = None

    # ── public API ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    async def answer(
        self,
        question: str,
        history: Optional[List[Dict[str, str]]] = None,
        page_path: Optional[str] = None,
        use_knowledge: bool = True,
        include_children: Optional[bool] = None,
        child_depth: Optional[int] = None,
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Answer a documentation question.

        Args:
            question: Natural-language question.
            history: Previous turns as ``[{"role": "user"|"assistant", "content": ...}]``.
            page_path: Wiki page currently open in the UI (used as context hint).
            use_knowledge: Enrich context with knowledge-base search results.

        Returns:
            Dictionary with ``answer``, ``citations``, ``suggestions`` and
            ``pages_used``. Never raises for AI failures: a graceful fallback
            answer is returned instead.
        """
        question = (question or "").strip()
        if not question:
            raise ValueError("A question is required")
        history = [
            {
                "role": message.get("role", "user"),
                "content": str(message.get("content", ""))[:2000],
            }
            for message in (history or [])[-MAX_HISTORY_MESSAGES:]
            if message.get("content")
        ]

        # Always work from a fresh manifest. The scheduler normally rebuilds it,
        # but this makes the assistant see pages written by another process (or
        # a restarted background worker) without waiting for the next batch.
        site = self.site_builder.build_if_stale(write=True)
        pages = list(site.get("pages", {}).values())
        selected = self._select_pages(question, pages, page_path)
        context_pages = self._load_page_context(selected) if selected else []

        if include_children is None:
            include_children = bool(getattr(self.settings, "wiki_search_children", True))
        if child_depth is None:
            try:
                child_depth = int(getattr(self.settings, "wiki_search_depth", 2) or 2)
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                child_depth = 2
        child_depth = max(0, min(10, int(child_depth)))
        # Child pages are limited by wiki_search_children/depth; declared
        # dependency projects are always added on top.
        child_pages = self._child_page_context(question, child_depth, include_children)
        context_pages.extend(child_pages)

        knowledge = []
        if use_knowledge:
            knowledge = await asyncio.to_thread(
                self._search_knowledge, question, include_children, child_depth
            )

        prompt = self._build_prompt(question, history, context_pages, knowledge, site)
        try:
            answer = await self._ask_ai(prompt)
            mode = "ai"
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.exception("Wiki assistant AI call failed: %s", ex)
            answer = self._fallback_answer(question, context_pages, knowledge)
            mode = "fallback"

        citations = self._citations(answer, context_pages, knowledge)
        return {
            "project": {
                "name": self.settings.project_name,
                "codx_path": self.settings.codx_path,
            },
            "question": question,
            "answer": answer,
            "mode": mode,
            "citations": citations,
            "suggestions": self._followups(question, selected, citations),
            "pages_used": [page["path"] for page in context_pages],
            "context": {
                "wiki_pages": len(context_pages),
                "child_pages": len(child_pages),
                "child_projects": include_children,
                "child_depth": child_depth,
                "knowledge_documents": len(knowledge),
                "codebase_search": bool(use_knowledge),
            },
            "generated_at": int(time.time()),
        }

    # ── retrieval ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def _select_pages(
        self,
        question: str,
        pages: List[Dict[str, Any]],
        current_page: Optional[str],
    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        if not pages:
            return []
        tokens = _tokens(question)
        ranked = sorted(
            pages,
            key=lambda page: (
                _score_page(tokens, page, current_page),
                page.get("updated_at", 0),
            ),
            reverse=True,
        )
        selected = [page for page in ranked if _score_page(tokens, page, current_page) > 0]
        if not selected:
            selected = [page for page in ranked if page.get("kind") == "overview"][:2]
        if not selected:
            selected = ranked[:3]
        return selected[:MAX_PAGES]

    def _load_page_context(self, pages: Iterable[Dict[str, Any]]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Attach the markdown body of each selected page."""
        context: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        budget = MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS
        for page in pages:
            loaded = self.site_builder.page(page["path"])
            if not loaded:
                continue
            body = strip_frontmatter(loaded.get("content", ""))
            allowed = max(0, min(len(body), budget))
            context.append({
                **page,
                "content": _trim(body, allowed),
                "headings": loaded.get("headings", []),
            })
            budget -= allowed
            if budget <= 0:
                break
        return context

    def _child_projects(self, depth: int) -> List[Any]:
        """Return descendant projects within *depth* levels."""
        if depth <= 0:
            return []
        try:
            from codx.junior.project.project_discover import (
                find_all_projects,
                is_path_child_of,
            )

            current = os.path.normpath(self.settings.abs_project_path or "")
            if not current:
                return []
            children = []
            for project in find_all_projects().values():
                path = os.path.normpath(project.abs_project_path or "")
                if not path or path == current or not is_path_child_of(path, current):
                    continue
                if len(os.path.relpath(path, current).split(os.sep)) <= depth:
                    children.append(project)
            return sorted(children, key=lambda project: project.abs_project_path or "")[:8]
        except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - discovery is optional
            logger.debug("Cannot resolve child projects for assistant: %s", ex)
            return []

    def _dependency_projects(self) -> List[Any]:
        """Return the declared dependency projects (never the current one)."""
        try:
            return self.settings.get_related_projects(include_children=False)
        except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - discovery is optional
            logger.debug("Cannot resolve dependency projects for assistant: %s", ex)
            return []

    def _related_projects(self, depth: int, include_children: bool = True) -> List[Any]:
        """
        Projects whose wiki pages and knowledge are searched with this one.

        Children are limited to *depth* levels through ``wiki_search_children``
        / ``wiki_search_depth``; declared dependencies are added on top because
        they may live anywhere on disk (``search_related_projects`` gates both).
        A project that is both a child and a dependency is searched only once.
        """
        related: List[Any] = list(self._child_projects(depth)) if include_children else []
        seen = {project.codx_path for project in related}
        seen.add(self.settings.codx_path)
        for project in self._dependency_projects():
            if project.codx_path in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(project.codx_path)
            related.append(project)
        return related

    def _child_page_context(
        self,
        question: str,
        depth: int,
        include_children: bool = True,
    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Select a few wiki pages from related (child/dependency) projects."""
        context: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        budget = MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS // 3
        for child in self._related_projects(depth, include_children):
            if budget <= 0:
                break
            try:
                builder = WikiSiteBuilder(settings=child)
                child_site = builder.build_if_stale(write=False)
                if not child_site:
                    continue
                child_project = child_site.get("project", {})
                pages = list(child_site.get("pages", {}).values())
                selected = self._select_pages(question, pages, None)[:2]
                for page in selected:
                    loaded = builder.page(page["path"])
                    if not loaded:
                        continue
                    body = strip_frontmatter(loaded.get("content", ""))
                    allowed = max(0, min(len(body), budget))
                    context.append({
                        **page,
                        "project": child_project.get("name") or child.project_name,
                        "project_title": child_project.get("title") or child.project_name,
                        "wiki_url": f"?project={child.project_name}&page={page['path']}",
                        "content": _trim(body, allowed),
                        "headings": loaded.get("headings", []),
                    })
                    budget -= allowed
                    if budget <= 0:
                        break
            except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - one child must not break the answer
                logger.debug("Cannot load child wiki pages for %s: %s", child.project_name, ex)
        return context

    def _search_knowledge(
        self,
        question: str,
        include_children: bool = False,
        child_depth: int = 0,
    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Best-effort knowledge search; failures are non-fatal."""
        try:
            from codx.junior.knowledge.knowledge_backend import create_knowledge_db

            documents = create_knowledge_db(settings=self.settings).search(question, _limit=8)
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.debug("Wiki assistant knowledge search unavailable: %s", ex)
            return []
        results: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        for document in documents or []:
            metadata = getattr(document, "metadata", {}) or {}
            content = getattr(document, "page_content", "") or ""
            if not content.strip():
                continue
            source = metadata.get("source") or metadata.get("file") or ""
            results.append({
                "source": source,
                "content": _trim(content, 1800),
                "score": metadata.get("score"),
                "project": self.settings.project_name,
            })
            if len(results) >= 4:
                break
        # A dependency is searched even when the project has no children, so the
        # scope is resolved once through _related_projects.
        related = self._related_projects(child_depth, include_children)
        if related:
            for child in related[:3]:
                try:
                    from codx.junior.knowledge.knowledge_backend import create_knowledge_db

                    documents = create_knowledge_db(settings=child).search(question, _limit=3)
                except Exception as ex:
                    logger.debug("Child knowledge search unavailable for %s: %s", child.project_name, ex)
                    continue
                for document in documents or []:
                    metadata = getattr(document, "metadata", {}) or {}
                    content = getattr(document, "page_content", "") or ""
                    source = metadata.get("source") or metadata.get("file") or ""
                    if not content.strip() or not source:
                        continue
                    results.append({
                        "source": source,
                        "content": _trim(content, 1200),
                        "score": metadata.get("score"),
                        "project": child.project_name,
                    })
                    if len(results) >= 10:
                        return results
        return results

    # ── prompt / AI ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def _build_prompt(
        self,
        question: str,
        history: List[Dict[str, str]],
        pages: List[Dict[str, Any]],
        knowledge: List[Dict[str, Any]],
        site: Dict[str, Any],
    ) -> str:
        project = site.get("project", {})
        page_blocks = []
        for page in pages:
            page_blocks.append(
                f"<doc project=\"{page.get('project', '')}\" path=\"{page['path']}\" "
                f"title=\"{page['title']}\" section=\"{page.get('section', '')}\">\n"
                f"{page.get('content', '')}\n</doc>"
            )
        knowledge_blocks = [
            f"<snippet project=\"{item.get('project', '')}\" source=\"{item['source']}\">\n{item['content']}\n</snippet>"
            for item in knowledge
        ]
        history_text = "\n".join(
            f"{message.get('role', 'user')}: {message.get('content', '')}"
            for message in history
            if message.get("content")
        )
        child_projects = site.get("child_projects", [])
        children_text = "\n".join(
            self._child_project_summary(child) for child in child_projects
        ) or "none"
        return f"""
<project>
  <name>{project.get('title') or project.get('name')}</name>
  <description>{project.get('description', '')}</description>
  <kind>{project.get('kind', 'generic')}</kind>
  <languages>{', '.join(project.get('languages', []))}</languages>

<child_projects>
{children_text}
</child_projects>

<documentation>
{chr(10).join(page_blocks) or '(no wiki pages available)'}
</documentation>

<code_context>
{chr(10).join(knowledge_blocks) or '(no extra code context)'}
</code_context>

<conversation>
{history_text or '(new conversation)'}
</conversation>

<question>

</question>

Answer the question for a developer reading this project's documentation.
Use the documentation as the primary source. Use code context only to add
precision. Cite pages as [Page title](wiki:path). Keep the answer under ~350
words unless a step-by-step example needs more. End with a "Sources" section.
""".strip()

    async def _ask_ai(self, prompt: str) -> str:
        from codx.junior.ai import AI
        from codx.junior.ai.utils import strip_tool_call_markup
        from codx.junior.model.model import CodxUser

        model = self.settings.get_rag_model() or self.settings.get_wiki_model()
        # ``harness=False`` keeps this a plain documentation completion: no
        # agent system prompt and no tool schemas. With the agent harness the
        # model believes it may explore the codebase, emits a tool call the run
        # cannot execute and the answer reaches the user as raw tool-call
        # markup instead of prose.
        self._ai = AI(
            settings=self.settings,
            llm_model=model,
            user=CodxUser(username="wiki-assistant"),
            system=_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
            harness=False,
        )
        messages = await self._ai.a_chat(
            prompt=prompt,
            headers={"tags": "wiki,assistant"},
        )
        content = strip_tool_call_markup(messages[-1].content or "")
        if content.startswith("```") and content.endswith("```"):
            content = "\n".join(content.splitlines()[1:-1])
        if not content.strip():
            # No readable answer (the model only produced a tool call): let
            # ``answer`` fall back to the deterministic page list.
            raise RuntimeError("The model returned no documentation answer")
        return content

    def _fallback_answer(
        self,
        question: str,
        pages: List[Dict[str, Any]],
        knowledge: List[Dict[str, Any]],
    ) -> str:
        """Deterministic answer used when the AI provider is not available."""
        name = self.settings.project_name or "this project"
        lines = [
            f"I could not reach the AI model to answer **{question}** completely.",
            "",
            f"Here are the most relevant places in the {name} documentation:",
            "",
        ]
        for page in pages:
            lines.append(
                f"- [{page['title']}](wiki:{page['path']}) — "
                f"{page.get('description', 'Open this page for details.')}"
            )
        if knowledge:
            lines.extend(["", "Related code context:", ""])
            for item in knowledge[:3]:
                lines.append(f"- `{item.get('source', 'source')}`")
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("Ask again in a moment, or open one of the pages above.")
        return "\n".join(lines)

    def _child_project_summary(self, child: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
        """Describe a child project and its most important wiki pages."""
        lines = [
            f"- {child.get('title')}: {child.get('description', '')} "
            f"(wiki: {child.get('wiki_url', '')}, {child.get('page_count', 0)} pages)"
        ]
        try:
            docs_path = os.path.join(
                child.get("wiki_path") or os.path.join(child.get("codx_path") or "", "wiki"),
                "docs.json",
            )
            if os.path.isfile(docs_path):
                with open(docs_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                    child_site = json.load(handle)
                for page in list(child_site.get("pages", {}).values())[:8]:
                    lines.append(
                        f"    · {page.get('title')}: {page.get('description', '')}"
                    )
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            pass
        return "\n".join(lines)

    # ── citations / follow-ups ──────────────────────────────────────────────

    def _citations(
        self,
        answer: str,
        pages: List[Dict[str, Any]],
        knowledge: List[Dict[str, Any]],
    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        cited_paths = set(re.findall(r"wiki:([^\s)\]>]+)", answer or ""))
        citations: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        seen = set()
        for page in pages:
            path = page["path"]
            project = page.get("project") or self.settings.project_name
            key = f"{project}:{path}"
            if key in seen:
                continue
            if cited_paths and path not in cited_paths:
                # Keep used pages as suggestions even when the model omitted a
                # link; this keeps the UI useful when citations are incomplete.
                pass
            seen.add(key)
            citations.append({
                "type": "wiki",
                "title": page["title"],
                "path": path,
                "project": project,
                "project_title": page.get("project_title", project),
                "wiki_url": page.get("wiki_url", f"?page={path}"),
                "description": page.get("description", ""),
                "icon": page.get("icon", "fa-regular fa-file-lines"),
            })
        for item in knowledge[:3]:
            source = item.get("source", "")
            if source and source not in seen:
                seen.add(source)
                citations.append({
                    "type": "source",
                    "title": source.split("/")[-1] or source,
                    "path": source,
                    "project": item.get("project", self.settings.project_name),
                    "description": "Project source / knowledge snippet",
                    "icon": "fa-solid fa-code",
                })
        return citations

    def _followups(
        self,
        question: str,
        pages: List[Dict[str, Any]],
        citations: List[Dict[str, Any]],
    ) -> List[str]:
        suggestions: List[str] = []
        for page in pages[:2]:
            suggestions.append(f"Show me an example from \"{page['title']}\".")
        suggestions.extend([
            "What are the main modules and how do they connect?",
            "What should I read next?",
            "Where is the entry point of the project?",
        ])
        seen = set()
        result = []
        for suggestion in suggestions:
            if suggestion not in seen and suggestion.lower() != (question or "").lower():
                seen.add(suggestion)
                result.append(suggestion)
        return result[:4]

#!/bin/bash

# Dynamically set CODX_JUNIOR_PATH to the parent directory of the script
export CODX_JUNIOR_PATH="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
echo "CODX_JUNIOR_PATH: $CODX_JUNIOR_PATH"
echo "Installing api. USER: ${USER} ($(id -u):$(id -g)) HOME: ${HOME}"
echo "Fix permissions"
sudo chown -R ${USER} ${HOME}

source ${CODX_JUNIOR_PATH}/set_env.sh

# Install docker
codx docker &

export PYTHONPATH=${CODX_JUNIOR_PATH}/api

cd ${CODX_JUNIOR_PATH}/api

if [ ! -d "$CODX_JUNIOR_API_VENV/bin" ]; then
  echo "Installing codx-junior API for the first time at $CODX_JUNIOR_API_VENV ...will take some time."

  ls -la /home/codx-junior

  echo "Ensure folder exists"
  mkdir -p ${CODX_JUNIOR_API_VENV}

  ls -la /home/codx-junior

  curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
  # Add uv to PATH
  PATH=$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH
  # No hardlinks in docker
  export UV_LINK_MODE=copy
  
  # Create environment using uv with specified Python version
  uv venv --python 3.11 "$CODX_JUNIOR_API_VENV"
  source "${CODX_JUNIOR_API_VENV}/bin/activate"

  # Extras installed by default: local embeddings (torch/sentence-transformers)
  # and the browser client. A slim deployment can opt out with
  # CODX_JUNIOR_API_EXTRAS="" (see codx-junior-installer/demo/Dockerfile).
  API_EXTRAS=${CODX_JUNIOR_API_EXTRAS:-local-models,browser,milvus}

  # Install editable package using uv with the best-match strategy
  if [ -n "$API_EXTRAS" ]; then
    uv pip install -e ".[${API_EXTRAS}]" \
      --extra-index-url https://pytorch.org \
      --index-strategy unsafe-best-match
  else
    uv pip install -e . --index-strategy unsafe-best-match
  fi

else
  echo "!!codx-junior API already installed at ${CODX_JUNIOR_API_VENV}"
fi

class FakeEmbeddings:
    """Deterministic 8d embeddings: hash the words into buckets."""

    model_name = "fake-64d"

    @property
    def embedding_dim(self):
        return 64

    def _vector(self, text):
        import hashlib

        vector = [0.0] * 64
        for word in (text or "").lower().split():
            digest = hashlib.md5(word.encode()).digest()
            vector[digest[0] % 64] += 1.0
        norm = sum(value * value for value in vector) ** 0.5 or 1.0
        return [value / norm for value in vector]
    def embed_query(self, text):
        return self._vector(text)

    def embed_documents(self, texts):
        return [self._vector(text) for text in texts]

"""
LanceDB knowledge database — the built-in (embedded) knowledge backend.

Motivation
----------
The knowledge base no longer needs a service: LanceDB is an *embedded* vector
database (an on-disk Lance dataset, queried in-process), so knowledge/RAG works
out of the box on the single-container demo installation. There is no Milvus
container to start, no gRPC connection to wait for and nothing to configure.

What this module provides
-------------------------
:class:`KnowledgeDBLanceDB` is a drop-in replacement for
:class:`~codx.junior.knowledge.knowledge_db.KnowledgeDB` (the Milvus backend):
same public surface, same ``<codx_path>/db`` layout, same source-map file, so
``Knowledge``, ``ProfileKnowledge``, the wiki index and the API routers do not
know which backend they are talking to. The backend is selected with
``CODX_JUNIOR_KNOWLEDGE_BACKEND`` (see :mod:`knowledge_backend`); ``lancedb`` is
the default, ``milvus`` remains available for existing data / big corpora.

Retrieval
---------
Two legs, exactly like the Milvus implementation:

* **lexical** — full-text search on ``page_content`` (BM25 in Milvus, the
  LanceDB full-text index here),
* **dense** — cosine similarity over the embedding of the document.

``search_hybrid`` fuses both rankings with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) in
Python. LanceDB also offers hybrid search natively, but its rerankers require an
external model download (the ``sentence-transformers`` cross encoder or the
Cohere/OpenAI rerank APIs) — that would put a heavy, network dependent step on
the critical path of a trial installation, so the fusion is done here with 20
lines and no dependency.

Embeddings
----------
The dense leg needs an embeddings provider. Three sources, in this order:

``CODX_JUNIOR_EMBEDDINGS_BACKEND``
    ``auto`` (default)  local if ``sentence-transformers`` is installed,
                        otherwise the configured AI provider.
    ``local``           ``sentence-transformers`` (``all-MiniLM-L6-v2``, 384d).
    ``provider``        the project's configured *embeddings* model through any
                        OpenAI-compatible endpoint (``text-embedding-3-small``,
                        ``text-embedding-004``...). This is what makes knowledge
                        work in the slim image, which does not ship torch.
    ``none``            lexical search only.

When no embeddings are available the adapter degrades to full-text search
instead of raising, so a project is always searchable.

Storage layout
--------------
::

    <codx_path>/db/<index_name>/
        lancedb/                      Lance dataset (embedded, no server)
        index_meta.json               backend + embedding dimension + model
        <index_name>_file.json        source map (shared with the Milvus backend)

``index_meta.json`` records the embedding dimension. Embedding dimensions are
not interchangeable, so when the configured provider changes the dimension the
table is rebuilt (and the source map reset) instead of mixing vectors of
different sizes — the knowledge base is then reindexed on next load.

Diagram:
flowchart TD
    A[KnowledgeDBLanceDB] --> B[lancedb.connect db_path/lancedb]
    A --> C[embeddings provider selection]
    C -- local --> D[sentence-transformers]
    C -- provider --> E[OpenAI-compatible embeddings API]
    C -- none --> F[dense leg disabled]
    A --> G[search_hybrid: FTS + vector, RRF fusion]
    A --> H[source map JSON shared with Milvus]

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
