## 3. What the demo includes — and what it leaves out

The demo is **one container**: FastAPI + the background worker + nginx serving the
built SPA, published on `19981`. There is no Traefik, no LocalAI, no second API
container, no init container, no Node at runtime and nothing is installed when the
container restarts.

| Included | Left out (and how to get it) |
|---|---|
| chat, agent turns, project/file browsing, the web UI | **Traefik / TLS / custom domain** → server tier |
| AI provider + models configured on first start | **LocalAI** → server tier, `--profile local-models` |
| knowledge/RAG **built in** — embedded LanceDB, nothing extra to run (see §4) | **workspaces, browser/computer sessions** → need `/var/run/docker.sock`, commented in `docker-compose.yaml` |
| document editing, git operations | **PDF/DOCX export, OCR** → `.[tex]` / tesseract are not in the slim image |

Full detail, per-component, in [`demo/README.md`](demo/README.md).

## 4. Knowledge / RAG — built in, no extra service

Knowledge is a **built-in** feature, not an optional profile. The vector store is
**LanceDB**, embedded (on-disk, one process) inside the API container: there is no
Milvus to start, no extra container, no `--knowledge` flag and no RAM to reserve.

The backend is chosen with one variable:

| `CODX_JUNIOR_KNOWLEDGE_BACKEND` | What runs | When |
|---|---|---|
| `lancedb` *(default)* | embedded, no service | demo, laptop, single VM |
| `milvus` | your external Milvus (`pip install 'codx-junior[milvus]'`) | existing data, large corpora |
| `none` | nothing | knowledge switched off |

- **Hybrid search is native**: BM25 (full-text) + dense vectors fused with RRF,
  the same shape the Milvus backend returns — the API and the UI do not know which
  backend is in use.
- **RAG also needs an embeddings model.** `deepseek`, `openrouter` and `groq` do not
  provide one; on those presets search runs **lexical only** instead of failing.
  `openai`, `gemini`, `mistral` and `ollama` presets configure one automatically.
- **It degrades, never breaks.** If the embeddings stack cannot load, the dense leg
  is switched off (one warning in the log) and the lexical leg keeps answering.
  Knowledge never prevents the API from booting.

To reuse an existing Milvus instead of the embedded store:

```bash
# .env
CODX_JUNIOR_KNOWLEDGE_BACKEND=milvus
CODX_JUNIOR_MILVUS_URL=http://my-milvus:19530
```

## 5. Development deployment (watch + hot reload)

Use this when you change codx-junior itself, not to show it to users.

There is **no `docker-compose.dev.yaml`**: the source mount and `DEBUG` are hardcoded
in `docker-compose.yaml`, where the api and api-background services run with `DEBUG=1`
and mount `../../.` over the image. That compose file *is* the dev setup.

```bash
cd codx-junior-installer/codx-junior
cp .env.example .env
docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml up -d              # images must exist already
docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml -f docker-compose.build.yaml up -d --build
```

What it gives you: the source tree mounted over the image, `DEBUG=1` on the API,
`uv sync` + the recursive `chown` on every start, and the API watching when
`CODX_JUNIOR_API_RELOAD=1`. Every project folder under
`CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS_PATH` is visible at once.

> The **web client** runs `npm run preview` (a production build in a Node server)
> because its service sets `DEBUG=0`. Set `DEBUG=1` on `codx-junior-client` in
> `docker-compose.yaml` to get the Vite dev server and HMR instead.

That deployment is deliberately generous with resources. To stop paying for the
installs on every restart, and to make the images slimmer, set:

| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `CODX_JUNIOR_SKIP_INSTALL=1` | skip the recursive `chown` + `uv sync` that `scripts/run_api.sh` runs on every start |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_API_EXTRAS` | extras installed by `scripts/install_api.sh` (default `local-models,browser`, empty for a slim install) |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_API_RELOAD=1` | uvicorn `--reload`; off by default because a reload interrupts in-flight agent turns |

If you only need the **full feature set** (local embeddings, Playwright, TeX, OCR)
without editing the source, that is the server tier below.

## 6. Server deployment (TLS, workspaces, local models)

Same compose project as the dev deployment, without the build overlay:

```bash
cd codx-junior-installer/codx-junior
cp .env.example .env          # set CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN and the ACME email
docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml up -d
```

The default `up` still brings the whole 8-service stack (api, api-background, client,
milvus, localai, traefik and two init containers). The profile split — `proxy`,
`local-models`, `dev`, with production as the default — is item 5 of
["still open" in `FAST-DEPLOYMENT.md`](FAST-DEPLOYMENT.md) §7.5. Knowledge is no
longer one of those profiles: it is built into the API (see §4).

`codx-junior-dind/` wraps this stack in docker-in-docker (Sysbox) for the
one-VM-per-customer product and can additionally install Coolify; it is a separate
deliverable and not part of the trial path.

## 7. Publishing the image

`demo/up.sh` is pull-first. Publish once from a machine that has the repo:

```bash
docker build -t codxjunior/codx-junior:demo \
  -f codx-junior-installer/demo/Dockerfile .
docker push codxjunior/codx-junior:demo
```

The build context is the **repository root** (the Dockerfile copies `client/`,
`api/`, `scripts/`), which is why the command is run from the root and why the root
`.dockerignore` matters.

## 8. Operating the demo

```bash
cd codx-junior-installer/demo
./up.sh                       # start (idempotent, re-applies nothing)
./up.sh --build               # build from source instead of pulling
./up.sh --port 8080           # another web port
./up.sh --projects /srv/projects
docker compose logs -f codx-junior
docker compose down           # stop; settings and projects are kept
docker compose down -v        # stop and delete settings + analytics
```

Upgrading: `CODX_JUNIOR_IMAGE=codxjunior/codx-junior:demo` in `.env`, then
`docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`. The two named volumes
(`codx-junior-settings`, `codx-junior-analytics`) survive the upgrade; the projects
folder is a bind mount and is never touched.

## 9. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `ERROR: codx-junior needs an AI provider before it can do anything` | you did not pass `--provider` + `--key` (and `.env` has no values yet) |
| Container is `unhealthy` / the script prints logs and exits | `docker compose logs --tail 100 codx-junior`; the API log is `api.log` in `$CODX_SUPERVISOR_LOG_FOLDER` |
| UI opens, chat says "no model configured" | the bootstrap did not run: `docker exec codx-junior-demo curl -s localhost:19980/api/bootstrap` |
| `401 / invalid api key` in the logs | wrong key, or a `custom` URL without the `/v1` suffix |
| Chat works, knowledge search finds nothing | check the embeddings model for the preset (see §4): `deepseek`, `openrouter` and `groq` have none, so search stays lexical |
| Port 19981 already in use | `./up.sh --port 8080` |
| Projects folder empty / permission denied | `./up.sh --projects /absolute/path`; the container runs as root so it can write to host folders |
| `pull access denied` for `codxjunior/codx-junior:demo` | the tag is not published yet — add `--build` |

## 10. Architecture

```
codx-junior                          the application image
  ├── FastAPI (19980)                api + background worker, supervisord
  ├── nginx (19981)                  serves the built SPA, proxies /api + socket.io
  └── volumes                        settings, analytics

demo/                                tier 1: that image, one container
codx-junior/                         tier 2/3: compose stack (api, client, milvus,
                                     localai, traefik, workspaces)
codx-junior-dind/                    docker-in-docker wrapper (Sysbox) + Coolify
vllm/, litellm/, localai/            optional model-serving sidecars
```

RAG internally is one `KnowledgeDB` interface with two interchangeable backends,
selected by `CODX_JUNIOR_KNOWLEDGE_BACKEND` in
`api/codx/junior/knowledge/knowledge_backend.py`: **LanceDB** (default, embedded,
`knowledge_lancedb.py`) and **Milvus** (`knowledge_milvus.py`, imported lazily so a
LanceDB install never pulls `pymilvus`). The LLM layer has no local model manager: it talks to any
OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`/chat/completions` + `/embeddings`), configured from the
provider presets in `api/codx/junior/bootstrap.py`.

| Setting | Required | Example | Purpose |

You can pass them on the command line (`./up.sh --provider … --key …`), or write
them in `.env` (copy `.env.example`), or export them in your shell.

### Provider presets

`CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER` selects a preset; codx-junior fills in the base URL,
the chat model, the wiki model and the embeddings model for you.

| Provider | Base URL used | Default chat model | Embeddings model | Get a key |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `openai` | `https://api.openai.com/v1` | `gpt-4.1-mini` (`gpt-4.1` for wiki) | `text-embedding-3-small` (1536) | platform.openai.com/api-keys |
| `deepseek` | `https://api.deepseek.com/v1` | `deepseek-chat` | *none* → RAG disabled | platform.deepseek.com/api_keys |
| `gemini` | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai` | `gemini-2.0-flash` | `text-embedding-004` (768) | aistudio.google.com/app/apikey |
| `openrouter` | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | `openai/gpt-4o-mini` | *none* → RAG disabled | openrouter.ai/keys |
| `mistral` | `https://api.mistral.ai/v1` | `mistral-large-latest` | `mistral-embed` (1024) | console.mistral.ai/api-keys |
| `groq` | `https://api.groq.com/openai/v1` | `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` | *none* → RAG disabled | console.groq.com/keys |
| `ollama` | `http://localhost:11434/v1` | `llama3.1` | `nomic-embed-text` (768) | local, no key |

* **Everything goes through the `openai` client.** Any gateway exposing

* Providers without an embeddings endpoint keep **knowledge/RAG search disabled**

## 2. What codx-junior configures by itself

On the first start the API reads the settings above and, **only if no provider
has been configured yet**, it:

1. creates the `AIProvider` (name = the provider you chose) with its base URL
   and key;
2. creates the models `knowledge` (chat/coding/RAG/guardrail) and `embeddings`
   (plus a `wiki` entry when the preset uses a different model for the wiki);
3. points the five global model slots (`llm_model`, `rag_model`, `wiki_model`,
   `guardrail_model`, `embeddings_model`) at them;
4. writes a summary to `$CODX_JUNIOR_CONFIG_FOLDER/bootstrap.json`.

Result: you open the UI, pick a project, and the chat works. No settings page,
no model import, no "no model configured" dead end.

It is **idempotent and non-destructive**: an installation already configured
from the UI is never touched. To re-apply (e.g. after rotating a key):

```bash
docker exec codx-junior curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19980/api/bootstrap/apply
docker exec codx-junior curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:19980/api/bootstrap   # inspect
```

`CODX_JUNIOR_AI_FORCE=1` makes every start re-apply it;
`CODX_JUNIOR_AI_BOOTSTRAP=0` disables it entirely.

The key itself is **not** written to the settings files: the provider stores
`$CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY` and it is expanded from the environment at use time
(`global_settings.get_provider_settings`).

## 3. What this deployment leaves out

| Component of the full stack | Why it is not here | How to get it back |
|---|---|---|
| **client** container (Node + `vite preview`) | the SPA is compiled in a builder stage and served by nginx | never needed |
| **api-background** container | runs as a supervisord program in the same container | never needed |
| **traefik** | same-origin: nginx proxies `/api` to the API | add a proxy in front, or use the server tier |
| **localai** | replaced by "bring your own provider key" | `codx-junior/docker-compose.yaml` |
| **milvus** | not needed: the vector store is embedded LanceDB, running in the API process | never needed (point at your own Milvus only if you have data in it) |
| **analytics-init / codx-junior-init** | their `mkdir`/`chown` work is done by the entrypoint | — |
| torch / sentence-transformers / vLLM / Playwright / TeX / Tesseract / Firefox | runtime deps of optional features; now `pip` extras (`.[local-models,browser]`) | full deployment installs them |

Features **not available** in the demo without extra work: local (offline)
embeddings, document → PDF/DOCX conversion, Tesseract OCR, browser/computer
sessions and workspaces (they need `/var/run/docker.sock`).

### Knowledge / RAG: built in, no vector database to run

Knowledge is a **built-in** feature of this deployment: the vector store is
**LanceDB**, embedded on disk and running in the API process. There is no Milvus
container, no `--knowledge` flag and no extra RAM.

- **One switch**: `CODX_JUNIOR_KNOWLEDGE_BACKEND` — `lancedb` (default,
  embedded), `milvus` (your external server, needs
  `pip install 'codx-junior[milvus]'`) or `none`.
- **Native hybrid search**: BM25 full-text + dense vectors fused with RRF — the
  same result shape as the Milvus backend, so the UI is identical.
- **RAG also needs an embeddings model.** `deepseek`, `openrouter` and `groq` do
  not provide one, so on those keys search stays **lexical** (full-text) instead
  of failing; `openai`, `gemini`, `mistral` and `ollama` configure one
  automatically.
- **It degrades, never breaks.** If the embeddings stack cannot load, the dense
  leg is switched off with a single log warning and the lexical leg keeps
  answering; knowledge never stops the API from booting.

So there is nothing to enable: the chat, the projects, the agent, the file tools
and knowledge search all work with one container.
To enable the docker-dependent features, uncomment the socket mount in
`docker-compose.yaml`. Be aware that it gives the container control of the host
Docker daemon.

---

## 4. Operating it

```bash
./up.sh                      # start (idempotent)
./up.sh --build              # build the image from source instead of pulling
docker compose logs -f codx-junior
docker compose down          # stop (volumes are kept)
docker compose down -v       # stop and delete settings/analytics
```

Ports and volumes:

| | |
|---|---|
| `19981` | Web UI (published) |
| `19980` | API (internal, proxied by nginx) |
| volume `codx-junior-settings` | global settings, per-project `.codx`, presets |
| volume `codx-junior-analytics` | token usage, AI logs, API metrics |
| bind `${CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS_PATH}` | your repositories |

The health check is `GET /api/health`. `docker compose ps` shows `healthy` when
the API answers.

---

## 5. Development deployment (unchanged)

The watch/reload deployment is `codx-junior/docker-compose.yaml` (+ the
`docker-compose.build.yaml` overlay when the images still have to be built). There
is **no `docker-compose.dev.yaml`**: the source mount and `DEBUG=1` are hardcoded in
that compose file, `scripts/run_api.sh` syncs the environment on start, and the web
client only runs the Vite dev server when you switch its service to `DEBUG=1`
(it ships with `DEBUG=0`, i.e. `npm run preview`). Use it when you hack on
codx-junior itself, not to show it to a user.

Two knobs make the source deployment behave like this one:

* `CODX_JUNIOR_SKIP_INSTALL=1` — skip the recursive `chown` and `uv sync` that
  `scripts/run_api.sh` runs on every start.
* `CODX_JUNIOR_API_EXTRAS` — extras installed by `scripts/install_api.sh`
  (default `local-models,browser`, empty for a slim install).

---

## 6. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
|---|---|
| UI loads, chat answers "no model configured" | the bootstrap did not run: check `docker exec codx-junior curl -s localhost:19980/api/bootstrap` and that `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY` is set in `.env`. |
| `401` / `invalid api key` in the logs | wrong key, or `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL` missing `/v1`. |
| Chat works, "knowledge search" finds nothing | check the embeddings model for the preset (see §3): `deepseek`, `openrouter` and `groq` have none, so search stays lexical |
| Container is `unhealthy` | `docker compose logs --tail 100 codx-junior`; the API log is `api.log` inside `$CODX_SUPERVISOR_LOG_FOLDER`. |
| Port 19981 already in use | `./up.sh --port 8080`. |
| Projects folder empty / permission denied | `./up.sh --projects /absolute/path`; the demo container runs as root so it can write to host folders. |

Deeper analysis of the original deployment and the full change list:
[`../FAST-DEPLOYMENT.md`](../FAST-DEPLOYMENT.md).

# codx-junior installer — how to deploy

Three deployments, one command each. Pick the one that matches what you are doing:

| You want to… | Deployment | Where | Containers |
|---|---|---|---|
| **try codx-junior**, show it to somebody, evaluate it | **demo** | [`demo/`](demo/) | **1** |
| hack on codx-junior itself (watch + hot reload) | **dev** | `codx-junior/` + `docker-compose.dev.yaml` | 2 + tools |
| run it for a team (TLS, workspaces, local models) | **server** | `codx-junior/` + profiles | up to 8 |

Start with the demo. It is the only path that needs no domain, no TLS, no vector
database and no build.

- Settings reference for the demo: [`demo/README.md`](demo/README.md)
- Why the deployment looks like this, and what is still open: [`FAST-DEPLOYMENT.md`](FAST-DEPLOYMENT.md)

---

## 1. Requirements

| | |
|---|---|
| Docker | 20.10+ with the `compose` v2 plugin (`docker compose`, not `docker-compose`) |
| RAM | 2 GB free for the demo (the full stack wants ~8 GB) |
| Disk | ~1.5 GB for the demo image |
| AI provider | one API key (OpenAI, DeepSeek, Gemini, OpenRouter, Mistral, Groq or a local Ollama) |

## 2. Quick start — demo deployment

```bash
git clone https://github.com/codx-junior/codx-junior.git
cd codx-junior/codx-junior-installer/demo
```

**Step 1 — choose a provider.** This prints every preset together with the models
codx-junior will configure for it, so you know what you are getting before you pay
for anything:

```bash
./up.sh --list-providers
```

**Step 2 — start it** with that provider and your key:

```bash
./up.sh --provider deepseek --key sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
```

```
Projects folder: /home/you/codx-junior/codx-junior-installer/demo/projects
Pulling the demo image...
Starting codx-junior...
Waiting for the API to become healthy (first start ~30s)...
Configuring the AI provider from the environment...
=============================================================================
 codx-junior is running

   Web UI : http://localhost:19981
   Projects: /home/you/.../demo/projects
   Settings: /home/you/.../demo/.env
=============================================================================
```

**Step 3 — open <http://localhost:19981>**, create or pick a project and chat. The
provider, the models and the five global model slots are already configured, so
there is no settings page to fill in.

### What those two settings are

| Setting | Required | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER` | **yes** — `openai` `deepseek` `gemini` `openrouter` `mistral` `groq` `ollama` `custom` | `deepseek` |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY` | **yes** (not for `ollama`) | `sk-…` |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL` | only for `custom` | `https://gw.acme.com/v1` |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_MODEL` | no — the preset already picks one | `deepseek-chat` |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS_PATH` | no — default `./projects` | `/srv/projects` |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_WEB_PORT` | no — default `19981` | `8080` |

Flags, `.env` and environment variables are equivalent; `up.sh` writes the values
into `demo/.env` (mode 600, git-ignored) so later runs need no flags.

# codx-junior on a cloud VM — unattended install

One script, no questions, no interactive prompt: a fresh VM becomes a running
codx-junior. This is the automated path on top of the
[demo installer](../demo/README.md) — it installs Docker, downloads the
repository, writes the settings and then runs the same `demo/up.sh` a human
would run, so there is only one place that knows how the stack starts.

```bash
sudo ./bootstrap.sh --provider deepseek --key sk-xxxxxxxx
```

```
==> codx-junior unattended install
==>   provider : deepseek
==>   port     : 19981
==>   projects : /opt/codx-junior/projects
==> Downloading the repository (shallow clone of main)
==> Installing codx-junior (this pulls or builds the image: 1-2 min pulled, 5-10 min built)
...
CODX_JUNIOR_READY http://203.0.113.10:19981
```

Exit code `0` means the health check passed **from the host**, on the published
port. Open the URL: the provider and its models are already configured, so the
chat works immediately.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `bootstrap.sh` | the unattended installer (this is the entry point) |
| `codx-junior` | operations CLI, installed at `/usr/local/bin/codx-junior` |
| `cloud-init.yaml` | user-data for any cloud-init provider (Hetzner, DigitalOcean, OpenStack, Scaleway, …) |
| `aws-user-data.sh` | EC2 user-data |
| `gcp-startup-script.sh` | GCE `startup-script` metadata |

## 1. What you need

| | |
|---|---|
| VM | 2 vCPU, **4 GB RAM**, 20 GB disk, x86_64 (Ubuntu 22.04+/Debian 12+, or Amazon Linux 2023) |
| AI key | one key from OpenAI, DeepSeek, Gemini, OpenRouter, Mistral or Groq (or an Ollama endpoint you own) |
| Network | inbound TCP `19981` — from your IP, or 80/443 if you put a TLS proxy in front (see §6) |
| Root | the script needs `sudo` (it installs Docker) |

Nothing else has to be pre-installed: Docker, git and the compose plugin are
handled.

> **ARM (Hetzner CAX, Graviton, Ampere):** works, but the published image is x86
> only today, so the first boot compiles it on the VM (10-20 min on 2 vCPU). Use
> x86 (`cx22`, `cpx11`, `t3.medium`) if you want the fast path.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# codx-junior — UNATTENDED installer for cloud VMs
#
# Takes a fresh Ubuntu/Debian or RHEL-family machine (or a shell with root) to a
# running codx-junior and prints the URL. No questions, no interactive prompt,
# safe to run twice.
#
# It is deliberately thin: it installs Docker, downloads the repository, writes
# the settings and then delegates the start to `demo/up.sh` — the same script a
# human runs — so there is exactly ONE place that knows how the stack starts.
#
#   sudo ./bootstrap.sh --provider deepseek --key sk-xxxxxxxx
#   sudo ./bootstrap.sh --env-file /etc/codx-junior/settings.env
#   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/codx-junior/codx-junior/main/codx-junior-installer/cloud/bootstrap.sh \
#     | sudo bash -s -- --provider openai --key sk-xxxxxxxx
#
# Settings (lowest to highest precedence):
#   default  <  /etc/codx-junior/settings.env  <  environment  <  flags
#
#   --provider NAME      CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER    default: deepseek
#   --key KEY            CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY     required (or --key-file)
#   --key-file PATH      CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY_FILE  read the key from a file
#   --url URL            CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL     only for `custom` providers
#   --model ID           CODX_JUNIOR_AI_MODEL       default: the preset's model
#   --port PORT          CODX_JUNIOR_WEB_PORT       default: 19981
#   --projects PATH      CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS_PATH  default: $HOME/projects
#   --home PATH          CODX_JUNIOR_HOME           default: /opt/codx-junior
#   --repo URL           CODX_JUNIOR_REPO           default: the public repo
#   --ref BRANCH|TAG     CODX_JUNIOR_REF            default: main
#   --branch BRANCH|TAG  alias of --ref
#   --env-file PATH      CODX_JUNIOR_ENV_FILE       default: /etc/codx-junior/settings.env
#   --build              build the image locally instead of pulling it
#   --no-docker-install  fail instead of installing Docker
#   --open-firewall      ufw: allow ssh + the web port (OFF by default)
#   -h, --help
#
# Exit code 0 means the instance answered its health check from the host.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

DEFAULT_HOME="/opt/codx-junior"
DEFAULT_REPO="https://github.com/codx-junior/codx-junior.git"
DEFAULT_REF="main"
DEFAULT_PORT="19981"
DEFAULT_PROVIDER="deepseek"
DEFAULT_ENV_FILE="/etc/codx-junior/settings.env"
CONTAINER="codx-junior-demo"

# --- logging ---------------------------------------------------------------
LOG_FILE="${CODX_JUNIOR_LOG:-/var/log/codx-junior-install.log}"
if ! mkdir -p "$(dirname "${LOG_FILE}")" 2>/dev/null || ! touch "${LOG_FILE}" 2>/dev/null; then
    LOG_FILE="/tmp/codx-junior-install.log"
fi
exec > >(tee -a "${LOG_FILE}") 2>&1

log()  { printf '\033[1;32m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '\033[1;33m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
die()  { printf '\033[1;31mERROR:\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

usage() {
    # The header comment block, not a fixed line range, so the help cannot drift
    # from the options. Works when this script is piped into bash too.
    if [[ -n "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" && -f "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" ]]; then
        awk 'NR == 1 { next } /^#/ { sub(/^# ?/, ""); print; next } { exit }' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
    else
        printf 'codx-junior unattended installer — see install.sh --help for the options\n'
    fi
    exit 0
}

# --- generic helpers -------------------------------------------------------
os_id() {
    local id="unknown"
    if [[ -r /etc/os-release ]]; then
        id="$(. /etc/os-release; printf '%s' "${ID:-unknown}")"
    fi
    printf '%s' "${id}"
}

pkg_install() {
    case "$(os_id)" in
        debian|ubuntu|raspbian|linuxmint)
            apt-get update -qq
            DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -qq "$@" ;;
        amzn|rhel|centos|fedora|rocky|almalinux|ol)
            dnf install -y -q "$@" ;;
        *) die "unsupported distribution '$(os_id)': install git and docker manually" ;;
    esac
}

# --- 1. settings -----------------------------------------------------------
# The settings file is scanned first so that every value below can come from it.
ENV_FILE_SETTING="${CODX_JUNIOR_ENV_FILE:-${DEFAULT_ENV_FILE}}"
CLI_ARGS=("$@")
for ((i = 0; i < ${#CLI_ARGS[@]}; i++)); do
    if [[ "${CLI_ARGS[$i]}" == "--env-file" && $((i + 1)) -lt ${#CLI_ARGS[@]} ]]; then

Start with the demo. It is the only path that needs no domain, no TLS, no vector
database and no build.

- Settings reference for the demo: [`demo/README.md`](demo/README.md)
- Why the deployment looks like this, and what is still open: [`FAST-DEPLOYMENT.md`](FAST-DEPLOYMENT.md)

## 0. One line: install or update

The entry point for a machine you do not control yet — or for updating one you
already run — is `install.sh` in the repository root:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/codx-junior/codx-junior/main/install.sh \
  | sudo bash -s -- --provider deepseek --key sk-xxxxxxxx
```

It resolves the installer of the requested branch, installs Docker when it is
missing, clones or **updates** the repository and ends by verifying the
published port from the host. Exit code `0` means the health check passed.

| Situation | Command |
|---|---|
| first install | `curl … \| sudo bash -s -- --provider deepseek --key sk-…` |
| second run = upgrade | same command again (projects and settings are kept) |
| test a branch or tag | add `--branch my-feature` |
| see before acting | add `--dry-run` |
| no internet on the host | `git clone`, then `./install.sh --provider … --key …` |

Only `--provider` and `--key` are required (`ollama` needs no key). Every other
value has a default; `install.sh --help` is the full reference, and
[`cloud/README.md`](cloud/README.md) covers the unattended cloud-VM path.

## 1. Requirements

| | |
|---|---|
| Docker | 20.10+ with the `compose` v2 plugin (`docker compose`, not `docker-compose`) |
| RAM | 2 GB free for the demo (the full stack wants ~8 GB) |
| Disk | ~1.5 GB for the demo image |
| AI provider | one API key (OpenAI, DeepSeek, Gemini, OpenRouter, Mistral, Groq or a local Ollama) |

## 2. Quick start — demo deployment

```bash
git clone https://github.com/codx-junior/codx-junior.git
cd codx-junior/codx-junior-installer/demo
```

**Step 1 — choose a provider.** This prints every preset together with the models
codx-junior will configure for it, so you know what you are getting before you pay
for anything:

```bash
./up.sh --list-providers
```

**Step 2 — start it** with that provider and your key:

```bash
./up.sh --provider deepseek --key sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
```

```
Projects folder: /home/you/codx-junior/codx-junior-installer/demo/projects
Pulling the demo image...
Starting codx-junior...
Waiting for the API to become healthy (first start ~30s)...
Configuring the AI provider from the environment...
=============================================================================
 codx-junior is running

   Web UI : http://localhost:19981
   Projects: /home/you/.../demo/projects
   Settings: /home/you/.../demo/.env
=============================================================================
```

**Step 3 — open <http://localhost:19981>**, create or pick a project and chat. The
provider, the models and the five global model slots are already configured, so
there is no settings page to fill in.

### What those two settings are

| Setting | Required | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER` | **yes** — `openai` `deepseek` `gemini` `openrouter` `mistral` `groq` `ollama` `custom` | `deepseek` |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY` | **yes** (not for `ollama`) | `sk-…` |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL` | only for `custom` | `https://gw.acme.com/v1` |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_MODEL` | no — the preset already picks one | `deepseek-chat` |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS_PATH` | no — default `./projects` | `/srv/projects` |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_WEB_PORT` | no — default `19981` | `8080` |

Flags, `.env` and environment variables are equivalent; `up.sh` writes the values
into `demo/.env` (mode 600, git-ignored) so later runs need no flags.

### Without a git clone

The image is self-contained, so once `codxjunior/codx-junior:demo` is published:

```bash
docker run -d --name codx-junior -p 19981:19981 \
  -v "$HOME/codx-projects:/home/codx-junior-projects" \
  -v codx-junior-settings:/home/codx-junior/.codx-junior \
  -e CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER=deepseek \
  -e CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY=sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx \
  codxjunior/codx-junior:demo
```

> **Until the image is published** `docker compose pull` fails and `up.sh` falls
> back to a local build (a few minutes). Pass `--build` to make that explicit, and
> see ["publishing the image"](#7-publishing-the-image) below.

### On a cloud VM — one command, fully unattended

On a remote server you do not need to clone anything by hand. This installer
installs Docker, downloads the repository, writes the settings, starts the
container, waits for the health check and prints the URL:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/codx-junior/codx-junior/main/codx-junior-installer/cloud/bootstrap.sh -o /tmp/codx-junior.sh
sudo bash /tmp/codx-junior.sh --provider deepseek --key sk-xxxxxxxx
# -> CODX_JUNIOR_READY http://<server-ip>:19981
```

It is idempotent (re-running upgrades) and it also installs a small operations
CLI: `codx-junior status | logs | restart | upgrade | down`. Hetzner,
DigitalOcean, AWS and GCE examples, the full settings reference, HTTPS with a
domain and the troubleshooting table are in **[cloud/README.md](cloud/README.md)**.

## 3. What the demo includes — and what it leaves out

The demo is **one container**: FastAPI + the background worker + nginx serving the
built SPA, published on `19981`. There is no Traefik, no LocalAI, no second API
container, no init container, no Node at runtime and nothing is installed when the
container restarts.

| Included | Left out (and how to get it) |
|---|---|
| chat, agent turns, project/file browsing, the web UI | **Traefik / TLS / custom domain** → server tier |
| AI provider + models configured on first start | **LocalAI** → server tier, `--profile local-models` |
| knowledge/RAG **built in** — embedded LanceDB, nothing extra to run (see §4) | **workspaces, browser/computer sessions** → need `/var/run/docker.sock`, commented in `docker-compose.yaml` |
| document editing, git operations | **PDF/DOCX export, OCR** → `.[tex]` / tesseract are not in the slim image |

Full detail, per-component, in [`demo/README.md`](demo/README.md).

## 4. Knowledge / RAG — built in, no extra service

Knowledge is a **built-in** feature, not an optional profile. The vector store is
**LanceDB**, embedded (on-disk, one process) inside the API container: there is no
Milvus to start, no extra container, no `--knowledge` flag and no RAM to reserve.

The backend is chosen with one variable:

| `CODX_JUNIOR_KNOWLEDGE_BACKEND` | What runs | When |
|---|---|---|
| `lancedb` *(default)* | embedded, no service | demo, laptop, single VM |
| `milvus` | your external Milvus (`pip install 'codx-junior[milvus]'`) | existing data, large corpora |
| `none` | nothing | knowledge switched off |

- **Hybrid search is native**: BM25 (full-text) + dense vectors fused with RRF,
  the same shape the Milvus backend returns — the API and the UI do not know which
  backend is in use.
- **RAG also needs an embeddings model.** `deepseek`, `openrouter` and `groq` do not
  provide one; on those presets search runs **lexical only** instead of failing.
  `openai`, `gemini`, `mistral` and `ollama` presets configure one automatically.
- **It degrades, never breaks.** If the embeddings stack cannot load, the dense leg
  is switched off (one warning in the log) and the lexical leg keeps answering.
  Knowledge never prevents the API from booting.

To reuse an existing Milvus instead of the embedded store:

```bash
# .env
CODX_JUNIOR_KNOWLEDGE_BACKEND=milvus
CODX_JUNIOR_MILVUS_URL=http://my-milvus:19530
```

## 5. Development deployment (watch + hot reload)

Use this when you change codx-junior itself, not to show it to users.

There is **no `docker-compose.dev.yaml`**: the source mount and `DEBUG` are hardcoded
in `docker-compose.yaml`, where the api and api-background services run with `DEBUG=1`
and mount `../../.` over the image. That compose file *is* the dev setup.

```bash
cd codx-junior-installer/codx-junior
cp .env.example .env
docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml up -d              # images must exist already
docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml -f docker-compose.build.yaml up -d --build
```

What it gives you: the source tree mounted over the image, `DEBUG=1` on the API,
`uv sync` + the recursive `chown` on every start, and the API watching when
`CODX_JUNIOR_API_RELOAD=1`. Every project folder under
`CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS_PATH` is visible at once.

> The **web client** runs `npm run preview` (a production build in a Node server)
> because its service sets `DEBUG=0`. Set `DEBUG=1` on `codx-junior-client` in
> `docker-compose.yaml` to get the Vite dev server and HMR instead.

That deployment is deliberately generous with resources. To stop paying for the
installs on every restart, and to make the images slimmer, set:

| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `CODX_JUNIOR_SKIP_INSTALL=1` | skip the recursive `chown` + `uv sync` that `scripts/run_api.sh` runs on every start |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_API_EXTRAS` | extras installed by `scripts/install_api.sh` (default `local-models,browser`, empty for a slim install) |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_API_RELOAD=1` | uvicorn `--reload`; off by default because a reload interrupts in-flight agent turns |

If you only need the **full feature set** (local embeddings, Playwright, TeX, OCR)
without editing the source, that is the server tier below.

## 6. Server deployment (TLS, workspaces, local models)

Same compose project as the dev deployment, without the build overlay:

```bash
cd codx-junior-installer/codx-junior
cp .env.example .env          # set CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN and the ACME email
docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml up -d
```

The default `up` still brings the whole 8-service stack (api, api-background, client,
milvus, localai, traefik and two init containers). The profile split — `proxy`,
`local-models`, `dev`, with production as the default — is item 5 of
["still open" in `FAST-DEPLOYMENT.md`](FAST-DEPLOYMENT.md) §7.5. Knowledge is no
longer one of those profiles: it is built into the API (see §4).

`codx-junior-dind/` wraps this stack in docker-in-docker (Sysbox) for the
one-VM-per-customer product and can additionally install Coolify; it is a separate
deliverable and not part of the trial path.

## 7. Publishing the image

`demo/up.sh` is pull-first. Publish once from a machine that has the repo:

```bash
docker build -t codxjunior/codx-junior:demo \
  -f codx-junior-installer/demo/Dockerfile .
docker push codxjunior/codx-junior:demo
```

The build context is the **repository root** (the Dockerfile copies `client/`,
`api/`, `scripts/`), which is why the command is run from the root and why the root
`.dockerignore` matters.

## 8. Operating the demo

```bash
cd codx-junior-installer/demo
./up.sh                       # start (idempotent, re-applies nothing)
./up.sh --build               # build from source instead of pulling
./up.sh --port 8080           # another web port
./up.sh --projects /srv/projects
docker compose logs -f codx-junior
docker compose down           # stop; settings and projects are kept
docker compose down -v        # stop and delete settings + analytics
```

Upgrading: `CODX_JUNIOR_IMAGE=codxjunior/codx-junior:demo` in `.env`, then
`docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`. The two named volumes
(`codx-junior-settings`, `codx-junior-analytics`) survive the upgrade; the projects
folder is a bind mount and is never touched.

## 9. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `ERROR: codx-junior needs an AI provider before it can do anything` | you did not pass `--provider` + `--key` (and `.env` has no values yet) |
| Container is `unhealthy` / the script prints logs and exits | `docker compose logs --tail 100 codx-junior`; the API log is `api.log` in `$CODX_SUPERVISOR_LOG_FOLDER` |
| UI opens, chat says "no model configured" | the bootstrap did not run: `docker exec codx-junior-demo curl -s localhost:19980/api/bootstrap` |
| `401 / invalid api key` in the logs | wrong key, or a `custom` URL without the `/v1` suffix |
| Chat works, knowledge search finds nothing | check the embeddings model for the preset (see §4): `deepseek`, `openrouter` and `groq` have none, so search stays lexical |
| Port 19981 already in use | `./up.sh --port 8080` |
| Projects folder empty / permission denied | `./up.sh --projects /absolute/path`; the container runs as root so it can write to host folders |
| `pull access denied` for `codxjunior/codx-junior:demo` | the tag is not published yet — add `--build` |

## 10. Architecture

```
codx-junior                          the application image
  ├── FastAPI (19980)                api + background worker, supervisord
  ├── nginx (19981)                  serves the built SPA, proxies /api + socket.io
  └── volumes                        settings, analytics

demo/                                tier 1: that image, one container
codx-junior/                         tier 2/3: compose stack (api, client, milvus,
                                     localai, traefik, workspaces)
codx-junior-dind/                    docker-in-docker wrapper (Sysbox) + Coolify
vllm/, litellm/, localai/            optional model-serving sidecars
```

RAG internally is one `KnowledgeDB` interface with two interchangeable backends,
selected by `CODX_JUNIOR_KNOWLEDGE_BACKEND` in
`api/codx/junior/knowledge/knowledge_backend.py`: **LanceDB** (default, embedded,
`knowledge_lancedb.py`) and **Milvus** (`knowledge_milvus.py`, imported lazily so a
LanceDB install never pulls `pymilvus`). The LLM layer has no local model manager: it talks to any
OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`/chat/completions` + `/embeddings`), configured from the
provider presets in `api/codx/junior/bootstrap.py`.

## 1. What you need

| | |
|---|---|
| VM | 2 vCPU, **4 GB RAM**, 20 GB disk, x86_64 (Ubuntu 22.04+/Debian 12+, or Amazon Linux 2023) |
| AI key | one key from OpenAI, DeepSeek, Gemini, OpenRouter, Mistral or Groq (or an Ollama endpoint you own) |
| Network | inbound TCP `19981` — from your IP, or 80/443 if you put a TLS proxy in front (see §6) |
| Root | the script needs `sudo` (it installs Docker) |

Nothing else has to be pre-installed: Docker, git and the compose plugin are
handled.

> **ARM (Hetzner CAX, Graviton, Ampere):** works, but the published image is x86
> only today, so the first boot compiles it on the VM (10-20 min on 2 vCPU). Use
> x86 (`cx22`, `cpx11`, `t3.medium`) if you want the fast path.

## 2. Hetzner Cloud

```bash
# settings first: provider + key (+ anything optional)
$EDITOR codx-junior-installer/cloud/cloud-init.yaml   # write_files: section

hcloud server create \
  --name codx-junior \
  --type cx22 \
  --image ubuntu-24.04 \
  --location nbg1 \
  --ssh-key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub \
  --user-data-from-file codx-junior-installer/cloud/cloud-init.yaml

hcloud server ip codx-junior     # -> http://<ip>:19981 in 3-8 minutes
```

Then open port `19981` for your IP (Hetzner Cloud Firewall → add rule
`tcp/19981`, source = your IP), or pass `CODX_JUNIOR_OPEN_FIREWALL=1` in the
settings to let the installer enable `ufw` on the machine itself.

Watch the boot:

```bash
ssh root@<ip> tail -f /var/log/codx-junior-install.log
```

## 3. DigitalOcean

```bash
doctl compute droplet create codx-junior \
  --image ubuntu-24-04-x64 \
  --size s-2vcpu-4gb \
  --region ams3 \
  --ssh-keys "$(doctl compute ssh-key list --format ID --no-header | head -1)" \
  --user-data-file codx-junior-installer/cloud/cloud-init.yaml \
  --wait

DigitalOcean Cloud Firewalls: allow `tcp/19981` (or use `ufw` as above).

## 4. AWS EC2

```bash
# 1. security group: inbound tcp/19981 (and 22) from your IP
# 2. launch with the user-data script (edit its four settings first)
aws ec2 run-instances \
  --image-id ami-0xxxxxxxxxxxxxxx \
  --instance-type t3.medium \
  --key-name mykey \
  --security-group-ids sg-xxxxxxxx \
  --user-data file://codx-junior-installer/cloud/aws-user-data.sh \
  --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=instance,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=codx-junior}]'
```

`aws-user-data.sh` works on Amazon Linux 2023 and on Ubuntu AMIs.

## 5. Google Compute Engine

```bash
gcloud compute instances create codx-junior \
  --machine-type e2-medium \
  --image-family ubuntu-2404-lts-amd64 \
  --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --zone europe-west1-b \
  --tags codx-junior \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=codx-junior-installer/cloud/gcp-startup-script.sh

gcloud compute firewall-rules create codx-junior-web \
  --allow tcp:19981 --target-tags codx-junior
```

The GCE script runs on every boot, which is fine: the installer is idempotent
and only reconciles. It writes `/etc/codx-junior/settings.env` only once, so a
rotated key survives a reboot.

## 6. Anything else (VPS, Proxmox, LXD, bare metal)

Any machine where you have a root shell:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/codx-junior/codx-junior/main/codx-junior-installer/cloud/bootstrap.sh \
  -o /tmp/codx-junior.sh
sudo bash /tmp/codx-junior.sh --provider openai --key sk-xxxxxxxx
```

### HTTPS with a domain

The installer publishes plain HTTP on `19981`. To serve a real domain, put any
reverse proxy in front — Caddy is two lines on the host:

```bash
sudo apt-get install -y caddy
sudo tee /etc/caddy/Caddyfile >/dev/null <<'EOF'
codx.example.com {
    reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:19981
}
EOF
sudo systemctl reload caddy
```

Caddy gets the certificate automatically and passes websockets through. Set
`CODX_JUNIOR_PUBLIC_URL=https://codx.example.com` in the settings so the install
summary prints that address, and close `19981` in the cloud firewall.

## 7. Settings

Everything lives in `/etc/codx-junior/settings.env` — one `KEY=value` per line.
Precedence: **default < settings file < environment < command line flags**.

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER` | `deepseek` | `openai` `deepseek` `gemini` `openrouter` `mistral` `groq` `ollama` `custom` — it also decides the models |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY` | — | **required** (not for a local `ollama`) |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY_FILE` | — | read the key from a file instead (keeps it out of `ps`/argv) |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL` | preset | OpenAI-compatible endpoint; required for `custom` |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_MODEL` | preset | override the chat model |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS_PATH` | `/opt/codx-junior/projects` | where your projects live (bind mount) |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_WEB_PORT` | `19981` | published web port |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_PUBLIC_URL` | auto-detected | address printed at the end of the install |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_HOME` | `/opt/codx-junior` | everything the installer creates lives here |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_REPO` / `CODX_JUNIOR_REF` | GitHub `main` | what to deploy (pin a tag for a fixed version) |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_BUILD` | `0` | `1` = build the image on the VM instead of pulling it |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_INSTALL_DOCKER` | `1` | `0` = fail instead of installing Docker |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_OPEN_FIREWALL` | `0` | `1` = `ufw allow` ssh + the web port |

Flags of the same name exist for everything (`--provider`, `--key`, `--port`,
`--projects`, `--ref`, `--build`, `--open-firewall`, `--env-file`, …); run
`bootstrap.sh --help`.

### Where things end up

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `/opt/codx-junior/src` | git checkout of this repository (upgrade with `codx-junior upgrade`) |
| `/opt/codx-junior/src/codx-junior-installer/demo/.env` | the settings `up.sh` wrote (mode 600 — **it holds the API key**) |
| `/opt/codx-junior/projects` | your projects |
| `/etc/codx-junior/settings.env` | the input settings (mode 600) |
| `/etc/default/codx-junior` | home + port for the `codx-junior` CLI |
| `/var/log/codx-junior-install.log` | full install log |
| docker volumes `codx-junior-settings`, `codx-junior-analytics` | global settings, AI logs, token usage |

The key is stored twice on purpose: `settings.env` is what you edit,
`demo/.env` is what the container reads. Both are `600 root`.

## 8. Verify

```bash
codx-junior status                 # container state, health, URL
curl -fsS http://localhost:19981/  # nginx answers
docker exec codx-junior-demo curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:19980/api/bootstrap
```

The last command prints the provider and the models the installer configured
(`{"status":"ok","bootstrap":{...}}`). If `reason` says the configuration was
incomplete, the key was rejected — check the provider and key, then:

```bash
codx-junior logs --tail 50
```

## 9. Day-2 operations

The installer also puts a small CLI on the machine:

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `codx-junior status` | container state, health and URL |
| `codx-junior url` | the URL this instance answers on |
| `codx-junior logs [-f] [--tail N]` | container logs |
| `codx-junior restart` | restart the container |
| `codx-junior up` | start / recreate (run it after editing `.env`) |
| `codx-junior down` | stop and remove the container (volumes are kept) |
| `codx-junior upgrade` | `git pull` + pull/build the image + recreate |
| `codx-junior env` | show the settings with the API key masked |

**Upgrade:** `codx-junior upgrade`, or re-run `bootstrap.sh` (same effect,
idempotent; projects and settings are untouched).

**Change the provider later:** edit `/etc/codx-junior/settings.env`, then
`codx-junior up` — `up.sh` re-applies the configuration. You can also pick a
different provider in the UI (Settings → AI); the preset models come from the
same catalogue the installer uses.

**Restart on reboot** is handled by Docker (`restart: unless-stopped`).

## 10. Cost

The demo fits comfortably in the smallest x86 instance of every provider
(2 vCPU / 4 GB), roughly **€4-8 / month** on Hetzner, **$12-18 / month** on
DigitalOcean, ~**$30 / month** on `t3.medium` (spot/graviton is cheaper). It
scales down to 2 GB once the image is pulled if you do not build on the VM.

## 11. Uninstall

```bash
codx-junior down
docker volume rm codx-junior-settings codx-junior-analytics
sudo rm -rf /opt/codx-junior /etc/codx-junior /etc/default/codx-junior /usr/local/bin/codx-junior
```

## 12. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
|---|---|
| `permission denied while trying to connect to the Docker daemon` | the script did not finish installing Docker; run `sudo systemctl start docker` and re-run |
| install log stops after "Downloading the repository" | no outbound network / GitHub blocked — set `CODX_JUNIOR_REPO` to your mirror |
| stops at "pull access denied" | `codxjunior/codx-junior:demo` is **not published yet**; the installer falls back to a local build. On a small VM set `CODX_JUNIOR_BUILD=1` so it does not retry the pull, and give it 4 GB RAM |
| killed during the build (`exit 137`) | out of memory while building: use a 4 GB instance, or a machine with swap |
| URL unreachable from your laptop | the port is blocked: cloud firewall (Hetzner/DO/AWS) or `ufw status` on the host |
| page loads but chats fail | the provider key was rejected: `docker exec codx-junior-demo curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:19980/api/bootstrap` and `codx-junior logs` |
| `docker compose` not found | the compose plugin install failed; `bootstrap.sh` retries it — check `/var/log/codx-junior-install.log` |

## 13. What this tier does **not** include

Single container, single user, no TLS of its own:

- no workspaces, browser/computer sessions or the infra panel — those need
  `docker.sock` and are part of the [server deployment](../README.md#6-server-deployment-tls-workspaces-local-models)
- no local models (LocalAI/Ollama are not started; bring your own endpoint via
  `custom`)
- no vector database container — knowledge/RAG runs on embedded LanceDB
- no automatic domain or certificate — the Caddy snippet in §6 is the whole story

"""Secret detection and redaction.

This is the detector that answers the incident that motivated the CISO module:

Two complementary techniques are used, because either one alone has a blind

  Stripe, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Azure, Hugging Face, npm, PyPI, JWT,
  private key blocks, ...) and credential assignments
  (``password = "..."``), which are precise but only cover what is known.
* **Entropy** — long random-looking base64/hex runs, which catch unknown
  formats but need a placeholder filter to stay quiet.

Every finding is redacted before it is returned: findings travel to logs, chat
messages and audit files, so a detector must never re-leak what it detected.

def shannon_entropy(value: str) -> float:
    """Return the Shannon entropy (bits per character) of *value*.

    Args:
        value: Text to measure.

    Returns:
        float: Entropy in bits/char; ``0.0`` for an empty string.

    Example:
        >>> round(shannon_entropy("aaaaaaaa"), 2)
        0.0
        >>> shannon_entropy("aB3$xY9!qW2&zR5%") > 3
        True
    """
    if not value:
        return 0.0
    counts = Counter(value)
    length = len(value)
    return -sum((count / length) * math.log2(count / length) for count in counts.values())

        >>> is_secret_file("config/.env.production")
        True
        >>> is_secret_file("src/app.py")
        False

    return any(pattern.search(normalised) for pattern in _SECRET_FILE_PATTERNS)

    entropy detector: ``codx/junior/security/ciso/gate.py`` or
    ``/home/user/projects/my-api`` are long, low-redundancy and full of
    separators. A credential is not usually shaped like a path, so a candidate
    that is one is rejected.

    Args:
        value: Candidate secret value.

    Returns:
        bool: True when the value looks like a path.
    """
    candidate = (value or "").strip()
    if not candidate:
        return False
    if candidate.startswith(("/", "~/", "./", "../")):
        return True
    if "/" not in candidate and "\\" not in candidate:
        return False
    normalised = candidate.replace("\\", "/")
    last_segment = normalised.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    # ``docs/readme.md`` or ``codx/junior/app.py``: a dotted final segment.
    return "." in last_segment


def is_secret_placeholder(value: str) -> bool:
    """Return True when *value* looks like a placeholder instead of a secret.

    Filters documentation examples, environment variable references and
    identifiers, which are the main source of false positives.

    Paths are also rejected: a long absolute project path
    (``/home/user/projects/my-project-api``) has enough entropy to look like a
    token, and every settings or config file written by the platform contains
    dozens of them.

    Args:
        value: Candidate secret value.

    Returns:
        bool: True when the value must not be reported.
    """
    candidate = (value or "").strip()
    if not candidate:
        return True
    if len(candidate) < 8:
        return True
    if looks_like_path(candidate):
        # Filesystem path, not a credential.
        return True
    return any(pattern.search(candidate) for pattern in _PLACEHOLDER_PATTERNS)

def _redact(value: str) -> str:
    """Render a detected secret in a shape that cannot be reused.

    A short prefix is kept so a human can tell *which* credential leaked in a
    report, while the remainder is unrecoverable.

    Args:
        value: Raw secret.

    Returns:
        str: Redacted representation.
    """
    text = (value or "").strip()
    if not text:
        return REDACTED_MARKER
    if len(text) <= 8:
        return REDACTED_MARKER
    return f"{text[:4]}{REDACTED_MARKER}({len(text)} chars)"


def _line_of(text: str, index: int) -> int:
    """Return the 1-based line number of *index* inside *text*."""
    return text.count("\n", 0, index) + 1


def _excerpt(text: str, start: int, end: int, max_chars: int) -> str:
    """Build a redacted, bounded excerpt around a match."""
    radius = max(20, max_chars // 2)
    left = max(0, start - radius)
    right = min(len(text), end + radius)
    excerpt = text[left:right].replace("\n", " ⏎ ")
    if len(excerpt) > max_chars:
        excerpt = excerpt[:max_chars] + "…"
    return excerpt


def redact_text(text: str, policy: Optional[CisoPolicy] = None) -> Tuple[str, int]:
    """Neutralise every detected secret inside *text*.

    Args:
        text: Payload to sanitise.
        policy: Optional policy (size and excerpt limits).

    Returns:
        tuple: ``(redacted_text, replacements)``. When nothing matched the
        original string is returned unchanged and replacements is ``0``.

    Example:
        >>> redact_text('password = "s3cr3t-value-1234"')[0]
        'password = "s3cr…'
    """
    policy = policy or CisoPolicy()
    result = text or ""
    replacements = 0

    def _replace(match: re.Match) -> str:
        nonlocal replacements
        raw = match.group(0)
        if is_secret_placeholder(raw):
            return raw
        replacements += 1
        return _redact(raw)

    for _, _, _, pattern in _TOKEN_PATTERNS:
        result = pattern.sub(_replace, result)

    def _replace_assignment(match: re.Match) -> str:
        nonlocal replacements
        value = match.group("value")
        if is_secret_placeholder(value):
            return match.group(0)
        replacements += 1
        return match.group(0).replace(value, _redact(value))

    result = _ASSIGNMENT_PATTERN.sub(_replace_assignment, result)

    def _replace_url(match: re.Match) -> str:
        nonlocal replacements
        password = match.group("password")
        if is_secret_placeholder(password):
            return match.group(0)
        replacements += 1
        return match.group(0).replace(f":{password}@", f":{_redact(password)}@", 1)

    result = _URL_CREDENTIALS_PATTERN.sub(_replace_url, result)
    return result, replacements


def scan_text(
    text: str,
    path: Optional[str] = None,
    policy: Optional[CisoPolicy] = None,
) -> Tuple[List[SecurityFinding], str, bool]:
    """Detect secrets in *text*.

    Args:
        text: Payload to scan.
        path: File the payload belongs to (used for reporting and for the
            entropy relaxation inside documentation files).
        policy: Optional policy.

    Returns:
        tuple: ``(findings, redacted_text, truncated)``. The redacted text is
        safe to log and is what callers must store when they only need to keep
        a record of the payload.
    """
    policy = policy or CisoPolicy()
    payload = text or ""
    truncated = False
    if len(payload.encode("utf-8", errors="replace")) > policy.max_scan_bytes:
        payload = payload.encode("utf-8", errors="replace")[: policy.max_scan_bytes].decode(
            "utf-8", errors="replace"
        )
        truncated = True

    findings: List[SecurityFinding] = []

    def _add(
        rule_id: str,
        title: str,
        severity: SecuritySeverity,
        category: SecurityCategory,
        start: int,
        end: int,
        evidence: str,
        remediation: str,
    ) -> None:
        if policy.ignores_rule(rule_id):
            return
        findings.append(SecurityFinding(
            rule_id=rule_id,
            title=title,
            severity=severity,
            category=category,
            reason=f"Detected {title.lower()} in the payload",
            path=path,
            line=_line_of(payload, start),
            # The excerpt is copied into reports, logs and chat messages, so it
            # is redacted with the same rules as the evidence: a finding must
            # never reproduce the credential it reports.
            excerpt=_redact(_excerpt(payload, start, end, policy.max_excerpt_chars)),
            evidence=_redact(evidence),
            remediation=remediation,
            confidence=0.95,
        ))

    for rule_id, title, severity, pattern in _TOKEN_PATTERNS:
        for match in pattern.finditer(payload):
            _add(
                rule_id=rule_id,
                title=title,
                severity=severity,
                category=SecurityCategory.SECRET,
                start=match.start(),
                end=match.end(),
                evidence=match.group(0),
                remediation=(
                    "Remove the credential from the file, rotate it at the provider "
                    "and load it from the environment or the project secret store."
                ),
            )

    for match in _ASSIGNMENT_PATTERN.finditer(payload):
        value = match.group("value")
        if is_secret_placeholder(value):
            continue
        key = match.group("key")
        severity = SecuritySeverity.HIGH
        if (match.group("quote") == '"' or match.group("quote") == "'") and len(value) >= 16:
            severity = SecuritySeverity.CRITICAL
        _add(
            rule_id="secret.hardcoded-credential",
            title=f"Hardcoded credential in '{key}'",
            severity=severity,
            category=SecurityCategory.SECRET,
            start=match.start("value"),
            end=match.end("value"),
            evidence=value,
            remediation=(
                "Read the value from an environment variable or a secret manager "
                "and keep only a placeholder in the source file."
            ),
        )

    for match in _URL_CREDENTIALS_PATTERN.finditer(payload):
        password = match.group("password")
        if is_secret_placeholder(password):
            continue
        _add(
            rule_id="secret.url-embedded-credentials",
            title="Credentials embedded in a URL",
            severity=SecuritySeverity.CRITICAL,
            category=SecurityCategory.SECRET,
            start=match.start("password"),
            end=match.end("password"),
            evidence=password,
            remediation=(
                "Remove the user:password pair from the URL and pass the "
                "credential through a header or a secret reference."
            ),
        )

    if policy.entropy_threshold > 0:
        for match in _ENTROPY_CANDIDATE_PATTERN.finditer(payload):
            token = match.group(0)
            if len(token) < policy.min_secret_length:
                continue
            if is_secret_placeholder(token):
                continue
            # A long run of the same character class is usually an identifier,
            # a hash of a non-secret or an already redacted value.
            if REDACTED_MARKER in token:
                continue
            if shannon_entropy(token) < policy.entropy_threshold:
                continue
            _add(
                rule_id="secret.high-entropy-token",
                title="High entropy string (possible unknown token format)",
                severity=SecuritySeverity.MEDIUM,
                category=SecurityCategory.SECRET,
                start=match.start(),
                end=match.end(),
                evidence=token,
                remediation=(
                    "Confirm what this value is. If it is a credential, rotate it "
                    "and load it from the environment."
                ),
            )

    redacted, _ = redact_text(payload, policy)
    return findings, redacted, truncated

def shannon_entropy(value: str) -> float:
    """Return the Shannon entropy (bits per character) of *value*.

    Args:
        value: Text to measure.

    Returns:
        float: Entropy in bits/char; ``0.0`` for an empty string.

    Example:
        >>> round(shannon_entropy("aaaaaaaa"), 2)
        0.0
        >>> shannon_entropy("aB3$xY9!qW2&zR5%") > 3
        True
    """
    if not value:
        return 0.0
    counts = Counter(value)
    length = len(value)
    return -sum((count / length) * math.log2(count / length) for count in counts.values())

        bool: True for ``.env``, ``*.pem``, ``id_rsa``, ``.npmrc``, ...

    Example:
        >>> is_secret_file("config/.env.production")
        True
        >>> is_secret_file("src/app.py")
        False
    """

        return False
    normalised = path.replace("\\", "/")
    return any(pattern.search(normalised) for pattern in _SECRET_FILE_PATTERNS)

    entropy detector: ``codx/junior/security/ciso/gate.py`` or
    ``/home/user/projects/my-api`` are long, low-redundancy and full of
    separators. A credential is not usually shaped like a path, so a candidate
    that is one is rejected.

    Args:
        value: Candidate secret value.

    Returns:
        bool: True when the value looks like a path.
    """

    if not candidate:
        return False
    if candidate.startswith(("/", "~/", "./", "../")):
        return True
    if "/" not in candidate and "\\" not in candidate:
        return False
    normalised = candidate.replace("\\", "/")
    last_segment = normalised.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]

    return "." in last_segment


def is_secret_placeholder(value: str) -> bool:
    """Return True when *value* looks like a placeholder instead of a secret.

    identifiers, which are the main source of false positives.

    Paths are also rejected: a long absolute project path
    (``/home/user/projects/my-project-api``) has enough entropy to look like a
    token, and every settings or config file written by the platform contains
    dozens of them.

    Args:
        value: Candidate secret value.

    Returns:
        bool: True when the value must not be reported.
    """
    candidate = (value or "").strip()

        return True
    if len(candidate) < 8:

    if not text:
        return REDACTED_MARKER
    if len(text) <= 8:
        return REDACTED_MARKER
    return f"{text[:4]}{REDACTED_MARKER}({len(text)} chars)"


def _line_of(text: str, index: int) -> int:
    """Return the 1-based line number of *index* inside *text*."""
    return text.count("\n", 0, index) + 1


def _excerpt(text: str, start: int, end: int, max_chars: int) -> str:
    """Build a redacted, bounded excerpt around a match."""
    radius = max(20, max_chars // 2)
    left = max(0, start - radius)
    right = min(len(text), end + radius)
    excerpt = text[left:right].replace("\n", " ⏎ ")
    if len(excerpt) > max_chars:
        excerpt = excerpt[:max_chars] + "…"
    return excerpt


def redact_text(text: str, policy: Optional[CisoPolicy] = None) -> Tuple[str, int]:
    """Neutralise every detected secret inside *text*.

    Args:
        text: Payload to sanitise.
        policy: Optional policy (size and excerpt limits).

    Returns:
        tuple: ``(redacted_text, replacements)``. When nothing matched the
        original string is returned unchanged and replacements is ``0``.

    Example:
        >>> redact_text('password = "s3cr3t-value-1234"')[0]
        'password = "s3cr…'
    """
    policy = policy or CisoPolicy()
    result = text or ""
    replacements = 0

    def _replace(match: re.Match) -> str:
        nonlocal replacements
        raw = match.group(0)
        if is_secret_placeholder(raw):
            return raw
        replacements += 1
        return _redact(raw)

    for _, _, _, pattern in _TOKEN_PATTERNS:
        result = pattern.sub(_replace, result)

    def _replace_assignment(match: re.Match) -> str:
        nonlocal replacements
        value = match.group("value")
        if is_secret_placeholder(value):
            return match.group(0)
        replacements += 1
        return match.group(0).replace(value, _redact(value))

    result = _ASSIGNMENT_PATTERN.sub(_replace_assignment, result)

    def _replace_url(match: re.Match) -> str:
        nonlocal replacements
        password = match.group("password")
        if is_secret_placeholder(password):
            return match.group(0)
        replacements += 1
        return match.group(0).replace(f":{password}@", f":{_redact(password)}@", 1)

    result = _URL_CREDENTIALS_PATTERN.sub(_replace_url, result)
    return result, replacements


def scan_text(
    text: str,
    path: Optional[str] = None,
    policy: Optional[CisoPolicy] = None,
) -> Tuple[List[SecurityFinding], str, bool]:
    """Detect secrets in *text*.

    Args:
        text: Payload to scan.
        path: File the payload belongs to (used for reporting and for the
            entropy relaxation inside documentation files).
        policy: Optional policy.

    Returns:
        tuple: ``(findings, redacted_text, truncated)``. The redacted text is
        safe to log and is what callers must store when they only need to keep
        a record of the payload.
    """
    policy = policy or CisoPolicy()
    payload = text or ""
    truncated = False
    if len(payload.encode("utf-8", errors="replace")) > policy.max_scan_bytes:
        payload = payload.encode("utf-8", errors="replace")[: policy.max_scan_bytes].decode(
            "utf-8", errors="replace"
        )
        truncated = True

    findings: List[SecurityFinding] = []

    def _add(
        rule_id: str,
        title: str,
        severity: SecuritySeverity,
        category: SecurityCategory,
        start: int,
        end: int,
        evidence: str,
        remediation: str,
    ) -> None:
        if policy.ignores_rule(rule_id):
            return
        findings.append(SecurityFinding(
            rule_id=rule_id,
            title=title,
            severity=severity,
            category=category,
            reason=f"Detected {title.lower()} in the payload",
            path=path,
            line=_line_of(payload, start),
            # The excerpt is copied into reports, logs and chat messages, so it
            # is redacted with the same rules as the evidence: a finding must
            # never reproduce the credential it reports.
            excerpt=_redact(_excerpt(payload, start, end, policy.max_excerpt_chars)),
            evidence=_redact(evidence),
            remediation=remediation,
            confidence=0.95,
        ))

    for rule_id, title, severity, pattern in _TOKEN_PATTERNS:
        for match in pattern.finditer(payload):
            # Same guard as `redact_text` and the rules below: a value the
            # redactor refuses to touch must not be reported either, otherwise
            # the gate reports a credential it cannot neutralise and the
            # cleanup never converges.
            if is_secret_placeholder(match.group(0)):
                continue
            _add(
                rule_id=rule_id,
                title=title,
                severity=severity,
                category=SecurityCategory.SECRET,
                start=match.start(),
                end=match.end(),
                evidence=match.group(0),
                remediation=(
                    "Remove the credential from the file, rotate it at the provider "
                    "and load it from the environment or the project secret store."
                ),
            )

    for match in _ASSIGNMENT_PATTERN.finditer(payload):
        value = match.group("value")
        if is_secret_placeholder(value):
            continue
        key = match.group("key")
        severity = SecuritySeverity.HIGH
        if (match.group("quote") == '"' or match.group("quote") == "'") and len(value) >= 16:
            severity = SecuritySeverity.CRITICAL
        _add(
            rule_id="secret.hardcoded-credential",
            title=f"Hardcoded credential in '{key}'",
            severity=severity,
            category=SecurityCategory.SECRET,
            start=match.start("value"),
            end=match.end("value"),
            evidence=value,
            remediation=(
                "Read the value from an environment variable or a secret manager "
                "and keep only a placeholder in the source file."
            ),
        )

    for match in _URL_CREDENTIALS_PATTERN.finditer(payload):
        password = match.group("password")
        if is_secret_placeholder(password):
            continue
        _add(
            rule_id="secret.url-embedded-credentials",
            title="Credentials embedded in a URL",
            severity=SecuritySeverity.CRITICAL,
            category=SecurityCategory.SECRET,
            start=match.start("password"),
            end=match.end("password"),
            evidence=password,
            remediation=(
                "Remove the user:password pair from the URL and pass the "
                "credential through a header or a secret reference."
            ),
        )

    if policy.entropy_threshold > 0:
        for match in _ENTROPY_CANDIDATE_PATTERN.finditer(payload):
            token = match.group(0)
            if len(token) < policy.min_secret_length:
                continue
            if is_secret_placeholder(token):
                continue
            # A long run of the same character class is usually an identifier,
            # a hash of a non-secret or an already redacted value.
            if REDACTED_MARKER in token:
                continue
            if shannon_entropy(token) < policy.entropy_threshold:
                continue
            _add(
                rule_id="secret.high-entropy-token",
                title="High entropy string (possible unknown token format)",
                severity=SecuritySeverity.MEDIUM,
                category=SecurityCategory.SECRET,
                start=match.start(),
                end=match.end(),
                evidence=token,
                remediation=(
                    "Confirm what this value is. If it is a credential, rotate it "
                    "and load it from the environment."
                ),
            )

    redacted, _ = redact_text(payload, policy)
    return findings, redacted, truncated

Run it from a git hook::

    PYTHONPATH=<repo>/api python -m codx.junior.security.ciso.precommit

    1   a credential was found: the commit must be stopped,
    3   the scanner could not run (missing dependencies, no git): the hook
        decides whether that is fatal (``CISO_PRECOMMIT_STRICT=1``).

    on a bare ``python3``: a fresh clone, a PR worktree (``api/.venv`` is
    never committed), a container image or CI. Needing the application
    dependency tree (pydantic, fastapi, the LLM clients) would make the gate
    die with an ImportError precisely at commit time, which is how it used to
    break; ``tests/security/ciso_import_check.py`` locks that property in.

    else blocks only when it lands in a file that can execute, because a commit
    stores content and runs nothing. A task card, a wiki page or a vulnerability

    already a blob in the local object database, reachable from any branch and
    from the reflog, and stopping it then costs a history rewrite plus a

import os
import subprocess
import sys
from typing import Any, List, Optional

#: Exit code when the staged changes are clean.
EXIT_OK = 0
#: Exit code when a finding blocks the commit.
EXIT_BLOCKED = 1
#: Exit code when the gate could not run at all.
EXIT_UNAVAILABLE = 3

DIFF_COMMAND = ["git", "diff", "--cached", "--unified=0", "--no-color"]

#: families are downgraded to a report.

)
#: Extensions that hold documentation or configuration data.
PROSE_SUFFIXES = (
    ".md",
    ".markdown",
    ".rst",
    ".txt",
    ".json",
    ".yaml",
    ".yml",
    ".csv",
    ".log",
)


def staged_diff() -> str:
    """Return the staged patch (``git diff --cached``).

    Returns:
        str: Unified diff of the changes the next commit would include.

    Raises:
        OSError: ``git`` is not available.
        subprocess.CalledProcessError: the command failed (not a repository).
    """
    completed = subprocess.run(
        DIFF_COMMAND,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    )
    return completed.stdout or ""


def package_prefix() -> str:
    """Return the repo-relative folder of the CISO package itself.

    Returns:
        str: ``"<path>/"`` (with a trailing slash), or ``""`` when the package
        is not inside the repository being committed.
    """
    here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    try:
        completed = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
        )
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
        return ""
    root = (completed.stdout or "").strip()
    if not root:
        return ""
    relative = os.path.relpath(here, root).replace(os.sep, "/")
    if relative.startswith(".."):
        return ""
    return f"{relative}/"


def excluded_prefixes() -> tuple:
    """Return the repo-relative folders this gate does not scan.

    Two folders must CONTAIN the patterns the detectors look for:

    * the CISO package itself — rule tables and their documentation,
    * ``<api>/tests/security`` — fixtures with fake AWS keys, a reverse shell,
      ``rm -rf /`` and ``ignore previous instructions``.

    Every secret scanner needs such an allowlist: without it the gate blocks
    its own maintenance, and people learn to reach for ``--no-verify``, which
    disables the protection everywhere.

    Returns:
        tuple: Path prefixes (with trailing slash) to skip.
    """
    package = package_prefix()
    if not package:
        return ()
    api_root = package.split("/", 1)[0]
    return (package, f"{api_root}/tests/security/")


def relevant_findings(findings: List) -> List:
    """Drop findings located inside the scanner or its fixtures.

    Args:
        findings: Findings produced by :func:`guard_diff`.

    Returns:
        List: Findings that must still block the commit.
    """
    prefixes = excluded_prefixes()
    if not prefixes:
        return list(findings)
    return [
        finding
        for finding in findings
        if not any(
            (getattr(finding, "path", "") or "").replace(os.sep, "/").startswith(prefix)
            for prefix in prefixes
        )
    ]


def is_prose_path(path: Optional[str]) -> bool:
    """Return True when *path* holds prose or data rather than executable code.

    Args:
        path: Repo-relative path of the finding.

    Returns:
        bool: True for documentation, task cards, wiki pages and config data.
    """
    if not path:
        return False
    normalised = path.replace(os.sep, "/")
    if normalised.startswith(PROSE_PREFIXES):
        return True
    return normalised.lower().endswith(PROSE_SUFFIXES)


def blocking_findings(findings: List, categories: Any) -> List:
    """Return the findings that are allowed to block the commit.

    A credential always blocks: the blob *is* the leak, wherever it lands.
    Everything else blocks only in a file that can execute — injected code in a
    ``.py`` or a ``Makefile`` is the incident this gate exists for, while the
    same string inside a task card is a quotation.

    Args:
        findings: Findings produced by :func:`guard_diff`, already filtered.
        categories: The ``SecurityCategory`` enum of the CISO models.

    Returns:
        List: Findings that decide the verdict.
    """
    return [
        finding
        for finding in findings
        if getattr(finding, "category", None) == categories.SECRET
        or not is_prose_path(getattr(finding, "path", "") or "")
    ]


def main(argv: Optional[list] = None) -> int:
    """Scan the staged changes and decide whether the commit may proceed.

    Args:
        argv: Unused (kept for ``python -m`` compatibility).

    Returns:
        int: One of :data:`EXIT_OK`, :data:`EXIT_BLOCKED`, :data:`EXIT_UNAVAILABLE`.
    """
    try:
        from codx.junior.security.ciso import gate
        from codx.junior.security.ciso import policy as ciso_policy
        from codx.junior.security.ciso.models import SecurityCategory, SecurityDomain
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - depends on the environment
        print(f"CISO: the secret scanner is not importable ({ex})", file=sys.stderr)
        return EXIT_UNAVAILABLE

    try:
        patch = staged_diff()
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as ex:
        print(f"CISO: could not read the staged diff ({ex})", file=sys.stderr)
        return EXIT_UNAVAILABLE

    if not patch.strip():
        return EXIT_OK

    scanned = gate.guard_diff(patch)
    findings = relevant_findings(scanned.findings)
    if not findings:
        return EXIT_OK

    # Re-evaluate the ladder on the findings that survive the filter: keeping
    # the original decision would block on a rule the filter just dropped.
    blocking = blocking_findings(findings, SecurityCategory)
    quoted = len(findings) - len(blocking)
    if not blocking:
        print(
            f"CISO: {len(findings)} finding(s) in the staged diff, all of them "
            "quotations in documentation/data files; a commit executes nothing, "
            "so nothing blocks."
        )
        return EXIT_OK

    policy = ciso_policy.resolve_policy(None)
    verdict = ciso_policy.evaluate(
        blocking,
        domain=SecurityDomain.GIT_COMMIT,
        policy=policy,
        rules_evaluated=scanned.rules_evaluated,
        truncated=scanned.truncated,
    )

    if quoted:
        print(
            f"CISO: {quoted} further finding(s) are quotations in "
            "documentation/data files and are reported, not blocking."
        )
    print(
        ciso_policy.render_report(
            verdict,
            title="CISO pre-commit report",
            min_severity=policy.block_above,
        )
    )
    if verdict.blocked:
        print(
            "\nCISO: commit blocked. Remove the credential, rotate it (assume it "
            "is disclosed) and stage the fix.\n"
            "Inspect the staged changes with: git diff --cached",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return EXIT_BLOCKED
    return EXIT_OK


if __name__ == "__main__":  # pragma: no cover
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
